As regards national threat, the government until now placed very much emphasis on defence, she says. "What you see is that very much attention goes to investments in weapons, in the army. And that there is relatively little attention for people and society. The budget in the Miljoenennota for neighbourhoods and districts is 40 million. That is for 2027. After that it becomes 20 million for the two years after that. And if you then look at the investments in defence, that is not in proportion to each other."

title: British forensic student murders woman in 'Dexter' room
lead: In England, a forensic science student has confessed to murdering a 24-year-old woman, after luring her to a 'murder room' in an Airbnb property. Benjamin Day was obsessed with the television series Dexter, says the British public prosecutor. Last year in December, Day, then 19, called a sex worker with a disposable phone. He had rented a room in Tividale near Birmingham, which he had furnished based on a room from the American series. Dexter is about a forensic expert with the police who is also a serial killer and knows how to erase his traces. Shopping list Day lined the room with plastic wrap and made a "shopping list" that included an apron and cleaning products. He stabbed the woman 78 times and wanted to cut her into pieces, but stopped because he had injured himself. After the murder, the student left the property and called the emergency number to ask for medical help for himself. The police noticed that his story did not add up. Later, the landlord of the Airbnb also called the police, because another tenant had seen blood. After his arrest, Day initially said that he acted in self-defence and had only furnished the room to record a Dexter tribute for TikTok. Later he retracted that and, grinning, confessed guilt, writes the BBC. Day will hear on 4 December what his sentence will be. Earlier 'Dexter' murder It is not the first time that a Briton appears to have been inspired by the series to commit a murder. In 2014, a 17-year-old boy from England was sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of his girlfriend, after he had stabbed her to death and sawed her into pieces in his bedroom.

title: Unrest in Hoogeveen for days, young people arrested again
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> arrested six people in Hoogeveen this evening, including several minors. The centre has been restless for days: yesterday there were also eight arrests due to misconduct, such as throwing fireworks at passers-by. The police are emphatically present in the city centre. Because fireworks bangs were also heard this evening, officers frisked young people on the street, reports RTV <entity id="org:provincie-drenthe">Drenthe</entity> . Minor young people In recent days incidents have regularly taken place in Hoogeveen. These often involve minor young people who, among other things, ride through the centre on fatbikes, intimidate passers-by and set off fireworks and throw them at people. The eight arrestees of yesterday evening were all minors. Furthermore, 32 fines were handed out and two fatbikes were confiscated. Earlier, the municipality tried to get the young people under control through the deployment of extra cameras and a gathering ban. The police will remain present in the centre this evening to prevent further escalation.

title: Christa Pike conscious and responsive after failed execution
lead: The prisoner from the American state of Tennessee who underwent a failed execution last week is conscious and responsive. Her lawyers have made this known. "Against all expectations, Christa Pike is conscious and can talk," the lawyers say in a statement after a visit to the hospital where Pike is staying. "She is still receiving intensive medical care. Despite the serious injuries to her arms, she is still chained to the bed with hand and foot shackles." The lawyers call her unexpected recovery "medically unprecedented". They expect it will take a long time before she is fully recovered. It is still unclear what will happen to her once she is back on her feet. Pricked twice The 50-year-old Pike had been sentenced to death because at age 18 she had tortured and murdered another teenager. Last Wednesday she was to become the first woman in 200 years to be executed in Tennessee, but that did not go according to plan. She received a dose of a substance that should have been deadly twice, but she kept breathing . After more than an hour the execution was halted and she was taken to the hospital. Pike's lawyers say that the executors of the execution had failed to find a vein, something they had warned about in advance. They suspect that the injection was misplaced, causing the deadly fluid not to enter her bloodstream. After the failed execution, Tennessee decided not to carry out any more death sentences for the time being. On Saturday, the highest official of the prison system in the state decided to resign . The investigation into what exactly went wrong is still ongoing.

title: Oscar winner Eva Marie Saint (102) died, known for On the Waterfront
lead: One of the last remaining actresses from the golden age of Hollywood, Eva Marie Saint, has died. The American made a splash in the 50s and 60s with roles in the films On the Waterfront and North by Northwest . She died Tuesday in her home in Los Angeles. Saint was 102 years old. Before she made her debut on the silver screen, Saint began her career in the late 40s on television and radio. Her first film role was immediately a bullseye: in 1954 she was Marlon Brando's co-star in the crime drama On the Waterfront. The newspapers were full of praiseful reviews, both about the film and about the "newcomer". For instance, The New York Times wrote that she was certainly "pretty and blonde", but that she was worth more than just those outward characteristics. "She brings tenderness and sensitivity to a sincere romance, amid a bloodbath." Her debut immediately earned her an Oscar for Best Supporting Actress. Heavily pregnant, she ascended the stage and was handed the golden statuette by Frank Sinatra. Two days later her son Darrell was born. Saint's career could have taken off after that milestone, but remarkably enough she chose to slow down herself. Although the enthusiastic Hollywood producers were lining up for her, she was sparing with her time, because she wanted to be there for her family. In her first decade in the film industry she accepted only seven roles. Another legendary film on which she left her mark was Alfred Hitchcock's thriller North by Northwest (1959). Though that too did not come about by itself; her husband, director Jeffrey Hayden, had to convince her to take that role. "I remember so well that he said: 'I will take care of the children, I want you to really think it over carefully and read the script again'", Saint said in 2014 to Vanity Fair. "He was completely right. That is what husbands are good for." Saint and Hayden were married for 65 years, until he died in 2016. Back to television In the 60s she played in, among others, Exodus , Raintree County and All Fall Down . After that her attention shifted to television. In the 80s her popularity had a revival when she played the mother of Cybill Shepherd in the sitcom Moonlighting . Her second major award followed in 1990. She won an Emmy for the miniseries People Like Us . Saint wanted nothing to do with a quiet retirement. She kept acting until a late age, with roles in, among others, Superman Returns and Winter's Tale . In 2021 she still played the aunt of Marisa Tomei in the radio play The Bus Ride . For her contributions to the film and television industry, Saint received two stars on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

title: American arrested for assistance with shooting at school in Canada
lead: Police in the American state of Washington have arrested a 30-year-old woman in connection with a shooting at a school in Canada in February. An 18-year-old shooter killed her mother and half-brother at home, after which she killed five children and a teacher at her former secondary school in Tumbler Ridge. 25 others were injured. Afterwards she took her own life. Tips via online chat The prosecutor in Seattle says that the 30-year-old James Cody Bryant had contact with the shooter, Jesse Van Rootselaar, for at least six months. According to the prosecutor, Bryant gave Van Rootselaar tips via online chat to commit the murders in such a way that they would have as much impact as possible. "In a corridor people have many ways to escape, by hiding behind a corner for example," Bryant wrote according to the indictment. "An expansive open space means large numbers." Bryant is also said to have sent Van Rootselaar money to buy a lighter, with which she could make an explosive. And she gave advice on how the plan could remain secret, by deleting the online message traffic, the prosecution says. Clicking The two are said to have met each other three years ago via a chat site. The first year there was only sporadic contact because Van Rootselaar is said to have had a forced admission due to psychological problems. In the six months preceding the attack they had daily contact. Both the shooter and the accomplice are a trans woman, but the prosecutors say they have no indications that they sought contact with each other online for that reason. According to the prosecutor, Bryant tried several more times to make Van Rootselaar change her mind. But when Van Rootselaar expressed her concerns that Bryant would "click", Bryant said she would not do that. "I know I could save lives or something, but I don't know," she wrote according to the indictment. In the end she indeed did not go to the police. Van Rootselaar not only had contact with Bryant, but also prepared her act with the help of ChatGPT. The province of British Columbia filed a lawsuit last month against OpenAI, the company behind the AI service. The province argues that the company could have prevented the shooting by alerting the authorities. Need help? Are you thinking about suicide or are you worried about someone? Talking about it helps. That is possible 24/7 free and anonymously via the chat at www.113.nl or by telephone on 113 or 0800-0113.

title: Wake-up service 7/10: Attacks in Israel commemorated • Nobel Prize for Chemistry
lead: Good morning! In Sweden it will be announced who receives the Nobel Prize for Chemistry, and worldwide the attacks in Israel, three years ago, are being commemorated. First the weather: the day begins regionally with fog or mist. After that the sun shines regularly. Later today cloud cover increases and this evening rain follows from the west. It will be 19 to 23 degrees and a moderate southeast wind will blow. Are you going out today? Here you will find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks and here everything about the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? The woman who underwent a failed execution last week in the American state of Tennessee is conscious and responsive. That is what her lawyers say. The 50-year-old Christa Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for a murder she committed when she was eighteen. Pike was to be executed last Wednesday. She was given two lethal injections, but nevertheless kept breathing. The execution was halted and Pike was taken to hospital. According to her lawyer, she is still receiving intensive medical care there and it will take a long time before she is fully recovered. What will happen to Pike after that is still unclear. Other news from the night: And then this too: 1100 bus stops have disappeared in the Netherlands in the past 6 years. Especially in Drenthe and in Groningen many have been abolished. Our reporter Jeroen Gortworst tried to get from the Zeeland village of Brouwershaven to the hospital in Goes. Have a nice day!

title: Polder talks with cabinet, which hopes for ideas for economy and WIA
lead: After months of actions and strikes, employers and employees will again talk with the cabinet today in the Catshuis. Earlier the trade unions walked away, but now that the cuts to the AOW, WIA and WW have been scrapped, they want to talk again. Politics expects quite a lot from the social partners, in other words 'the polder'. Five questions about a possible social agreement. What is now expected of the polder? "Cooperation with the social partners, society and both Chambers is the only way forward", the cabinet writes in the invitation. Ageing, job loss due to artificial intelligence and dropout due to illness are named as major societal challenges. The polder must think along about the sustainability of social security, the cabinet believes. A plan must also come for a stronger economy, in other words about the future of the earning capacity of the Netherlands as described in the Wennink report . It is not a surprising agenda, because the trade unions and employers have already discussed this in recent months, formally and informally, without the cabinet. That economic growth is the best way to safeguard social provisions, the social partners agree. They also agree that something must be done about the disability assessments in the context of the WIA. Will there be no cuts to social security at all anymore? Probably there will be, but at the moment it is not yet possible to say how much. What is clear is that in order to get the trade unions back to the table, the minority cabinet has removed the announced cuts to social security entirely from the budget of the Ministry of Social Affairs. That leaves a gap of 2.4 billion euros in the budget. This makes clear that the problem has not yet been solved. "Bills do not go away by pretending they are not there. There will have to be reforms, one way or another", said <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> last week during the General Financial Considerations. So the cabinet is counting on the talks in the polder ultimately leading to an agreement with savings. Especially with the WIA, the expectation is that this must succeed. And at the same time, it has not yet been said that those talks will already be finished in the spring and whether they will lead to enough savings to close the budget gap. In that case, the coalition will again enter into talks with each other in the spring to solve that and to see whether and where additional cuts are needed. For now, the budget gap is in any case parked for half (1.2 billion) at Education. What does the Netherlands gain from such an agreement? The Netherlands has a long tradition of consultation between employers and employees. The Wassenaar Agreement of 1982 is often mentioned as an important historical outcome of polder consultation. The economy was performing poorly, unemployment was high and the polder ultimately agreed on wage moderation. Another example is the pension agreement of 2019, which made a rigorous change to the pension system possible. The advantage of such agreements is that the signature of employers and employers ensures that the plans hold, even if a cabinet falls. It therefore offers a chance to tackle major societal or economic problems, without trade unions and employers putting new demands on the table again. What do they agree on regarding the WIA? Both employers and employees believe that the assessment system for the disability benefit WIA is too complex. It is not the condition that determines whether you receive a benefit, but the amount of income loss. In calculating that, many mistakes have been made in recent years. And people with a higher income have a greater chance of a benefit. In addition, the waiting list grows due to a shortage of assessing physicians. Furthermore, employers believe that too many Dutch people end up in the WIA. In 2018, the <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity> still granted 41,400 new WIA applications. In 2025, that was 71,300. Trade unions point out that Dutch people have to keep working a little longer and more often drop out towards their pension. Employers would also do too little to prevent dropout and, ultimately, disability. Employers and employees have previously made agreements about healthy working through to retirement and about the continuous retraining of staff to prevent employees from ending up without work. That yields too little result, the trade unions say. They want employers to be obliged to make work of prevention and retraining. In turn, employers are now putting continued payment of wages during illness on the agenda. Following the Wennink report, employers believe that they have to continue paying wages for too long during illness. Sickness absence will therefore be on the agenda, but the social partners differ greatly in insight about reducing absence. When will there be such a social agreement? Today's consultation seems mainly intended to restart the conversation. The cabinet also wants to discuss a timeline for such a social agreement. Last week minister Heinen called the spring an "benchmark", but the trade unions are not in a hurry. There will be no agreement before Christmas, they say. It could be a matter of months, or perhaps two years, they let know. It is also still the question whether it should become one big agreement. It could also be that separate agreements come about, for example about absence, the labor market and economic growth.

title: Hostage Maxim one year after his release from Gaza: 'I will never be the same person again'
lead: "I will never again be the person I was on 6 October, that is impossible", says the 37-year-old Maxim Harkin. "You cannot erase memories and just forget it all. However much I would want to." Harkin belonged to the last group of hostages who were released from Gaza last year, as part of an agreement between Israel and Hamas. The joy in Israel was great. But for the released hostages, the greatest challenge was yet to begin. "On the one hand it was an enormous relief to see my family again and to see that they were doing well", says Harkin. "But it was also immediately clear to me that the real battle had yet to begin. Now we must fight for the mental and physical health of ourselves and of our families." Abducted to Gaza Harkin was with friends at the Nova music festival when Hamas launched the attack on the morning of 7 October 2023. "People screamed, cried and begged for their lives", he says in the living room at his mother's place to the NOS. Thousands of festival-goers fled, including Harkin. After a phone call from a friend, he decided to turn back to help him. His friend was shot dead and he himself was abducted to Gaza. "Along the entire length of the road I saw enormous quantities of bodies everywhere." He speaks in a calm tone, without showing much emotion. "Everything and everyone was covered in blood." The first months Harkin spent above ground in homes, but the largest part of his captivity he stayed in tunnels under the ground. "I spent a year and four months without going up, without seeing the sun, without fresh air." He appeared in two propaganda videos of Hamas. In one of them he can be seen in a tunnel with a bloodied bandage around his head. In the video he says that he was injured in an Israeli bombardment. He also expresses criticism of the attacks of the Israeli army and calls on the population to take action. "It was all staged", Harkin now says. "It was not blood, but tomato sauce that they had smeared on the bandage. I would rather have eaten it." A small smile appears on his face when he talks about it. Trauma continues After 738 days of captivity, Maxim Harkin was released on 13 October 2025. "I have my driver's license back", he jokes. "That means I am relatively healthy, right?" He laughs again. But then says that he is still far from recovered. He weighed about 50 kilos when he came home. He still has little appetite, sleeps poorly and the most everyday things give him flashbacks to his time in captivity. "That can be a certain color, a smell, a sound, really anything." He receives help from the government and also from all kinds of private initiatives, such as 255. That organization guides former hostages and their families and looks at what they need. In this way 255 forms a bridge between the former hostages, their families and the government. According to Elyah Kadish, manager and aid worker at 255, the greatest challenge is the lack of specific knowledge and expertise. "All kinds of insights exist when it comes to hostages, but we have never been confronted with an event on this scale, in which such a large number of civilians were exposed to the kind of violence that took place on 7 October." According to Kadish, it therefore remains to be seen how their traumas will develop in the coming years. That forms a challenge for their treatment. Moreover, according to her, it is also important that the families receive sufficient attention. "The former hostages are recognized by the state as victims and receive help, but their families not always." For Maxim Harkin too, the well-being of his family is important. "I think they had it harder than I did. I at least knew that I was still alive, they had no idea. Physically and mentally they have also been completely broken by it." Maxim himself currently finds support mainly in the reactions on the street and social media. "The warm words of people here in Israel, but also in the rest of the world, are very important. That helps me."

title: Man shot at royal palace Sweden
lead: The Swedish police have shot a armed man at the royal palace in Stockholm. Officers were called after reports of an aggressive man. According to the Swedish broadcaster SVT, the man had a knife with him. What he intended is not yet known. About twenty police cars responded to the report. During his arrest, officers opened fire on him. The man was taken to hospital seriously injured, but he is not in life-threatening danger. During the incident, King Carl Gustav or other members of the royal family were not present in the palace. According to the police, there is also no further danger to public order.

title: Grounded tour boat back in the harbour of Breskens
lead: The passenger ship that ran aground yesterday afternoon along the coast near Zeeuws-Vlaanderen has come loose from the sandbank on its own. The high tide around midnight made the water there high enough. Tour boat de Festijn had 75 people on board yesterday, including five crew members. They were evacuated with rescue boats of the Koninklijke Nederlandse Redding Maatschappij (KNRM). Many of the passengers were elderly, which was taken into account during the rescue operation. The KNRM also deployed a helicopter, but it turned out not to be needed. A spokesperson spoke of a "large rescue operation". Seal safaris Three crew members stayed behind on the ship to wait for the next high tide, writes Omroep Zeeland . Now the Festijn is safely back in the harbour of Breskens. How the ship could run aground exactly is not yet clear. It is regularly used for tours with passengers who want to spot seals. The Festijn is about 100 years old. It is not the first time that passengers of the Festijn had to be evacuated. During a seal safari last year, smoke developed in the engine room, after which 63 passengers had to be taken off board .

title: Trump to call Putin about death at plague institute, WHO also wants more information
lead: US President Trump plans to call his Russian counterpart Putin "very soon" about the death at a plague institute in Irkutsk. According to Russian media, the woman died of plague, but the authorities contradict that and speak of "a pneumonia with unknown cause". "A phone call is planned, soon," Trump answered questions from reporters. "We are already discussing it extensively. Tomorrow we can probably say more about it." Trump had already offered Russia support a day earlier, should that be necessary. A Kremlin spokesperson responded that "mutual support is always appreciated", but did not yet say whether the offer will be taken up. Transparency crucial Last Friday, a laboratory employee of the anti-plague institute in Irkutsk, which has been researching the disease for almost 100 years, died. Russian media wrote that the 28-year-old woman had become infected with the plague when a test tube broke. The Russian authorities contradict that and say that the cause of death of the woman has not yet been established. As a precaution, people with whom she had been in contact have been placed in quarantine. No further infections have been reported yet. The World Health Organization WHO has contacted the Russian health services to get more information. The organisation hopes to get more details about the infection and the Russian approach and offered to step in where necessary. According to the WHO, the risk assessment is currently "moderate to small for Irkutsk, small for Russia and particularly small for Europe". WHO chief Tedros emphasises that "timely, complete and transparent information under international agreements is essential to clarify contradictory reports and make an accurate assessment of the health risks". 'No panic, but attention' "Maybe it is nothing, maybe it is bigger than we think, we don't know", US Secretary Rubio of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> responded yesterday. "We are monitoring it closely and I think the whole world is doing that." "There is no reason for panic, but there is for attention", he continued. "If something like that escapes, it can go quickly." He did note that there is currently little travel between Russia and the US. The disease can be treated with antibiotics if it is detected in time. The US embassy in the US says it is closely monitoring the situation, but also warns that it has few options to help Americans in Russia, certainly outside Moscow. The embassy points out that a negative travel advisory still applies to the whole country for general safety reasons.

title: Cabinet wants citizens to have a hybrid heat pump after all
lead: Many people who need a new heating boiler from 2029 onwards will then have to buy a smart hybrid heat pump. The standards are being tightened to such an extent that an ordinary gas-fired central heating boiler no longer meets them. <entity id="person:elanor-boekholt-osullivan">Minister Boekholt-O'Sullivan</entity> of Housing writes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> that the cabinet sees the hybrid heat pump as an intermediate step on the way to natural gas-free heating of all buildings in 2050. That is important to achieve the climate goals. In 2022, the Rutte IV cabinet already wanted to make the hybrid heat pump mandatory from 2026, but that plan was scrapped under the Schoof cabinet. PVV, NSC, VVD and BBB mainly found the costs for households too high. Experiences positive The current minority cabinet is now dusting off the plan again. In the coalition agreement it was agreed that the hybrid heat pump must become "the new standard". Such a device draws its heat from the outside air and the electricity grid, but can also still work together with a gas-fired central heating boiler at cold moments. Hundreds of thousands of households have recently switched to a fully electric heat pump or a hybrid variant. According to the minister, the experiences of many consumers are positive. The purchase is already being encouraged, but more is needed for a real acceleration of the development, according to Boekholt. Smart The new standard will only apply if the central heating boiler is replaced, so as long as the existing boiler functions it can stay. Residents of apartments and monuments also do not have to switch. There it is often not possible to use a heat pump. The cabinet would prefer that people switch to a fully gas-free heat pump, but a smart hybrid variant also meets the requirements. 'Smart' means that the installation can be set so that it mainly uses electricity at moments when the demand for electricity is low, just like the price. That is important to spare the overcrowded power grid. Hybrid heat pump A hybrid heat pump uses much less gas than a traditional central heating boiler: the saving can amount to up to 65 percent. The purchase costs are considerably higher: easily 8000 euros (including installation), compared to 2000 euros for a central heating boiler. There are subsidy schemes to make the purchase more attractive. With that, the costs come to approximately 6000 euros. Due to the lower energy bill, according to Vereniging Eigen Huis you now earn back a hybrid heat pump in about ten years. The cabinet states that in the coming years too, households with a heat pump will have a lower energy bill. Moreover, the investment leads to a substantial increase in the value of the home, Boekholt writes. The minister realises that 6000 euros is still "terribly much money" for many people. That is why she is announcing it now already, "so that you know that if your boiler needs replacing there is a cost item and that you can take that into account". In the coming period she will further work out how she can ensure that everyone can proceed to purchase. In any case, she wants to offer interest-free loans. Boekholt further emphasises that the hybrid heat pump is "the logical successor to the central heating boiler". "Just as we first got the VR boiler with improved efficiency and then the HR boiler with high efficiency."

title: Australian bishop must go to prison for sexual abuse of Aboriginal men
lead: The former Australian bishop Christopher Saunders must go to prison for sexually abusing two Aboriginal men. The 76-year-old Saunders was given a prison sentence of 6.5 years, but will be eligible for parole in February 2031. Saunders was arrested in 2024. A jury already ruled in August that the former bishop of the Roman Catholic Church was guilty of one rape and twelve cases of assault. He was then acquitted of abuse of a third young man. Now the former bishop heard his sentence. As bishop, Saunders had an important role within the Australian church and was able to do as he pleased for years in the remote Kimberley area. The abuse took place between 2008 and 2019 in his home, motels and a holiday home of the church. Lasting damage Saunders was ordained a priest in 1976 and appointed bishop of Broome in 1996. That diocese covers approximately 770,000 square kilometres, roughly comparable to the area of Turkey. The judge said that Saunders had caused lasting damage to his victims. The archbishop of Perth, Timothy Costelloe, said in a statement that the men who had come forward had shown great courage. "We are sorry that your trust was so directly and profoundly violated by a leader of the church."

title: Millions fraud by CIA employee with invented operations
lead: Gold bars, expensive watches, luxury apartments and private flights. A CIA employee managed to swindle all of it out of the American government with invented missions. David Rush has now confessed to having committed 194 million dollars in fraud. When the 49-year-old Rush was arrested in May , FBI agents found almost 300 gold bars in his house, worth about 40 million dollars. 35 luxury watches and 2 million dollars in cash were also found. Now it appears that the damage to the government is much higher. Rush managed to get the luxury goods from the intelligence service by pretending he needed them for a top-secret operation. For another invented mission he bought luxurious homes in Florida, which he planned to resell for his own gain. In addition, he had himself flown around on private trips at the expense of the taxpayer. That was another cost item of 1.8 million dollars. Leaked Initially Rush insisted that he actually needed all the luxury goods for his work. His lawyer called the reporting "sensationalist" and pointed out that Rush had, for example, neatly stored the gold bars in a safe. "Mr Rush has never said that they were his." Now he decided to cooperate with the prosecutors after all. He faces a sentence of 20 years for fraud. During the trial it also became clear that Rush leaked information about a secret source to a foreign government. Which country that concerns is not clear. He also turned out to have lied about military experience and he wrongly claimed tens of thousands of dollars in compensation from the army. Oversight American media wonder whether the case will have broader consequences for the oversight of the CIA: how is it possible that no one within that organisation questioned the enormous amounts that Rush spent? In a reaction to the case, CIA boss John Ratcliffe did not go into that. "David Rush has disgraced his position and the trust of the public and will be held fully responsible for his actions," he responds in writing. "The CIA will continue to ensure that the persons to whom the secrets of our country are entrusted meet the highest standard."

title: Last active NSC member leaves, does not want to cooperate with Mona Keijzer
lead: Member of the European Parliament Dirk Gotink is resigning his membership of Nieuw Sociaal Contract (NSC). With that, the party founded by Pieter Omtzigt loses its last people's representative. Gotink writes on LinkedIn that he does not want to belong to a party that seeks rapprochement with Mona Keijzer. "The choice for possible cooperation with Project2029 of Mona Keijzer is incomprehensible to me." Keijzer is a guest speaker on Saturday at the general members' meeting of NSC in Breda. She will then discuss the fundamental principles and starting points of the party. Continuing independently <entity id="person:maria-cornelia-gezina-keijzer">Kamerlid Keijzer</entity>, who has sat in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> as a one-person group since her break with BBB, is setting up a new social-conservative movement with the name Project2029. According to Gotink, Keijzer and he are "certainly when it comes to Europe" very differently positioned. He considers "sowing doubt about the importance of the EU" irresponsible and therefore feels compelled to leave. He will continue in the European Parliament as an independent member of the European People's Party (EPP). Wiped out NSC suddenly got twenty seats in 2023, then took part in <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Schoof, but left it. In the elections that followed, the party was wiped out. In January party leader Van Hijum stopped. There is no new leader yet. The board would be working on a restart. It is not said that a cooperation with Project2029 will be considered in that.

title: ABN Amro again slightly less in hands of Dutch State
lead: The Dutch State is further reducing its interest in ABN Amro. At the moment the State still holds 20.7 percent of the bank, but in the coming period this will be further reduced to 10.5 percent. That is announced by NL Financial Investments (<entity id="org:rwt-stichting-administratie-kantoor-financiele-instellingen-nlfi">NLFI</entity>), which manages the government interests in banks and insurers on behalf of <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>. ABN Amro was bought during the credit crisis for 16.8 billion euros. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> wanted to prevent the bank from collapsing with the intervention. In 2015 the State decided to gradually sell the shares in the bank again. Last July it was announced that the share had meanwhile been reduced to 20.7 percent. For years there was fear that the intervention would cost the Netherlands money. But recently the stock market value of ABN Amro has increased considerably, so that much more money is earned from the sale of the shares than was initially thought. There is now even a chance that the State will not lose money on it and will even earn a little. The NLFI sells the shares very gradually. How long it will take before the share has been reduced to 10.5 percent cannot be said. The last sales round of shares lasted about ten months and yielded almost 2.5 billion euros. Ultimately, the intention is that the State's interest in ABN Amro is reduced to 0.

title: Rotterdam opens permanent winter shelter, not only during freezing cold
lead: Rotterdam will offer shelter to homeless and roofless people all winter. The municipality calls it "a big step" in tackling homelessness. Normally the winter shelter is linked to the temperature and only opens at feels-like temperatures below freezing. From 1 November there is a permanent place for 150 people in the Overschie district. The winter shelter will remain open for five months. Social workers and medical help will be present. By letting people stay in one place for a longer time, the municipality hopes to guide them more easily to a follow-up trajectory. At the same location there are also fifty places for labour migrants from the European Union and twenty for people waiting for a home via Centraal Onthaal, the municipal registration point for homeless and roofless people. Evening meal According to the municipality, about two hundred to three hundred people sleep outside in Rotterdam every day. Alderman Astrid Kockelkoren (Homelessness) does not expect that they will all want to use the winter shelter, writes regional broadcaster Rijnmond . When it starts freezing outside, the basic shelter will be expanded. The opening hours of the shelter in Overschie will also be extended. The location was open in earlier winters from 18.00 to 09.00. From next month people can go there from 16.00 to 11.00. That should bring more rest. Homeless people also receive an evening meal and breakfast. The shelter is provided by the Nico Adriaans Stichting (NAS), a care organisation that works for vulnerable Rotterdam residents. Elections In the municipal council elections of last March, the homelessness problem was one of the most important themes in Rotterdam. The plan for the permanent winter shelter was signed by coalition parties Pro, D66, VVD, CDA and Volt. Opposition parties PvdD, CU, SP and Bij1 also signed. It is part of the Stadsakkoord Dakloosheid , which consists of eleven points to reduce the growing number of homeless and roofless people in the city. Permanent shelter Rotterdam is not the first Dutch municipality to offer permanent shelter in winter. In <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> there is also room for homeless and roofless people for five months from 1 November. In <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> homeless and roofless people can go to the winter shelter from 1 December. That is separate from the extra shelter that is realised when the feels-like temperature at night drops below zero.

title: Bats finally gone from Drenthe primary school, demolition can begin
lead: The bats that have been plaguing an old primary school in the Drenthe village of Eext for months are finally gone. The school spent at least 2 tons on attempts to get the animals to leave of their own accord and has now succeeded. The school building of primary school Prins Willem is outdated and must make way for a new building. But because a colony of protected bats lived in the attic, that was not allowed just like that. The demolition and new construction was postponed several times. The animals may not be chased away or fought, they must move of their own accord. The school had already hung bat boxes in the hope that they would go there, but the species that stayed there preferred large spaces - such as the roof of the attic. This spring, that roof was therefore rebuilt for 200,000 euros and placed next to the school. The roof had exactly the same angle of inclination and position relative to the sun as the existing roof. One-way flap But the bats were not tempted and stayed in the old roof. With a view to the upcoming hibernation in which moving is out of the question anyway, the school took action again three weeks ago. One-way flaps were installed on the facade of the old building, a kind of cat flaps through which the bats could get out, but no longer back in. All other openings of the building were sealed by bat experts. Demolition That worked, a spokesperson for the municipality of <entity id="org:gemeente-aa-en-hunze">Aa en Hunze</entity> says to RTV <entity id="org:provincie-drenthe">Drenthe</entity> . "The bats are all out of the school building and they are now in the rebuilt roof. We can start demolishing." The demolition is expected to start this autumn. The start of the new construction is early next year, and if all goes well, students can follow lessons in the new school building from the 2028/2029 school year.

title: Significantly more cancer diagnoses expected, 'but a healthy lifestyle can help'
lead: The number of people who get cancer in the Netherlands will continue to increase over the next twenty years. According to new calculations by the Integraal Kankercentrum Nederland (IKNL), there will be nearly 170,000 new diagnoses per year in 2045. Currently there are about 136,000. The figures are in line with expectations, says Jaike Schilte-Praagman, senior researcher at IKNL. "In the coming twenty years we will have more elderly people in the Netherlands, who also live to an older age on average. Since cancer occurs more often at an older age, that also brings more cancer diagnoses." By 2045, approximately 20 percent of the population will be 70 years or older. But more is at play than just ageing. Some of the cancer diagnoses can be prevented by investing more in prevention, IKNL writes. For example, smoking, alcohol consumption, overweight, insufficient physical activity and exposure to uv radiation increase the risk of various forms of cancer. "That prevention works, we see for example with lung cancer: because men have smoked less, their risk of lung cancer has decreased," says Schilte-Praagman. Skin cancer most common cancer Stomach cancer is the only type of cancer for which the number of diagnoses in both women and men is expected to decrease further. That has been declining for decades, says Praagman, due to a lower intake of salt and smoked food, and the successful treatment of infections with the bacterium Helicobacter pylori , an important cause of stomach cancer. Skin cancer, by contrast, will increase, although more and more people know that they must protect themselves well. That is because the effect of better application of sunscreen only becomes visible in the figures after years. In 2045, skin cancer will be the most common form of cancer, for both men and women, IKNL writes in the report. In men, prostate cancer is still the most common type of cancer, in women that is breast cancer. Tanmaxxing Although changes in lifestyle trends have not been included in the figures, IKNL does point to new worrying developments in its research. "Think of the increasing use of nicotine products among young girls or online challenges in which young people deliberately expose themselves unprotected to the sun for as long as possible." For example tanmaxxing , a social media trend in which people try to get as tanned as possible. According to Schilte-Praagman, about 30 percent of cancer cases are related to risk factors that we can influence, such as lifestyle. "Healthy eating, not smoking, not drinking too much and getting enough exercise help. In addition, it is important to protect your skin against uv radiation. It is not only a task for the individual; we must also ensure together that the living environment is healthy and that people can make healthy choices." Just bad luck That does not alter the fact that people who live healthily can also get cancer. In many cases it is a matter of bad luck and other factors play a role. Schilte-Praagman: "But a healthy lifestyle can certainly contribute to reducing the risk of cancer." Due to ageing and the associated rise in the number of cancer diagnoses, the number of people who die from cancer will also increase. But the risk of dying from cancer has been decreasing for years, a trend that is expected to continue over the next twenty years. "Thirty years ago, about half of cancer patients were still alive five years after diagnosis. That percentage is now 71 percent," concludes Schilte-Paagman. That is due among other things to improvement of treatments, (early) diagnostics and other factors, such as healthier living.

title: Houthis attack airports in Yemen and Saudi Arabia
lead: The Houthis have attacked an airport in Aden, in southern Yemen, with rockets and drones. Nothing is yet known about damage or casualties. A rocket is said to have landed close to the runway, a few minutes before a plane from Cairo was to land there. That plane was diverted to Saudi Arabia just in time. As a precaution, two planes that were on the runway were moved. A rocket is also said to have been fired at Saudi Arabia. It was intercepted and destroyed north of the capital Riyadh. Saudi Arabia supports the Yemeni army in the fight against the Houthis. Yesterday, two airports in Saudi Arabia were also attacked by the Houthis. At least three people were injured. The Houthis have not confirmed that they are behind the attack on the airport in Aden. A military spokesperson does say that the airport of Riyadh was attacked with "multiple drones". Strait Earlier this week, the Yemeni government army began a counteroffensive, in which, according to the Minister of Information, the important strait Bab al-Mandab was recaptured. It was occupied by the Houthis last month. The aim of operation "Dawn of Yemen" is to end the Houthi coup in Yemen and recapture occupied government institutions. The Houthis still control a large part of northern Yemen, including the capital Sanaa. They are supported by Iran. These are verified images of the government army's offensive earlier this week in Yemen at the strait Bab al-Mandab:

title: Interest on student debt rises sharply for large group of former students
lead: For students and 250,000 former students, the interest on student finance and student debt will rise next year. For some of them the interest rises by almost 1 percentage point, from 2.29 percent to 3.28 percent. How much the interest rises depends on whether you are still studying and under which repayment rules you fall. Most current students must repay their debt in 35 years. For them the interest rises much less: from 2.33 percent to 2.70 percent. The largest part of the people who have now graduated fall under the repayment rules of fifteen years. For them a new interest rate is set every five years. Five years ago they still paid 0 percent interest. Now that becomes 3.28 percent. Why does the interest differ? The interest on student loans is based on the interest that the government pays. The fact that the interest percentages differ so much is because they are calculated differently. For the 15-year scheme there is one reference date, while for the 35-year scheme the average interest over a longer period is taken. Earlier this week it was announced that the total student debt has decreased for the first time in a long time . However, the number of graduates with a very high student debt, of above 50,000 euros, has increased considerably. That is partly explained by the loan system, which has since been abolished again. There have long been voices to lower the interest for this group of students, also called the 'unlucky generation'. D66, VVD and CDA also want that: they have agreed in their coalition agreement to set the interest for students at a maximum of 2.5 percent. So far no plans for that have come out. <entity id="org:dienst-uitvoering-onderwijs">DUO</entity>, the organisation that handles student finance, takes someone's income into account when repaying student debts. Whoever earns little, needs to repay less. The debt that remains after a repayment period is ultimately written off.

title: Heavy Russian attack on Ukraine: 20 dead, including 4 children
lead: At least twenty people were killed last night in Russian attacks in various places in Ukraine. At least fourteen people died in an attack on an apartment building in the northern city of Pryloeky, including four children. Fifty people were also injured in the attack, including seven children. Video footage shows how emergency workers are still searching for people under the rubble. Ukrainian president Zelensky speaks of heavy attacks on the country. "One of the most important targets was our energy infrastructure. The Russians wanted to deal a painful blow," he writes. "In total, seventy missiles were launched, many of them ballistic, as well as Shaheds. Unfortunately, only a few of them were shot down. Russian ballistic missiles remain the biggest challenge." Ukraine has carried out counterattacks on four targets, in the regions of Perm, Samara and Astrakhan. Among other things, two oil facilities were hit. The new generation of Russian Shahed drones is even faster and more destructive and puts the balance on the battlefield on edge: The deaths occurred among others in Kyiv, in Pryloeky and in the Poltava region. The nearby regions of Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk were also targets. There is damage to homes and factories, the Ukrainian authorities report. The Ukrainian air force says that Russia last night fired not 70, but 130 drones and 48 cruise missiles and five ballistic missiles. The Russian Ministry of Defense confirms that its armed forces carried out a massive attack on facilities in Kyiv and other regions. According to Russia, targets included the Ukrainian defense company Fire Point, where Ukraine would store its Flamingo cruise missiles and medium- and long-range drones. Ballistic missile Last week, president Zelensky announced that Ukraine had for the first time fired a ballistic missile produced by Fire Point. In an interview with news agency Reuters last week, Zelensky said he expected the company to have an FP-9 missile with a greater range ready by the autumn; according to him, this ballistic missile has a range up to and including Moscow. Ukraine has been struggling for months with a serious shortage of air defense, in particular to shoot down Russian ballistic missiles. That is why Zelensky has repeatedly asked his allies to supply new weapons . That need is growing now that the Russian air attacks are becoming increasingly fierce. The European Commission announced today that Ukraine will receive 1.24 billion euros to purchase drones and anti-drone equipment with it. "Russia is pursuing a deliberate strategy of terror. Europe is taking its responsibility and others must also step up their support," says Commission president Von der Leyen.

title: French police temporarily stop using stun grenades at school pupil protests
lead: The French police will no longer use stun grenades at the school pupil protests in the coming period, says the minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> Nuñez. A stun grenade is used to blind or stun people with a loud bang and flash of light. The decision comes after a 15-year-old boy lost his hand at a demonstration in the city of Lens. The mayor of Wingles, where the boy lives, says that the teenager's left hand has been amputated. He also had a transplant on his right hand and sustained injuries to his face and chest. Since last week, protests have been held throughout France at schools against problems in education. School pupils are demonstrating against, among other things, overdue maintenance of school buildings, classes that are too large, school days that are too long and the teacher shortage in France. Arrested or thrown? What exactly went wrong in Lens is still unclear. The riot police were called in when the demonstration there, according to the French authorities, turned into riots. French media write based on a police source that the riot police threw a stun grenade and that the boy wanted to throw it back. The grenade would then have exploded in his hand. Eyewitnesses say that the stun grenade was thrown and landed directly in the hand of the 15-year-old. So he would not have picked the thing up. An investigation has been launched into the incident. The use of a stun grenade is suspended "until the truth has come to light", Nuñez says to the French branch of RTL . Several incidents It is not the first incident since the start of the protests. So far, 215 school pupils have been injured. For example, another boy last week suffered a double jaw fracture when he was hit in the face by a tear gas grenade. That case is also being investigated. Nuñez previously indicated that eighteen investigations are underway into violent incidents. The minister has called on the police to use proportionate violence. On the petition platform for the French parliament, a petition has been started to ban the use of weapons and grenades at the demonstrations. It has already collected thousands of signatures. Demonstrations announced Today no major protests appear to be planned. Many schools are simply open today. Yesterday, French prime minister Lecornu said that there would be no lessons at schools for three days. At that time it was not clear whether schools would comply with that. According to the Ministry of Education, lessons at 86 percent of secondary schools will simply continue today. At 528 schools, lessons have been partly or completely suspended. However, it seems that the protests will not stop yet. One of the largest trade unions in France, CGT, said that there are plans to continue demonstrating tomorrow. Lecornu will give a speech tonight about the ongoing unrest and demonstrations.

title: Cabinet and social partners had a good first conversation
lead: After months of actions, the cabinet and employers and employees have had a good conversation. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> called it afterwards a first conversation, in which there was also laughter at times. The atmosphere was good, confirmed among others FNV chairman Spekman and VNO-NCW chairman Van Oostrom. The urgency to talk further was felt by everyone. Jetten said that the trade unions have confirmed at the Catshuis that the actions have been suspended for the time being. In a few weeks there will be further talks. 'No austerity task' That must ultimately lead to a social agreement, but it is not that far yet. "The negotiations really still have to start", according to Jetten. He wants a number of agreements to have been made in the spring. FNV chairman Spekman said that in those negotiations there is no task to achieve a certain amount of cuts. According to him, that was confirmed at the table by the cabinet. He wants to talk about improvements to benefits for unemployment or disability and does not rule out that this will yield money. "But we do not have to meet a target." Bill at other ministries According to <entity id="person:hans-vijlbrief">minister Vijlbrief</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-sociale-zaken-en-werkgelegenheid">Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid</entity>, the reform of the WIA, the benefit for people who are ill, is "really the big thing". The cabinet has taken the cuts in social security off the table, but they are not entirely gone. If the cabinet and the unions do not reach an agreement, then the bill will end up at other ministries. Especially the Ministry of Education would then have to come up with a large part of that bill.

title: 'Phoenix planet' discovered, formed from the remains of a dead star
lead: British astronomers have discovered a new kind of celestial body: a planet orbiting a burnt-out star. The discoverers call it a phoenix planet, after the mythological bird that rises from its own ashes. The discovery could tell us more about the distant future of our own solar system. Scientists from the University of Warwick describe their discovery in the journal Nature Astronomy at the star HS 0209+0832, in the constellation Cetus. That is a white dwarf, about 250 light-years from Earth. A white dwarf is what remains when a star has lost most of its mass at the end of its existence. The sun will eventually meet that fate too: the star first swells up and swallows the nearest planets such as Venus, Mercury and perhaps the Earth. Most of the material is ultimately flung into space and forms an expanding nebula around a core that barely shines anymore. Clumped together The new research proves that this state need not be the end point of the life cycle of the planetary system. At HS 0209+0832 the material from the planetary nebula has apparently clumped together again into a new planet, just as happened billions of years earlier when the star formed. A 'second clutch' of this star, then. The scientists could rule out that it was a planet that had already formed earlier, because traces were found of heavy materials such as the metals zinc, copper and niobium. These are all elements that arise at the death of a star. Recycled The new planet is a gas giant slightly larger than Jupiter. It orbits its star every 4.4 days at only 4 percent of the distance between the sun and the Earth. That means that this planet is uninhabitable due to the radiation from its parent star. Because the distance is so small, the white dwarf moreover siphons off the outer layer of the planet. Similar planets made of recycled material had previously been found around pulsars, the end point of stars considerably larger than the sun. However, those are much less common in the universe than stars like the sun. That new planets can also form around that category was not yet known.

title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry for research into mirrored molecules
lead: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes to the Frenchman Henri Kagan and the Japanese Kenso Soai. They conducted research into the discovery of "non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis". In slightly more understandable Dutch: some molecules exist in two variants, which are each other's mirror image. If molecules are turned one way, they can have a different effect than if they are turned the other way. And that while they have the same composition. Scientists call that left-handed and right-handed. For example, there is the example of a cough suppressant, which is a painkiller when the molecules are reversed. "Medicines can have the desired effect one way, but the other way they may have no effect or may even be harmful," the committee states. Kagan (95) and Soai (76) have discovered exactly how that works. Kagan took the first step with his research from 1986, in which he managed to manipulate chemical reactions. Soai continued on that. In 1995 he discovered a chemical reaction in which only one of the two mirror images was formed. In the series Breaking Bad, chemistry teacher Walter White also once explained this principle: According to the Nobel committee, Kagan and Soai have found a solution to a "chemical mystery" more than a century old. "The chemical reactions they have developed are spectacular." Soai, affiliated with the Tokyo University of Science, heard the news while he was shopping. He calls it one of the most beautiful days of his life. Million euro The winners receive, in addition to eternal fame, also an amount of converted more than a million euros, which they must share between the two of them. They may spend the money on whatever they want. The Nobel Prize in Chemistry went last year to a Japanese, British and American-Jordanian researcher. They conducted research into so-called metal-organic frameworks. These are a kind of sponges that can make fruit ripen more slowly and can separate PFAS from water. Later this week, the Nobel Prize in Literature and the Nobel Peace Prize will also be awarded. Next week will then follow the Nobel Prize in Economics, although that is actually not a real Nobel Prize, because it was not devised by Alfred Nobel himself. The Nobel Prize in Economics has only been awarded since 1969, the others since 1901.

title: Searches at livestock farms in Overijssel over possible illegal cattle trading
lead: The <entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit</entity> (NVWA) searched homes and business premises of two cattle traders from Overijssel last week. They are suspected of fraud in cattle trading, illegally collecting cattle and transporting animals that may not be transported. The suspicion is that the two cattle traders worked together, says a spokesperson for the NVWA. The traders would have registered animals not at all or incorrectly. This poses a risk to animal health. In the event of a problem with the meat, such as leftover medicine residues, it is difficult to trace where the meat comes from. The searches were carried out last Wednesday by the Inlichtingen- en Opsporingsdienst (NVWA-IOD) of the authority. Among other things, business administration, telephones and ear tags for cattle were seized. That same day, a livestock truck was also intercepted that had left early in the morning from the business premises of one of the traders. The truck contained 21 cattle, none of them registered at the trader's address. At another livestock farm in Overijssel, another 32 cattle of the same suspect were found, which had been imported but not registered in the Netherlands. Unregistered cattle On the premises of one of the traders stood 88 animals that were not registered at that address, or not registered at all. At the other trader it concerned 19 animals. There were also cattle without the mandatory ear tag, a metal or plastic tag with a unique number with which the animals can be identified. With incorrect registration, the traders kept the real location of a business out of sight. On paper, the business was located at the address of the other trader. At the location that was thus kept out of sight, there were animals from home and abroad. Collecting animals for sale or slaughter is only allowed at a recognised location, writes the NVWA, and there are strict rules for this, for example to prevent the spread of diseases. Sick animals The inspectors also found a barn with sick cows. Some could no longer stand, others had serious infections. The suspect would have transported these animals, while this is not allowed due to their poor health. The animals were urgently examined by the veterinarian, three cows had to be put out of their suffering on the spot. The NVWA ensures that the other cows receive care. The suspects have not been arrested, but the criminal investigation is ongoing. For the sake of the investigation, the NVWA cannot comment on how they tracked the two down.

title: Stolen vase back to Sicily: 'Farewell painful, but serves a higher purpose'
lead: The Allard Pierson archaeology museum in Amsterdam has voluntarily returned an illegally excavated ancient vase to Sicily. The museum piece was handed over to an Italian delegation this morning. It concerns the Centuripe pyxis, which has been part of the collection for almost thirty years. The storage vessel from the third century BC depicts a wedding scene, watched by the Greek god Apollo. "A unique piece. So richly decorated, polychrome and also with gold leaf," curator Laurien de Gelder describes the vase. "Saying goodbye always hurts a little," she admits, "but it serves a higher purpose." Missing papers The vase was bought in 1997 at the Tefaf fair in Maastricht from a Swiss dealer. Although provenance documentation and an export permit were missing, according to the seller that was no problem. The vase was said to have been in Swiss private ownership since before 1970, the year in which a Unesco treaty laid down stricter rules. That it was in fact different became clear from a photo roll that Sicilian researchers found in 2016. It contained not only family snapshots of the former village photographer from Centuripe, but the man also turned out to have recorded the work and the loot of Sicilian grave robbers, including the pyxis. The photo roll also contained a wedding photo that turned out to be from 1976. The Swiss timeline turned out to be a lie. "Things have clearly not gone by the book," says Rogier Kalkers, who leads the provenance research into the Allard Pierson collection. "When we received a restitution request, it set us thinking." Legally speaking, return is not obligatory: our country only introduced the stricter rules in 2009, and they do not apply retroactively. "There has been a grey area for forty years for museums, collectors and dealers," says Kalkers. "In it, something could be ethically reprehensible, but strictly speaking not legally punishable." The museum says it no longer sees that as an excuse to hide behind. "We want to take our responsibility and therefore also part with it." And that is why an Italian delegation visited today, including the island's heritage minister, carabinieri and a representative of the Italian embassy. Kalkers: "There is a lot of attention for this problem in traditional source countries such as Italy, Greece, Turkey and Egypt, but less in market countries such as the Netherlands." Cooperation Kalkers is not afraid of empty display cases. "That is not the desired result for anyone, not for Italy either." The museum could, for example, still have asked for the vase on loan or for a replacement piece. Curator De Gelder: "Restitution is a solution for this kind of discussion, but it does not have to be the solution". Moreover, return also yields something for the Allard Pierson: ties with Sicily are strengthened. The museum will conduct further research into such pottery together with Sicilian experts. That will yield more knowledge about its production and use, and make it easier to trace forgeries, De Gelder predicts. In the coming years the museum will also continue to conduct proactive provenance research into its own collection. "This is not a final piece, but a stepping stone to joint follow-up research, in which we look with Sicilian and Italian authorities at how we proceed with other objects in our collection," says Kalkers. "We are focusing less on ownership and more on shared conservatorship."

title: Wild boars plough up cemetery in Schinnen: 'This is very painful'
lead: At a cemetery in Schinnen, wild boars have rooted up the ground of several graves. The graves are in a grass section and there is a fence around it, but that does not stop the animals. "It is very intense," the 88-year-old Nico Jetten tells L1 Nieuws . One of the ploughed-up graves is that of his deceased wife. She was buried last July in a new section of the cemetery. There are no traditional graves there, but small gravestones on a small grass field. Three weeks ago Jetten wanted to visit his wife's grave when he found the work of the wild boars. "It looked like a battlefield," he says. According to Jetten, the boars come onto the cemetery at night. They do not come as deep as the coffin, but he is afraid that the gravestones will be pushed over. "And it is simply painful." Warning signs hang at the cemetery: The cemetery is managed by the parish board. It is aware of the problems, says grave manager Huub Scholz. A few years ago the cemetery was expanded and especially that area is visited by the boars. "It is a green area with shrubs and trees, which the animals are attracted to." The cemetery is trying to put up a new fence as soon as possible. The <entity id="org:gemeente-beekdaelen">gemeente Beekdaelen</entity> is involved in this and is working with the parish board on a solution. "There will be a fence of about 150 metres at the back of the cemetery. Acoustic deterrents will also be used temporarily to keep the wild boars away," a spokesperson says.

title: Israel commemorates 7 October terror attacks, also gatherings in the Netherlands
lead: In various places in Israel, commemorations of the Hamas attack of 7 October 2023 are being held today. Several ceremonies began this morning at 06.29 local time. At that time, today three years ago, the terrorist attacks began. In various cities and villages, people are gathering today to commemorate. Israeli media write that in some municipalities flags are flying at half-mast. This morning there was a nationwide minute of silence and at 12.00 local time (11.00 Dutch time) that also happened. At 18.29, survivors and bereaved relatives gather in Israel at the place where the Nova music festival took place three years ago. At that festival, 378 people were murdered and 44 people were abducted to the Gaza Strip. This is how Israelis commemorated the attacks in Kfar Aza, 5 kilometres from the border with Gaza: Later in the evening is the largest commemoration, at 21.15 local time in Yarkon Park in Tel Aviv. The commemoration is organised by Kumu, a national citizens' movement founded after the tragedy of 7 October. The organisation consists of survivors and bereaved relatives of victims and hostages. According to The Jerusalem Post, the group refused to take part in the official commemorations of <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>. Many nationally organised commemorations already took place last Monday. The official national commemoration is legally fixed in Israel on the Hebrew date 24 Tishrei, which this year falls on 5 October. The Hebrew calendar shifts every year relative to our calendar. What happened on 7 October 2023? Shortly after sunrise, the Palestinian terrorist organisation Hamas attacked Israel. It began with thousands of rockets fired at the country. Meanwhile, an estimated 6000 Hamas militants crossed the border into Israel at dozens of places. Hamas members attacked military bases and stormed kibbutzim in small villages near the border. <entity id="org:gemeente-huizen">Huizen</entity> were set on fire and civilians were killed. The Nova music festival in the Negev desert was also a target. Festival-goers were shot en masse. 378 people were killed and 44 others were abducted. In total, around 1200 people were killed in the attacks. 251 people were taken hostage. Of the hostages, 168 were eventually released or rescued. The other 83 died. Israel responded to the attacks with a military offensive that resulted in genocidal violence. The war in Gaza has since cost more than 74,000 Palestinians their lives. This morning there were also protests by anti-government demonstrators. They believe that the government of Prime Minister Netanyahu failed in the run-up to 7 October and that there must be an independent investigation into the government's actions. In Tel Aviv, the fountain on Dizengoff Square was painted red. Photos and flowers have been laid on the fountain, in memory of the victims. Demonstrators also blocked a major highway in Tel Aviv for a moment of silence. They held up banners with the text "The people will not forget its sons and daughters". On a beach in Tel Aviv, unknown persons placed an installation depicting 1200 bodies. Next to it, in Hebrew, is the text "total failure". There are also commemorations in the Netherlands. In <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> there is a gathering in front of the Peace Palace, organised by the Council of Churches. It reports that Jews, Christians and Muslims will commemorate the events together and reflect on all civilian victims who fell on 7 October 2023 and later. Several speakers will be present at the commemoration. They will address the theme 'How do we move forward together?' Among others, minister Birke Rapp, rabbi Marianne van Praag and imam Shamier Madhar will speak. In <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>, the Israeli embassy and the Central Jewish Council are organising a commemoration. Batia Holin and her daughter Rotem Holin will talk about their personal experiences. On 7 October 2023 they lived in kibbutz Kfar Aza and survived the attack by Hamas.

title: Hidden AI debts also a risk for Dutch investors
lead: Tech companies such as Meta are investing in special financial constructions to keep AI investments off the books. Accountants must pay sharper attention to this, says regulator <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">DNB</entity>.

title: Schiedam shopping street floods after pipe burst
lead: Due to a broken main pipe, a shopping street in the centre of Schiedam flooded this morning. In some places the water stood 20 centimetres high. The financial damage runs into the tons. During work in the Hoogstraat the main water pipe was hit, causing the water to run into the street. At some shops it also ran inside. Water company Evides has shut off the main valve to prevent more damage. 'Everything is wet' "I come cycling along and suddenly I have a completely wet shop," a shopkeeper says to regional broadcaster Rijnmond . "From the front to the back of the storeroom." She has a shop where people can sell things they have made themselves. "New, old and made items. Everything is now wet." Mopping is difficult, she says, because the water cannot go anywhere. "The fire brigade is coming to help get the place dry, with a kind of vacuum cleaner for water." At an architecture firm further along, the place stayed dry. "We immediately tapped water so we can still make coffee," an employee says. "Now the water is shut off." Not ready for moving in The work took place at nine new rental homes in the Hoogstraat. They were supposed to be ready for moving in mid-November, but that is now delayed because four homes have water damage. "We have to open everything up," contractor Julias Huis in 't Veld says. "Plasterboard out, check pipes. The insulation also has to come out, otherwise mould will appear. It is a lot of extra work." The leak is also a financial setback, the contractor says. "The damage runs into the tons. People unfortunately have to wait even longer for their home. And the worst thing is that many businesses and shopkeepers here are affected." Leak closed Firefighters are helping to carry the water away. For example, they open drains so it can flow away better. The exact location of the leak is not yet known, Evides says. The investigation into it can take until the end of the afternoon.

title: Podcast De Dag: the magic of Messi
lead: Lionel Messi has played for the last time in the blue and white of Argentina. Last night he said farewell as an international during a friendly match against Benin. With tears, fireworks and beautiful words the footballer was honoured. Lionel Messi is the most decorated footballer ever: with 47 football prizes. He was named best footballer in the world more often than anyone else. Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Enjoying it? Then do not forget to subscribe. But that did not happen without a struggle, says sports journalist Edwin Winkels. He followed Messi closely in Barcelona and heard already at the beginning of this century about a boy in the club's youth academy who would be very good indeed. At FC Barcelona Messi managed to climb up and attract attention. But his bond with the national team of Argentina is more erratic. How did he nevertheless become the football hero who is now being farewelled? Want to respond? Email to dedag@nos.nl Presentation & editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editorial staff: Max Smedes

title: Apeldoorn air disaster 1946 commemorated again after ten years: 'Acknowledging grief'
lead: In Apeldoorn, an air disaster from eighty years ago was commemorated again after ten years. The accident at the time claimed the lives of 22 schoolchildren and the pilot. At today's commemoration, speeches were held and children laid wreaths at a monument. On 7 October 1946, a novice pilot flew a military aircraft over Apeldoorn. He had been selected to fly to the Dutch East Indies, but had to make a test flight first. The intention was to do that near Valkenburg airfield, near Katwijk. But the pilot decided to fly to Apeldoorn, specifically to the then Christian HBS, the current Christian Lyceum. He wanted to impress his mother, who lived nearby. But it went wrong. The pilot hit the school's chimney with a wing, causing the fuel tank to come loose and come down through the roof of the gymnasium. At that moment, 27 students were exercising in the hall. The aircraft's petrol caught fire and 22 students died. The pilot also did not survive the disaster. His mother rushed to the school after the accident. There she died of a heart attack when she heard that her son had died. Boys died The disaster made an enormous impression on the residents of Apeldoorn. Dies Griffioen knows that all too well. The 80-year-old woman had just been born at the time of the disaster, but the incident also affected her family. "Everyone in Apeldoorn heard that plane at some point," she says. "It flew over the HBS three times before it crashed." Her grandmother was told that her son, Griffioen's uncle Willem van Kampen, had been seriously injured in the accident. Later he died. Griffioen also thinks of the gym teacher, who had a hard time after the disaster. "He himself walked into that school to look for children and actually felt his whole life that he should have died instead of all the boys." Silence After the accident, it was no longer spoken about, says Griffioen. "The children were instructed to keep silent about the disaster. Among themselves they talked a little, of course, but it was not allowed. It had to be hushed up. After the war there was so much suffering that the strategy of mental health care was: silence." Forty years after the disaster, the first commemoration was held. In 2016 that happened for the last time. Until now. "At first I thought: I don't want this anymore," says Dies Griffioen. "But then that whole fear from the past creeps back. Like at our home, that the accident was not processed. That means you continuously have a kind of gigantic grief," she explains. "And that is as if a thin film is removed from the wound. And then it all comes back up." Griffioen today reflects on the boys who died, but also on the great grief of the surviving relatives. "It is also a kind of commemorating and acknowledging the grief."

title: Several cars set on fire in Zoetermeer parking garage, witnesses sought
lead: In a parking garage in Zoetermeer, several cars have been set on fire in recent times. The first fire was on 14 August and last week fires followed on 30 September and 4 October. In the night from Monday to Tuesday, two cars were set on fire and an attempt was made to set a third on fire, reports the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Cars parked next to the burning cars also sustained damage. All fires were at night. The police are investigating whether there is a connection between the arsons and call on witnesses to come forward. Camera surveillance Above the parking garage on the Parkdreef are homes. During the last fire of last night, residents had to leave their homes for some time. The municipality of Zoetermeer is installing camera surveillance, reports the Zoetermeers Dagblad . The hope is that this prevents new incidents. In addition, thanks to the surveillance, intervention can happen sooner.

title: Hoogeveen has had enough after days of unrest: 'They want to fight with police'
lead: In the quiet centre of Hoogeveen this afternoon, a terrace visitor points curiously at a group of teenagers hanging around near a monument. "Are those the children sitting there?", he asks a restaurant employee. "Yes", the employee explains. "But they can go far, you know." During the day, the Kerkplein near the Hoofdstraat is still peaceful, but in recent evenings fireworks, eggs and stones flew through the air.
