The LBIO and Jacobine Geel have so far not responded to questions from RTL, the broadcaster writes. <entity id="org:zbo-college-voor-de-rechten-van-de-mens">College voor de Rechten van de Mens</entity> Geel previously came under fire as chair of the College voor de Rechten van de Mens. In 2024, an independent committee investigated reports about her functioning and established "a pattern of systematically ignoring and excluding". Geel also showed "little sensitivity, empathy and understanding" towards two of the reporters. A pattern of discrimination was not established.

title: Israeli army continues to devastate Gaza, many missing bodies will never be found
lead: "The graves are ready, but still empty for now", says the 60-year-old Mohammed, who holds hope that one day he can retrieve his family members from under the rubble. In an Israeli bombardment he lost his wife, children, grandchildren and other family members. Some of them he was able to bury, others are untraceable. Many thousands of Palestinians are still missing. More than three years ago, after the attacks by Hamas, Israel began a devastating war in Gaza and bombed so heavily that tens of thousands of people ended up under the rubble. An estimated more than ten thousand people are missing, a large part of them lie under bombed buildings. Daily, surviving relatives and rescue workers try with the few resources they have to pull remains from the rubble, so they can then be buried. The victims can sometimes still be recognized by personal items such as jewelry, clothing or an ID card. They are buried during large funerals, often dozens at a time. These take place weekly in Gaza. Traces erased But many bodies will never be found, because they lie in areas where Palestinians and aid workers are not allowed to come. Israeli soldiers occupy at least 65 percent of the territory in Gaza. The government of Prime Minister Netanyahu keeps moving that border further, forcing the nearly two million Palestinians to survive huddled together along the coast in tent camps and destroyed buildings. Palestinians who cross the border markings, or according to the army come too close, are shot. Satellite images show that behind the so-called 'yellow line' the army is busy destroying buildings and clearing and moving rubble, while those buildings may still contain many bodies. The rubble makes way for cleared plains and military roads and bases. This is evident among other things from the analysis by the British research collective Forensic Architecture, which calls their research 'the cartography of genocide'. Using detailed maps, they chart the destruction of homes, agricultural land, hospitals, markets and other infrastructure. Everything needed for Palestinians to survive as a people. This also erases the traces of possible war crimes, the UN warned last month. The UN has long been calling on Israel to let researchers into the area. And the International Court of Justice has demanded this in the ongoing genocide case. But the border remains closed. Yet researchers can also collect evidence from a distance of destruction and attacks on civilians by using among other things satellite images, videos and witness statements. Even after last year's ceasefire, which is frequently violated, the army continues to destroy infrastructure. According to the Israeli government, this is necessary for its own security. Experts point out that the government is aiming to make the area uninhabitable and to displace Palestinians. Giving loss a place Exactly where the bodies still lie under the rubble is not known. Only surviving family members can indicate the locations. Moreover, it is difficult to retrieve the remains from under the buildings. Israel refuses to let heavy equipment, such as excavators, in. Many bodies have by now largely decomposed. Once rubble is cleared, evidence may have been lost that can never be found again, argues Jessica Dorsey, who conducts legal research on modern warfare at Utrecht University. "Think of impact marks, fragments of ammunition and the precise physical context of an attack. That does not make a case impossible, other evidence can reconstruct a lot." Quite apart from the investigation into war crimes, it is of great importance for surviving relatives to find and identify their dead, so they can mourn and give it a place. "The recognition for the dead is very important in war situations", says Dorsey. "The disappearance of the physical traces can take away that possibility for families forever." Mohammed, like many others in Gaza, may never be able to bury part of his family. Rescue workers have told him that they did everything to find the bodies of his family members, but that they cannot manage it. "I would have so much wanted them to have a grave", says Mohammed. "Then I could visit them during holidays."

title: Ban on assembly in Liège after education protests get out of hand
lead: A ban on assembly came into effect in Liège this morning after education protests got out of hand. It is not permitted to walk in the street in groups of more than three people. In Belgium, protests have taken place in recent days against planned cuts to education. In Liège, dozens of activists went past secondary schools on Tuesday, where they smashed windows and set fire to rubbish bins. The police dispersed the group. Some shops closed early because of the unrest. There have also been acts of vandalism and looting, writes the Flemish broadcaster VRT NWS . Violence increasing The head of the police in Liège speaks of "a continuing increase in violence". He also sees more rioters in the city. According to him, these are people who have nothing to do with the school pupils. Yesterday more than fifty people were arrested; several police officers were injured. The ban on assembly applies until 6 October 23.00, says mayor Demeyer. There are exceptions for families, police officers and emergency services. Other places in Belgium are also restless, but in Liège the protests are the most intense. Call for calm According to minister Quintin of Security and <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, the unrest is being stirred up by the Antifa movement. That is an umbrella term for radical-left activists who seek confrontation with the extreme right. "We know that a movement, of the Antifa type, is active in Liège," says the minister. "Adults who manipulate children to convey violent political messages. That is completely unacceptable." Spilled over from France The protests have partly spilled over from France, where since the end of last month school pupils have been demonstrating against overdue maintenance of buildings, classes that are too large and the teacher shortage. There too, it regularly ends in violence. Only yesterday the police in Marseille used tear gas. According to school pupils, the police also deployed flash grenades, which can briefly blind people. The police deny that. A school pupil lost his hand this week because a flash grenade exploded in his hand, after which the police announced that they would temporarily stop using these grenades.

title: Trial against Dave De K., who killed a toddler and left him behind on Zeeland island, begins
lead: In Ghent, the trial started today against Dave De K. (39) and his ex-girlfriend Romy W. because of the death of toddler Dean. Four years ago, the four-year-old Dean was found dead near the work island Neeltje Jans in Zeeland. The Belgian De K. is suspected of kidnapping and manslaughter of the Belgian toddler, his girlfriend of complicity in the kidnapping, writes Omroep Zeeland . The mother of Dean Verberckmoes voluntarily had herself treated for a depression at the psychiatric department of the hospital in Sint-Niklaas, near Antwerp, at that time. She had agreed with De K. and his girlfriend that they would take care of Dean. Drank too much During that sleepover, things went wrong. W. was in treatment for her alcohol addiction. Because she would have drunk too much after all, the couple got into an argument. De K. would have driven away angrily together with Dean. When the mother wanted to pick up her son a few days later, that was not possible, the couple let know. A day later, the mother called the police. They tracked down De K. a few days later. The toddler was not with him. After a day of police interrogations, De K. admitted that he had left Dean at Neeltje Jans. In 2010, De K. already received a prison sentence of ten years for the fatal abuse of his 2-year-old stepson. He served that sentence. Jury The trial is expected to last eight days. A jury of twelve citizens will, together with judges, consider the question of guilt. In Belgium, citizens between the ages of 28 and 65 are selected for a jury by lottery. Today the text is read out stating who is accused of what.

title: At least thirty dead in Russian attacks on city near front line
lead: Thirty people have been killed in Russian attacks on the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk. That is reported by the local governor. The city lies just behind the front line in the Donetsk region. The Russian army wants to take that area. Bombs fell in a street where two city buses were driving. President Zelensky speaks of an attack on a bus stop. Eighteen people were also injured. Governor Vadym Filashkin has shared images on Telegram of debris in the street. A burned-out bus can also be seen in them. "These are people who were killed by the Russian army," he said. "There is no justification for this, and there cannot be." The governor calls on people in the Donetsk region to flee to safer areas in Ukraine. Many civilians refuse to leave their homes and possessions behind. Ukraine has also carried out attacks on Russia again. The army reports that Ukrainian armed forces hit the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refinery in the Russian region of Bashkortostan. Death toll in Pryloeky rises Yesterday there were large-scale attacks in various places in Ukraine, including the northern city of Pryloeky. Rescue workers there found two more bodies while searching through the rubble. This has brought the death toll from the attacks to 22, including five children.

title: The Hague agrees after long-running feud, Van Gogh Museum can start renovating
lead: The Ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-onderwijs-cultuur-en-wetenschap">Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap</entity> (OCW) and the Van Gogh Museum have reached an agreement on the financing of the renovation of the building. "This has removed the long-term uncertainty about the future of the museum", the museum writes in a press release. According to the Amsterdam museum, a thorough renovation is needed. The building is said to be in poor condition after fifty years of "intensive" use. It would also fall short "in the areas of safety, climate control and sustainability", according to the statement. However, OCW and the museum could not agree on the financing of the project. The renovation is expected to cost around 104 million euros. And that could not be paid for with the annual subsidy of 8.5 million euros, museum director Emilie Gordenker said last year. At the time, the ministry said the museum was already receiving enough subsidy. Tempers ran high. Gordenker even told The New York Times that the museum might have to close if the State did not make more money available. For a moment it seemed that the two parties would fight out the financing issue in court, but at the last moment it was decided to talk to each other through a mediation process. Renovation to start in 2028 So OCW and the museum have now come to an agreement after all. What the details of the agreement are is not known. Museum director Gordenker is pleased with the agreements made: "The renovation is necessary to preserve this building and this world-famous collection in a responsible way for visitors, staff and the generations after us." The renovation will start in the autumn of 2028. The museum says that the building will not undergo "far-reaching changes" and that a large part of the improvement will take place behind the scenes. During the work, the museum will be partially open. The permanent collection will remain accessible, according to the Van Gogh Museum. It is unclear how long the renovation will take.

title: Maastricht to create 30 senior zones, against overburdening of care and loneliness
lead: Due to ageing, in 2030 one in four residents in South Limburg will be 65-plus. In order to be able to care for them, existing neighbourhoods in the Maastricht-Heuvelland area are being transformed into a kind of senior campus. In this way, elderly people can continue to live independently for longer. In total there will be 30 so-called housing-care zones in the Maastricht-Heuvelland area. This involves an investment of 33.4 million euros, reports L1 Nieuws . That amount is being made available by health insurers CZ and VGZ through the Integrated Care Agreement (IZA). The main goal of IZA is to keep care in the Netherlands good, accessible and affordable. From GP to flow-through broker What makes the Limburg project unique according to Petra Lamberts, chair of Deltaplan Maastricht Heuvelland, is that care and welfare organisations here work together with housing corporations. For example, apartment complexes, often social rental, are being adapted for rollators or wheelchairs and for people with dementia. The entrance or gallery is made more accessible, for example, or a passage to the meeting room is created. To counter loneliness, more activities are organised, for example in a communal living room. Because "loneliness is a predictor of care demand", says Lamberts. "People feel ailments sooner when they are alone. When they take part in activities, they are distracted and people are moreover stimulated to use their skills." Furthermore, care such as the dentist, outpatient clinic and GP are within walking distance. And the tasks of informal carers can occasionally be taken over, so that they do not become overburdened. Elderly people who do not yet have suitable housing can ask a flow-through broker to help them in their search for a suitable senior home. This is good for the flow in the housing market, but according to Lamberts can also relieve the burden on care. "We know that if people stay in unsuitable housing for too long, they move to a nursing home sooner. Such a move is often disruptive for those people. In many cases they deteriorate quickly." On time According to Lamberts, this project is not only intended for today's elderly, but also aimed at people who will soon be of age. "The biggest cost item in care is staff. Receiving a year of home care, such as wound care at home or helping people shower, costs around 12,000 euros per year. But living in a nursing home for a year costs more than a ton." With the 30 housing-care zones, she hopes that the few care staff that are still there can be deployed better. At the moment, nineteen zones are already in development. Next year all 30 must be ready. The plan is ambitious, but badly needed, says Lamberts "I think there will no longer be a care infarction, simply because we started on time." She says that the Ministry of Health, Sport and Welfare sees this project as an example. "This delta plan could just possibly be rolled out across the whole country."

title: In Limburg no dike reinforcement but piles under the home against the rising water
lead: A house in Well in North Limburg has been raised more than a metre and a half and placed on piles. This must provide protection against high water from the Maas and serves as an alternative to traditional dike reinforcement. In total, three houses in Well will be placed on piles. The old dike on De Kamp near Well no longer met the latest high-water standards, which meant there was a risk of flooding when the river rose. That had already happened in the past. Back then the houses flooded. Village view A traditional dike raising would, according to <entity id="org:waterschap-limburg">Waterschap Limburg</entity>, however seriously affect the historic village view and the landscape, writes L1 Nieuws . That is why the Waterschap chose, for the first time in its history, the so-called jacking up of the houses. There was also a financial motive, as a representative of Waterschap Limburg explains: "This saves about half in costs compared with a green dike ( ed., dike reinforcement )." In total, three homes will be raised by about a metre and a half. No wet feet Yesterday interested parties could admire the house on piles from a specially arranged viewing point. "I think it is great, it is really once in a lifetime that you can see something like this", one of the spectators beams. Another visitor points to the practical purpose of the intervention: "Wonderful that something like this is possible, but the most important thing is of course that those people will no longer get wet feet." Watch here how that went:

title: Yesilgöz now calls Russia 'the enemy' but that means 'not suddenly a different approach'
lead: Defence Minister Yesilgöz (VVD) no longer speaks of Russia as "the aggressor" but as "the enemy". With an increasing number of sabotage practices, drone attacks and other kinds of threats and incidents on our continent, the minister believes you must clearly name what is going on. For a long time Russia was not spoken of in such terms, so her words - during the treatment of the defence budget in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> - caused a stir in The Hague today. Yet it means nothing for the actual policy, Yesilgöz explained to the NOS during a suspension of the debate. That policy of investing more in our security, being alert and joining forces with European countries has been underway for years - since the invasion in Ukraine. "It is very clear that Russia presents itself as the enemy. That does not yet mean that we are at war or will suddenly have a completely different approach." This is how Yesilgöz put it in the Tweede Kamer: The minister does speak of a "new reality" because of the increasing number of incidents. Russia was already the greatest threat on our continent but that threat has become even greater, she says. The attacks just across the borders of European countries, pinpricks and intimidations have increased recently, says the minister. "Putin is testing how strong our alliance is". Experts advised the minister to name things as they are. "That is what I do", says Yesilgöz. <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">Minister Berendsen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> was asked in another debate about his opinion on his colleague's statements. In a <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> government members are supposed to "speak with one mouth", which means that they express the same opinion outwardly. "The <entity id="pos:minister-van-defensie">minister van Defensie</entity> also speaks on my behalf", said Berendsen. "Russia is our greatest security threat." Berendsen did acknowledge, after all kinds of questions from opposition parties, that he had not been informed in advance by Yesilgöz about her chosen words. Threat picture Earlier this year the intelligence service <entity id="org:directoraat-generaal-algemene-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">AIVD</entity> concluded in its annual report that in eighty years there had never before been a threat picture like now. Security service <entity id="org:militaire-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">MIVD</entity> also warned in its annual report that the armies of China and Russia are becoming ever stronger and cooperating more. The Kamer and minister are debating today about the planned billions in investments for defence. According to Yesilgöz, increasingly close coordination is taking place with European countries on how to respond to threats, but in "essence" nothing changes now in the approach. "We were already not naive and we will not become so." Embassy angry The Russian embassy in our country is taking the matter seriously. "With her statements, minister Yesilgöz again shows that the Netherlands chooses the destructive route of confrontation", the embassy writes on social media. Russia wants to know whether the minister spoke on behalf of the entire Dutch <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. "Russia has no aggressive intentions toward Europe and also not toward the Netherlands", states the embassy. "But at the same time we do not accept threats or ultimatums. We will respond to that directly and crushingly", according to the statement.

title: Former head of German intelligence possibly passed information to China
lead: The former leader of the German intelligence service passed secret information to China, writes Der Spiegel . According to the news magazine, the police are investigating the contacts that former chief August Hanning maintained with Chinese intelligence services after his retirement. Hanning is said to have passed the secret information to a foreign intelligence service in 2022. To do so, he may first have bought the information from an employee of the Bundesnachrichtendienst (BND); the German intelligence service. The police investigation is said to have revealed that the employee shared confidential documents with Hanning for years, also after the top official's retirement. Hanning (80) headed the BND from 1998 to 2005. After that he worked as a private adviser. He is said to have shared the information for payment. Treason German authorities came across the case after a house search at Hanning's home, because of a kidnapping case. Hanning may have been involved in that, although he himself denies it. During the house search, officers discovered highly sensitive information originating from the BND. It concerned recent documents that the former top official should never have had. The former head of the intelligence service was arrested at his home two days ago . Hanning is suspected of espionage, obtaining state secrets and treason. The former employee who is said to have passed on the information has also been arrested; until the spring he still worked for the BND and held a high position at the service. Activities approved Der Spiegel also reports today that the BND had officially approved that the suspected employee performed activities for Hanning alongside his work for the intelligence service. Der Spiegel calls it "unlikely" that the disclosure of secrets is legally covered by his secondary position. The magazine refers here to the Federal Civil Servants Act in Germany, which includes the duty of confidentiality for civil servants.

title: Police issue dozens of fines for filming accident A58 near Oirschot
lead: The police fined 29 drivers yesterday because they made images of a serious accident on the A58 near Oirschot while they were behind the wheel. The traffic police of East Brabant write on Instagram that taking photos and videos "crosses every standard of decency". Many emergency services came to the scene at the accident yesterday afternoon. They provided first aid to two injured people. An investigation was also carried out. The road was closed for several hours in the direction of Eindhoven. "By filming during a traffic jam, these drivers apparently accept the risk of a new collision for granted," the police write. "The fine amount of 449 euros, including administration costs, apparently does not deter sufficiently." The police report that post is on its way to the drivers. The police also ask road users to have respect for victims of an accident. "Behind every incident lies a personal drama."

title: How local residents in Rotterdam managed to prevent the collapse of houses
lead: When there are problems with the foundation of your house, it is easier to bury your head in the sand than to tackle the defects, recognises Remco Bruinsma from Rotterdam, who once had to deal with this himself. "But if your house is possibly on the verge of collapsing, then you do have to have an investigation carried out." Almost half a million houses in the Netherlands have problems with the foundation or will get them in the short term. Prevention can save a lot of houses, but people often do not know how the bottom layer of their house is doing. "The foundation is actually a kind of assassin," says Bruinsma. "You do not notice that it is not right until it is too late." The neighbourhood where Bruinsma lives, the Kleiwegkwartier, was rudely shaken awake just before King's Day in 2014, he says. "A whole block of houses was evacuated on the Margrietstraat because they had become unsafe. That is so close by that we asked ourselves: how is it with us then?" Groundwater level A group of residents had an investigation carried out and according to Bruinsma two thirds received bad news. In many places, pile rot has affected the wooden foundation. That can happen when the wooden piles stand dry for too long. Some houses had five to ten years left, for other houses the researchers said that residents can expect damage from the foundation within five years. Marianna Feenstra also lives in the Kleiwegkwartier and was shocked by the news. She and her husband Jelle were told that their house could last another five to ten years with the current foundation. "My husband wanted to measure the groundwater level himself. So he went through the neighbourhood with a measuring tape and saw that it was too low everywhere." Together with local residents, Jelle Feenstra therefore devised a plan. To drain rainwater better, the municipality had previously installed a new infiltration system in the neighbourhood. "Jelle often walked past the employees who installed it and brought the people a cup of coffee," says his wife. "In the end he asked whether they could place a pump to keep the groundwater better at level, so that not all the rainwater is immediately drained when the groundwater is already low." Pumps After many discussions with the municipality, it was possible in 2018 to place such a pump on a trial basis. "So it does not raise the groundwater and the drainage system still works well," emphasises Bruinsma, who was involved in the project. The trial succeeded and in the end the pump was added to the pumping stations of Rotterdam. The <entity id="org:zbo-stichting-autoriteit-financiele-markten">Autoriteit Financiële Markten</entity> previously calculated what the total costs are if all homes with foundation problems are repaired. That amounts to more than 11 billion euros. Bruinsma therefore thinks that more people in the Netherlands should use a pump to keep the groundwater level at level. Subsidence expert Otto Levelt of Deltares thinks it is a clever system that can continue to work reasonably long. "It is easier in some areas than in other areas, though." Good news At the beginning of this year, the Feenstras had their foundation investigated again. A few months later Marianna received the good news: the foundation has been declared in order for the next 25 years. That is the longest term that such an investigation can award. "The groundwater level must of course remain in order in the meantime," says Feenstra. Her husband Jelle did not live to see the news. He died in February. "It is a shame that he could not see the good result," says Marianna. She expects that an extra pump will soon be placed in the Statenlaanbuurt. "And the pumps will be called Jelle 1 and Jelle 2."

title: Podcast De Dag: Jane Doe and the revolt against elite university Cornell
lead: I am Jane Doe. Her name can be seen on signs at Cornell University in the state of New York, on campuses throughout the US and on social media. The case about the student who is said to have been drugged and then raped by a group of fellow students two years ago is causing a lot of commotion. Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. Reporter Simone Tukker reports from the US on what is now known about the case. It sparks a discussion about the culture on American campuses and the power of universities and student associations. And online, thousands of women open the conversation about their experiences. Respond? Email to dedag@nos.nl Presentation & editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editorial staff: Rosanne Sies

title: Rhine water level can no longer be gauged: sign switched off
lead: Not far from the point where the Rhine flows into the Netherlands, it is normally easy to see how high the water in the river is. At the well-known measuring point near Lobith, a large sign with illuminated numbers shows the current water levels there all year round. That sign no longer works due to the extremely low water levels. The measuring tube that hangs on the building by the sign is supposed to lie below the water surface in order to take measurements. After months of low water levels that is no longer the case, causing the data to no longer be correct. <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> has therefore decided to switch off the sign until the Rhine has recovered somewhat. The current water levels can still be followed online. For this, use is made among other things of a measurement a little further on, at Lobith Haven. A temporary measuring setup that collects data has also been placed on the other side of the sign. Beeping and creaking It is not the first time this year that measurements by Rijkswaterstaat get into trouble on the rivers in the east of the country. A week ago it became known that rivers there are so low that Rijkswaterstaat's sounding boats can no longer reach them. Inland shipping skippers must therefore now determine for themselves whether it is responsible to sail there. Although no major problems arise directly from switching off the level sign at Lobith, it is a symbol of a system that beeps and creaks under the extreme drought of recent months. Water experts and climate scientists expect that this kind of extreme low water will occur more often in the Netherlands in a changing climate. Rain needed Meanwhile, the water discharge at Lobith is around 580 cubic metres per second, which remains exceptionally low. When the Rhine will recover remains a question for now. That requires a great deal of rain, especially deeper in the Rhine basin in Germany and Switzerland. Rijkswaterstaat has had research done into how long it could take before the Rhine again reaches the somewhat more normal discharge of 1000 cubic metres per second, which incidentally would still be on the low side. Knowledge institute Deltares determined that if things go well that will happen in November or December, but that it is not excluded that it will only be the case in the new year. It could even be that the Rhine only recovers in the spring.

title: KLM cancels flights, fleet needs maintenance
lead: Airline KLM is cancelling several flights for the coming months. Many aircraft cannot be used temporarily because they are broken. As a result, the fleet is under pressure. It concerns flights in the period 26 October to the beginning of March. The aviation company does not yet know how many flights and which destinations are involved. "We are looking at flights with the least impact. Where we can rebook passengers as much as possible," a spokesperson says. With the early limiting of flights, the airline hopes to be able to guarantee a more reliable and stable schedule. Renewal According to KLM, cancelling the flights is necessary due to a combination of circumstances. There is unplanned maintenance and damage repair to aircraft, but also maintenance work that takes longer than anticipated. For example, the delivery of parts sometimes takes a long time. In May, the KLM division that performs maintenance on aircraft came under stricter supervision by the <entity id="org:inspectie-leefomgeving-en-transport">Inspectie Leefomgeving en Transport</entity> (ILT). Because the division allegedly did not meet new standards that prescribe that minor maintenance on aircraft must be handled and registered more quickly. The airline has recently invested seven billion euros in renewing the fleet. At the same time, old models are being phased out. A new type of aircraft recently arrived at Schiphol, the Airbus A350. "But it takes a while before that is operational," the spokesperson concludes.

title: British navy man suspected of attempted espionage for Russians
lead: A member of the navy was arrested in the United Kingdom on Tuesday, because he allegedly wanted to pass secret information to the Russians. He was charged today at a court in London. The hearing lasted only four minutes. "As you know, the matters you are accused of are too serious to be dealt with by this court," the judge said. He referred the case to a higher court, the Old Bailey also in London, where he must appear on 16 October. Wrong right away The 24-year-old suspect joined the Royal Navy in April 2024, and in November of that year he received his first posting on a ship. His task was to gather intelligence for warfare. Because of that position he had access to highly secret information. According to the charge, it went wrong almost immediately. The suspect copied secret information to which he had access to his private email account. He would also have translated an attempt at contact in Russian and searched the dark web for an address where he could pass information to Russia. Arrested earlier The counterterrorism police arrested him for the first time last year and again on Tuesday. Since then he has been in custody and will remain so at least until the hearing next week. The British navy does not want to comment further on the case. "As long as legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to respond," a spokesperson told the British press.

title: Climate summit in Fiji and Tuvalu largely failed, countries stay away en masse
lead: The preparatory climate summit in Fiji and Tuvalu, partly organized by Australia, has largely turned into a failure. From Monday, delegations were invited to these island groups to witness the consequences of the climate crisis. The turnout was greatly disappointing. In the end, only two leaders from countries outside the region attended the summit. These were Mauritius and East Timor, which cause only about 0.02 percent of global emissions. In addition, several ministers and officials from other countries were present. The idea was that world leaders would see these consequences with their own eyes, in order to influence the urgency of reducing emissions and thereby the decision-making during the most important climate summit of the year. Slowly underwater The delegations that did come saw how in Tuvalu an attempt is being made to create land, because what is left is slowly disappearing underwater. Tuvalu is only 26 square kilometers in size and consists of donut-shaped islands where erosion has caused the top of the island to disappear and water remains in the middle. On these narrow pieces of land, surrounded by an endless sea, only about 11,000 people live. There is no mountain or even a hill to be seen, causing the rising water to swallow more and more land. It is expected that the country may already disappear into the sea by the end of this century. The land reclamation project is a last attempt to survive, while the sea level keeps rising. In Fiji, delegations saw how, due to increased hurricanes and a rising sea level, more and more communities have to relocate. Here - as in many places in the Pacific - a true mass migration is underway. In Fiji, at least 700 communities are in extreme danger due to climate change. The government is in the process of relocating the most vulnerable villages to higher ground. Countries in the Pacific are on the front line of the climate crisis. The temperature here rises faster on average than in the rest of the world. The sea level also rises quickly. For example, the sea level at Suva, the capital of Fiji, rose by 29 centimeters between 1993 and 2024. This is not only due to climate change, local land subsidence also amplifies the effect. The plan to hold a preparatory climate summit before the major annual summit of the United Nations came mainly from Australian quarters. It had lobbied for years to organize this year - together with the countries in the Pacific - the major climate conference COP31. But after long diplomatic wrangling, it had to concede to Turkey. The preparatory summit in Fiji and Tuvalu was a compromise. The idea was that world leaders would have the precarious position of the island states in the Pacific firmly in mind before they make agreements during COP31 in Antalya. In Turkey, Australia may moreover lead the negotiations. Attention from the world But a trip to the isolated and difficult-to-reach Tuvalu proved too much for many. Yet according to the organizers it is not a complete fiasco. The leaders from the Pacific stood side by side with ministers from all over the world, including India, the United Arab Emirates and Turkey. Officials from the United Nations were also there, who have a say in climate financing. "We had said that we wanted to draw the world's attention to the problems in the Pacific, especially those of the small island developing states, and I think we succeeded in that," said Australian climate minister Chris Bowen. Tuvaluan climate refugees in New Zealand are already noticing that due to the lack of a future, the bond with Tuvalu is fading:

title: Provinces terminate contract with bus operator due to financial problems
lead: The provinces of <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">Flevoland</entity>, <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> and <entity id="org:provincie-overijssel">Overijssel</entity> will terminate the public transport contract with bus operator EBS early. The company would provide bus transport in large parts of the provinces until the end of 2035, but is running significant financial losses on this. The provinces have therefore agreed to terminate the contract in mid-2029. Due to the shortfalls at the bus operator, the provinces will provide financial support in the coming years to guarantee that the city and regional buses continue to run. The provinces do not want to say how much money is involved. The support comes on top of the tens of millions that the transport company receives annually from the provinces. Yet EBS announced earlier this year that the money falls short to continue carrying out the 12-year concession, writes Omroep Flevoland . Sounded the alarm According to the operator, this is due to "operational setbacks". For example, EBS is struggling with staff shortages, electric buses were delivered too late and due to shortages on the power grid there is insufficient capacity to charge buses. EBS has to do that at other locations, which leads to extra kilometres for which the company receives no compensation. The operator first sounded the alarm about this with the provinces in the spring. They then launched an investigation into the company's financial situation. The EBS buses have been running in Flevoland and parts of Gelderland and Overijssel since the end of 2022. The provinces gave the company preference over the operators Keolis and Qbuzz. Search for new operator Overijssel and Gelderland will look for another company that can provide public transport from July 2029. Gelderland wants to set up its own concession for the area of <entity id="org:gemeente-apeldoorn">Apeldoorn</entity> - Noord-Veluwe. What bus transport will look like from 2029 will be worked out in the coming months. EBS operates multiple public transport concessions spread across the country and will also provide bus transport in <entity id="org:provincie-zeeland">Zeeland</entity>. According to a spokesperson for the company, no losses are being incurred in other parts of the country. "It is purely this concession that is financially out of step, due to a combination of factors. The others are doing fine." Overloaded power grid In the <entity id="org:provincie-utrecht">provincie Utrecht</entity>, bus operators Transdev and Keolis are also experiencing problems due to the transition to electric buses . Keolis is in talks with the province of Utrecht, because the company is running much larger losses than expected in advance. Nothing is yet known about the outcome of the talks, writes RTV Utrecht .

title: Latvians arrested at British air force base
lead: The British military police arrested two Latvians (36 and 32) last night who were behaving suspiciously at an RAF air force base in the county of Cambridgeshire. They were initially detained for entering a prohibited area, later the suspicion was added that they wanted to cause damage to the United Kingdom. Guards at the base near the town of Molesworth discovered an abandoned car around 22:00 yesterday evening. There was also a small hole in the fence surrounding the base. The two had entered the site through it. The Latvians were found and arrested around 02:00. They were taken to a police station where the case was transferred to the counterterrorism department of the police in London. Fairford In a statement, the head of that department refers to the arrest last week of five men at the RAF base in Fairford, in the west of England. She understands that people immediately think of that, but for the time being she sees no connection whatsoever with that case. Americans It is striking that Americans are stationed at the base near Molesworth, according to the BBC . That was also the case at the base near Fairford. The American bombers that were stationed there have since left , because they would be in danger there. According to the BBC , American intelligence services are active at the base near Moleworth for operations in Europe and Africa. Searches In connection with the arrest of these Latvians, two addresses in Peterborough were searched. The explosives ordnance disposal service of the British army examined the car that was found, but found nothing unusual.

title: That crazy AI character on TikTok mainly wants you to buy his crypto
lead: A stylishly dressed young Frenchman who calls himself Jean Phil suddenly appears on TikTok and Instagram on 18 September. With his blonde bob and curled moustache, he is mainly shadowboxing in the videos. Many people find it funny-looking. Within a few days, the account attracts tens of millions of views, likes and hundreds of thousands of followers. He is the trendsetter and a new AI influencer seems to have been born. Jean Phil tries to cash in on that popularity with his own cryptocurrency $ JEANPHIL . Special, realistic-looking AI characters that promote their "own" cryptocurrency are springing up like mushrooms. They often have the same goal: going viral and getting people to buy their self-made cryptocurrency in order to then make money from it. Since recently, it is possible to create such an AI character within a few minutes. "Years ago, creating such content still required specific skills, such as very good knowledge of video editing," explains crypto expert Bart Mol. "Now everyone can copy each other directly and the question of what value such an AI influencer has is becoming increasingly relevant." Via a website, one can relatively easily create one's own cryptocurrency: the technical part of creating such a coin is taken off one's hands by the website. The unknown person behind $ JEANPHIL then promotes the cryptocurrency via social media. Genjutsu To create the videos on social media that are almost indistinguishable from real, the website Higgsfield is used, specifically the Genjutsu tool. The website launched its latest toy at the end of August. With the Genjutsu tool, you can take an existing video and then adapt it to your own wishes by replacing characters or specific elements from the video, while the rest remains unchanged. All of that can be done with a few mouse clicks. According to social media expert Kirsten Jassies, more and more of this kind of AI character are appearing. "The possibilities with AI are developing so terribly fast. We can hardly keep up with it ourselves." That people cannot keep up is visible in the reactions under videos of Jean Phil. Some think it is great, others do not like it at all. For example, people say they thought for days that Jean Phil was real and hoped so too. Others say they are disappointed in themselves because they only realised late that it was AI, after similar accounts appeared and the penny dropped. It is not forbidden to launch an AI character on social media, but since August new European legislation has been in force that should better protect people. In many cases, a digital watermark must be added to online content if it has been generated by AI. The AI regulation will be rolled out further in the coming years. In the videos on Jean Phil's account, the digital watermark is still barely visible; only in one video on both TikTok and Instagram. Money through trading Over time, online rumours circulated that a pump-and-dump scam would be carried out with the cryptocurrency, but so far that has turned out not to be the case. In a pump-and-dump, a cryptocurrency is artificially made popular, after which the creator sells his coins at a large profit and the price collapses. Since 2024, pump-and-dump actions with cryptocurrencies have been banned. However, public data from the $ JEANPHIL coin shows that every time people trade their purchased coins with each other, the creator of the coin keeps a small percentage of it. That would have earned the person about 250,000 dollars to date. "The creator of the coin will therefore also have the goal of keeping the trading in the coins alive, because that is how he makes money," Mol adds. At its peak, the coin had a total market value of almost eleven million dollars, converted to just under ten million euros. After similar accounts appeared online and people realised that this involves AI, the $ JEANPHIL coin lost a large part of its value.

title: Pro-Hamas uitingen bij demonstratie Amsterdam, had een wet iets veranderd?
lead: De Amsterdamse <entity id="person:femke-halsema">burgemeester Halsema</entity> keek "met grote afschuw" toe hoe pro-Palestijnse actievoerders gisteravond leuzen riepen als " Long live the 7th of October ", verwijzend naar de aanslagen van Hamas drie jaar geleden in Israël. Ook droegen ze spandoeken bij zich met teksten als " We Support Hamas ". De demonstratie werd echter niet verboden, totdat actievoerders elders in de stad tegen een politiecordon aanliepen. Waarom toen pas? Vier vragen over deze demonstratie: Had de demonstratie vanwege de leuzen verboden kunnen worden? Wat de demonstranten lieten zien was "shockerend en onsmakelijk" zei burgemeester Halsema mede namens het <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> en de <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> in een reactie , maar het was niet strafbaar. En dus kon ze niet ingrijpen. Een woordvoerder van het Amsterdamse OM licht toe: "Er was naar het standpunt van het OM geen sprake van opruiing; door de uitingen wordt men niet aangemoedigd strafbare feiten te plegen." Er is een wet in de maak die het verheerlijken van terrorisme strafbaar stelt, zo voegt hij toe. "Het zou goed kunnen dat sommige uitingen die gisteravond zijn gedaan strafbaar zullen zijn zodra dit wetsvoorstel wet is geworden. Maar om daar écht iets over te zeggen moeten we de tekst van de wet afwachten. Altijd zal per situatie en afhankelijk van de context moeten worden bepaald of iets strafbaar is of niet." "Een burgemeester gaat niet over de inhoud van een demonstratie", zo vertelt hoogleraar staats- en bestuursrecht Jon Schilder aan de NOS. "Zij mag alleen maar kijken of er wanordelijkheden dreigen. En dan pas mag ze ingrijpen." Halsema heeft dus juist gehandeld door de demonstratie niet direct aan het begin te verbieden, vindt hij. Waarom is de demonstratie dan toch op een gegeven moment verboden? Dat komt door de vrees voor wanordelijkheden. De actievoerders liepen vanaf de Dam een andere kant op dan ze aanvankelijk hadden aangekondigd, richting een plek waar veel gebouwen met een Joodse betekenis staan, zoals het Joods Museum, het Holocaust Namenmonument en de Portugese Synagoge. Agenten hielden de pakweg 75 actievoerders tegen bij het Waterlooplein en zeiden dat zij alleen naar het stadhuis mochten lopen, zo schrijft de lokale omroep AT5 . Een deel van de betogers probeerde door de linie van politieagenten te breken, wat hen niet lukte. De hele demonstratie is daarna door burgemeester Halsema ontbonden. Daarbij werd het even onrustig tussen demonstranten en politie. Wat zou een nieuwe wet veranderd hebben? Afgelopen zomer ging er een wetsvoorstel naar <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> waarin het verheerlijken van terroristische misdrijven strafbaar wordt gesteld, zowel persoonlijk als door het verspreiden van video of afbeeldingen met die strekking. Ook worden steunbetuigingen aan verboden terroristische organisaties verboden als de wet van kracht wordt. Een spandoek met 'We Support Hamas' erop, zoals gister op de Dam te zien was, zou na invoering van de voorgestelde wet niet meer mogen, zegt Schilder. "Zulke spandoeken zullen net als Hamas-vlaggen binnen de reikwijdte van dit wetsvoorstel vallen. Dat is iets dat daadwerkelijk wordt veranderd als deze wet zou worden ingevoerd." Als die wet al zou gelden, had dat nog steeds niet betekend dat burgemeester Halsema de demonstratie op 7 oktober op voorhand had kunnen verbieden, zegt hoogleraar Schilder. "Preventief optreden is niet mogelijk." Pas als bijvoorbeeld een vlag van Hamas ontvouwd wordt, kan de politie ingrijpen en mensen arresteren. Wat zou dan de straf zijn geweest? De straffen die daarbij horen zijn niet misselijk, vindt hij: maximaal twee jaar celstraf en een geldboete. Omdat het om een misdrijf gaat, zou overtreding ook een strafblad opleveren. Maar, zo waarschuwt hij, "het is maar de vraag of het OM er überhaupt aan toekomt: door ondercapaciteit moeten ze veel zaken laten liggen. Of ze zaken zoals deze gaan vervolgen, is dus voor een deel ook een politieke keuze." Een ander potentieel probleem met de wet is dat volgens hem "de grens niet duidelijk is" waar verheerlijking van terrorisme begint. Zo zou het spandoek met ' Long live the seventh of October ' dat gister in Amsterdam werd getoond een moeilijke zaak zijn voor de strafrechter. "Dat is grijs gebied, omdat niet duidelijk is wat er precies met die datum wordt bedoeld." "Het is niet zwart-wit. In dat opzicht doet het een beetje denken aan de 'minder Marokkanen'-uitspraak van <entity id="person:geert-wilders">Geert Wilders</entity>. Daar is jaren over gediscussieerd, tot uiteindelijk de <entity id="org:hoge-raad">Hoge Raad</entity> zei: dat was wel strafbaar." Op dezelfde manier, waarschuwt hij, kun je bij het verheerlijken van terrorisme niet bij voorbaat zeggen of iets wel of niet strafbaar is. "De strafrechter zal niet snel tot een veroordeling komen."

title: Christa Pike can walk again but is 'angry and confused', lawyers say
lead: Death row inmate Christa Pike can walk a little again. One of her lawyers said this to the British broadcaster BBC . The American woman is still in the hospital in a hazy state. Pike's lawyer Stephen Ferrell tells the BBC that he has not spoken to her directly, but had understood that her arms were swollen and that they barely functioned when she took her first steps in the hospital room. The 50-year-old Pike was to be executed last week in the US state of Tennessee by lethal injection, but that failed twice. She was convicted in 1996 for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. According to the non-profit organization Death Penalty Information Center, Pike is the first person to survive her death sentence by lethal injection. 'Angry and confused' Yesterday, another of Pike's lawyers said that she was "angry and confused" when she regained consciousness, but that she is very aware "that the state has tried to execute her". The first thing she asked after waking up was "where am I and who are you?", says her other lawyer Randy Spivey. According to Spivey, there was a lot of confusion with Pike and she wants to know what happened. "She asked about her team, she asked about the victim's family." The lawyer also said that Pike could not move her arms and could not swallow either. She also has pneumonia and a blood clot in one of her arms. Evidence What exactly went wrong during the execution is still unclear and is being investigated. A judge in Nashville yesterday ordered the state to preserve "everything that was in the room itself" as evidence of the failed execution attempt. According to her lawyers, Pike is handcuffed by one hand and her feet to the bed. The lawyers have asked the judge whether, given the injuries, she may be unfastened. The hospital staff is said to have requested this. The judge wants to decide on that only once the statement under oath is submitted, American media write. Her lawyers also argued that Pike has suffered enough and want the governor of Tennessee to commute her death sentence to life without the possibility of parole. Execution carried out in Texas Yesterday, the first execution since Pike's was carried out in the US. In the state of Texas, 46-year-old Jamaal Howard was put to death by lethal injection. Howard had been convicted of the murder of a shop employee during a robbery in 2000. He was 20 years old at the time. Shortly before the lethal injection with pentobarbital was administered, Howard apologized to the victim's relatives who were present at the execution. "I'm sorry for what happened. I hope you can forgive me one day." He also thanked his family and friends. The man took a few breaths and also gasped for air when the drug started to work. He then made snoring sounds and coughed, with the sound becoming softer each time. Howard was declared dead nineteen minutes after the injection, at 20:03.

title: Fake police officer gets four years in prison after raping international student
lead:
The court in The Hague sentenced a man to four years in prison for raping an international student. The 33-year-old man from The Hague, Ghalied A., posed as a police officer to get into the victim's home. In the night of 12 September 2024, A. rang the bell at the student's door, who at the time lived in a student complex in The Hague. He claimed to have been tipped off that there were drugs in her room and said he had come to check on that. The South Korean student, who had been in the Netherlands for only a month, did not know the rules and procedures and let the man in. Once inside, the woman had to stand naked with her hands against the wall and bend through her knees a few times, after which the man molested her. Immediately after the incident, the victim locked herself in the bathroom and called 112. The officers who arrived on the scene found her naked and crying.

Returned to South Korea

According to the court, the woman had dreamed her whole life of studying in Europe. After the incident, she allegedly came to hate the Netherlands so much that she immediately returned to South Korea. The court judged the victim's statements to be concrete, detailed and consistent. The suspect's statement was dismissed. The man from The Hague kept insisting that the two had got talking outside <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de kamer</entity> and that she had invited him inside.

Indecent exposure

A few months after the incident, the man tried again to strike in exactly the same manner. Again he rang the bell at the same student complexes and posed as a police officer. This time no one opened the door. The suspect is also guilty of indecent exposure in another student complex. Last year he allegedly showed his genitals in public there and openly stood masturbating. The Public Prosecution Service had demanded five years in prison and tbs with compulsory treatment. The judge decided not to impose tbs, because the man refused to cooperate with psychological examination. Extra supervision of the man will be maintained after his prison sentence.

title: Much smoke from fire in parking garage under Olympic Stadium
lead: In the parking garage under the Olympic Stadium in Amsterdam a fire raged last night. The fire released a lot of smoke. The fire broke out around 18:30 in the crawl space of the parking garage. The fire brigade did not disclose whether cars were on fire. Among other things foam was used to fight the fire. Because the seat of the fire was difficult to reach, extinguishing it took a lot of time. Around 00:38 the fire was under control. The area around the stadium was cordoned off, writes regional broadcaster NH . The safety region called on local residents to close windows and doors if they were bothered by the smoke.

title: Maduro and wife charged with torture of opponents and Americans
lead: The captured Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores have both had a new charge filed against them in the United States. They are now also accused of having tortured political opponents and American citizens to maintain their position of power in the South American country. Earlier they were already prosecuted for, among other things, corruption and facilitating large-scale, international cocaine trafficking. Flores (69) and Maduro (63) were abducted from Venezuela by the American army on 3 January and brought to New York. They pleaded not guilty to the drug charges and have been held in the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn since their arrest. Their trial is scheduled for 1 June 2027. Electric shocks News agency Reuters reports that Maduro and Flores risk a mandatory minimum sentence of 50 years in prison if they are found guilty. The US and human rights groups had long accused Venezuelan officials of the Maduro regime of torturing prisoners. Today's charge is the first time that Maduro is criminally prosecuted for those allegations. According to the charge, an American citizen was detained in Venezuela in 2022 and accused of conspiracy to murder Maduro. The man would have been tortured by military counterintelligence officers with beatings and electric shocks to his arms, legs and genitals. Heart surgery In another case, prosecutors state that Maduro in 2013 had ordered the arrest of a Venezuelan soldier whom he suspected of planning a coup. During interrogations, the officer would have been mistreated, among other things, repeatedly with a live wire. Today the judge rejected a request to release Flores from prison due to health problems. Flores's lawyers argued that she needs heart surgery and proposed moving her to a home with 24-hour security. They said she poses no danger to society. The prosecutors argued that Flores receives adequate medical care in the detention center in New York and that she is an extreme flight risk. In rejecting the request, the judge said that the evidence against Flores was substantial. Prosecutors say she accepted hundreds of thousands of dollars in bribes from a major drug lord.

title: Search of ex-Prince Andrew's homes unlawful, but investigation continues
lead: A small success for the British ex-Prince Andrew. A court in London agrees with him that the police made important mistakes in February during the searches of his homes in Sandringham and Windsor. The search warrants were based on the wrong article of law. The court has therefore declared the warrants unlawful. This does not mean that the investigation against him must now be stopped, according to the court. The searches were related to the investigation into the question of whether the ex-prince shared secret information with the American sex offender Jeffrey Epstein during the time he was British trade envoy (2001-2011). Mistakes acknowledged Andrew (66) - who now goes through life as citizen Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor - went to court to have the search warrants declared unlawful. Presumably he hoped that any evidence found during the searches could not be used against him. Whether that reasoning holds is still the question. The police do not yet have to return the prince's seized property. The court will consider next year whether material taken during the searches may still be used as evidence. Andrew did not appear in court himself, possibly partly because he did know how this would end. The police had namely already admitted in July that mistakes had been made in drawing up the search warrants, but had not yet made this public.

title: Gouden Televizier-Ring voor De Bondgenoten, presentator Jan Versteegh wint ook
lead: De Gouden Televizier-Ring 2026 is gewonnen door de SBS6-reality-spelserie De Bondgenoten . De keuze van de Nederlandse kijker werd bekendgemaakt door oudgediende tv-presentator Henny Huisman. De andere genomineerden waren consumentenprogramma Kassa van BNNVARA en de Twentse dramaserie Woeste Grond van AVROTROS. Presentator Jan Versteegh van De Bondgenoten won ook de Televizier-Ring voor beste presentator. Andere genomineerden waren Thomas van Groningen en Tim Hofman. Annet Malherbe won de Televizier-ring voor de beste acteur. Ze kreeg die voor haar rol als Emma in Rust en Vreugd . Die dramaserie ging over een net weduwe geworden vrouw die een tuintje krijgt op een volkstuinencomplex. Ze raakt daar betrokken bij de onderlinge spannen en vetes. PaardenpraatTV De prijs voor Televizier-Ring Talent, de publieksprijs voor aanstormend tv-talent, ging naar interieurstylist en tv-persoonlijkheid Daan Alferink. Hij versloeg radiomaker Bram Krikke en WNL-presentator Frank van Leeuwen. Even daarvoor won PaardenpraatTV, de Gouden Televizier-Ring Jeugd voor het populairste kinderprogramma. Het YouTube-kanaal over paarden wordt onder meer gepresenteerd door Britt Dekker. Britt Dekker was in extase toen ze de award in ontvangst nam: Het BNNVARA-programma Even Tot Hier won de Televizier Ring Impact, de prijs voor het tv-programma, tv-moment of de documentaire die de meeste maatschappelijke impact heeft gehad. Het programma haalde ruim 3 miljoen euro op voor het door oorlog getroffen Oekraïne. Dat deed het door de stichting van de Oekraïense accordeonist Oleg veelvuldig onder de aandacht te brengen, Met het opgehaalde geld konden ambulances en medische apparatuur worden gekocht. Bij Andy in de Auto werd winnaar van de Televizier-Ring Online-videoserie. In dat programma heeft oud-voetballer Andy van der Meijde gesprekken met uiteenlopende gasten in zijn auto. Van der Meijdes serie versloeg Opdracht van StukTV en Tobi's Eetclub , van Tobias Camman, die de prijs al eens won voor de FOMO Show .

title: Vier astronauten na 237 dagen terug op aarde, record voor Europese vrouw
lead: Vier astronauten zijn na acht maanden teruggekeerd naar aarde vanuit het internationale ruimtestation ISS. SpaceX bracht de bemanning met een ruimtecapsule veilig terug. De zogenoemde splashdown vond plaats voor de kust van Los Angeles. Nadat de capsule aan boord van een bergingsschip was gehesen, kwam het viertal naar buiten. "Eindelijk weer douchen", reageerde een van de astronauten bij terugkomst. De bemanning bestond uit twee Amerikanen, een Rus en een Française. Zij werden in februari met spoed naar het ruimtestation gebracht om vier andere bemanningsleden te vervangen. Die waren vroegtijdig naar huis gestuurd nadat een van hen ziek was geworden. Het was de eerste medische evacuatie van NASA in 65 jaar tijd. De astronauten zouden eigenlijk eerder geleden al terugkeren. Dat ging niet door omdat de nieuwe lichting astronauten drie weken later dan gepland bij het ISS aankwam. Hun ruimtecapsule kampte met een lek in de brandstofvoorziening en moest eerst worden gerepareerd. De ruimtereis duurde in totaal 237 dagen. Daarmee heeft de Franse astronaut Sophie Adenot een record gevestigd: nog nooit verbleef een Europese astronaut zo lang onafgebroken in de ruimte. Onderhoud aan het ruimtestation Tijdens haar verblijf voerde Adenot drie ruimtewandelingen uit om onderhoud te verrichten aan het inmiddels bijna 28 jaar oude ruimtestation. Daarmee is ze de tweede Europese vrouw die tijdens haar verblijf het ruimtestation verliet. De nieuwe bemanning, die vorige week aankwam, vestigde ook een Amerikaans record . Ze kwamen in acht uur aan bij ISS, veel korter dan het oude Amerikaanse record van 12,5 uur. Zij zullen ongeveer een halfjaar in de ruimte verblijven. Op dit moment zijn er zeven astronauten in het ruimtestation, afkomstig uit de Verenigde Staten, Canada en Rusland.

title: Well-preserved fossil tells how mammals came to eat differently from the dinosaurs
lead: A well-preserved fossil of 165 million years old shows scientists how mammals in the time of the dinosaurs developed a new way of swallowing. The find is so well preserved that the outline of the animal can be clearly seen and even impressions of its skin and fur are recognisable. The fossil was found several years ago in China. It concerns an animal that looked like a cross between a beaver and a platypus, with the flat, scaly tail of a beaver and the powerful swimming legs of the platypus. With its weight of 1 to 2 kilos and length of 50 centimetres, it was a hefty one in a time when most mammals were not much bigger than a mouse. With a reference to its large tail, scientists named the animal Megacauda sungei . Although the animal resembles two present-day species, no descendants of it remain today. Because the fossil remained so well preserved after the carcass ended up in the river mud, the animal's hyoid bone was also preserved. It is often not found because it is small and fragile and, unlike other bones, does not connect to other bones. This find sheds more light on how this kind of early mammal had a different way of eating than the dominant reptiles of that time. Because their bone was more complex than that of dinosaurs, mammals can use their mouth muscles to chew food and swallow it in small amounts. Reptiles, by contrast, bite off their prey in big bites like crocodiles, or devour it in one piece like a snake. The scientists explain how this development gave mammals an advantage. "Thanks to this function, different species could develop specific teeth and tap into a variety of food sources. They could become carnivores, insectivores, herbivores, omnivores and everything in between." Evolutionary innovation It led, after the extinction of the dinosaurs 66 million years ago, to mammals being able to develop into the new dominant animal species. "It was an enormous innovation in evolutionary terms. Mammals all swallow just as efficiently and effortlessly." The hyoid bone was also crucial for swallowing when suckling young animals. In the case of megacauda, the researchers discovered that its diet consisted of salamanders. Evidence for that were half-digested vertebrae that they found in its stomach and skeletons of these prey animals in the same soil layer. They deduce from this that this megacauda must have lived partly in the water, where it hunted like an otter. To avoid encountering flesh-eating dinosaurs, it was probably a nocturnal animal, which spent the day in burrows in the river bank.

title: Duizenden aanhangers opgepakt volgens Indiase Kakkerlakken-beweging
lead: De Indiase autoriteiten hebben duizenden aanhangers van de Kakkerlakken-beweging opgepakt, zegt de beweging op sociale media. Het is onduidelijk hoeveel mensen daadwerkelijk in totaal zijn opgepakt. Er is geen onafhankelijke bron die de aantallen bevestigt. Ook prominente leden als woordvoerder Deepak Baliyan zouden daags voor een groot protest in de hoofdstad New Delhi zijn gearresteerd. Al dagen worden in India demonstraties gehouden vanwege een omstreden herziening van de kieslijsten. Daardoor dreigen volgens de actievoerders miljoenen Indiërs niet te kunnen stemmen bij toekomstige verkiezingen. De actievoerders eisen het vertrek van het hoofd van de Indiase kiescommissie Gyanesh Kumar. De kiescommissie zegt dat de herziening nodig is om onder meer ongeldige inschrijvingen te verwijderen, maar volgens tegenstanders raken vooral minderheden hun stemrecht kwijt, met name moslims. In de deelstaat West-Bengalen verloren miljoenen mensen al hun stemrecht. Tegenstanders zien de herziening ook als een poging om toekomstige verkiezingswinsten veilig te stellen voor de Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) van premier Modi. Ook oppositiepartijen en prominente politici zoals Rahul Gandhi hebben zich aangesloten bij de protesten. Wat is de Kakkerlakken-beweging? De Kakkerlakken-beweging is een prominente beweging in de aanhoudende golf van publieke onvrede over de regering van de Indiase premier Modi. De acties begonnen met de roep om onderwijshervormingen na een groot examenfraudeschandaal. Indirect kostte dat schandaal de levens van meer dan twintig studenten die door psychische druk suïcide pleegden. Dagenlang gingen daarom duizenden studenten de straat op om het vertrek te eisen van de minister van Onderwijs. Die bewindspersoon is inmiddels afgetreden. De protestbeweging omarmde de naam 'Kakkerlakken' nadat een rechter de aanhangers daarvoor had uitgemaakt. De rechter noemde jongeren zonder opleiding of baan die zich bezighouden met activisme of journalistiek kakkerlakken en parasieten. Volgens de Kakkerlakken-beweging werd een groep studenten uit de westelijke stad Pune opgepakt en met een bus naar een onbekende locatie gebracht. De groep was op weg naar het protest tegen de herziening in New Delhi op zaterdag. Ook Daliyan zou naar een onbekende locatie zijn gebracht. Hij en zijn broer werden volgens de beweging door de Indiase politie zwaar mishandeld. De beweging eist hun vrijlating.

title: Eerst wel, toen niet, nu weer wel: regenboogvlag gaat toch bij Tweede Kamer hangen
lead: Een meerderheid van de Tweede Kamer is ervoor dat zondag een regenboogvlag bij het Tweede Kamergebouw wappert op Coming-Outdag. Dat bleek donderdagavond bij een hoofdelijke stemming. Bij de stemming donderdagavond laat in de Tweede Kamer waren 90 Kamerleden voor het hijsen, 36 waren er tegen. Het is voor het eerst dat deze vlag voor de Tweede Kamer te zien zal zijn. De Kamerleden hebben individueel gestemd, maar duidelijk was wel dat de meeste Kamerleden van D66, VVD, CDA, Pro, Partij voor de Dieren, SP, ChristenUnie, 50Plus en Volt voor stemden. De Kamerleden van JA21 en groep-Markuszower waren er niet. PVV, Forum voor Democratie, Denk en SGP waren tegen. Pittige discussie Het wel of niet hijsen van de regenboogvlag heeft de afgelopen dagen achter de schermen tot nogal een pittige discussie geleid in de Tweede Kamer. Aanvankelijk vond het presidium, het dagelijks bestuur van de Tweede Kamer, het wel een goed idee, maar dat zette er bij nader inzien toch een streep door, meldde RTL Nieuws eerder vandaag. Dat gebeurde nadat kleine christelijke partijen op de hoogte waren gebracht van het nieuwe vlaggenplan. Het stuitte op verzet bij de christelijke oppositiepartij SGP. In het presidium zitten alleen grotere partijen, maar het is wel de bedoeling dat er met de mening van kleinere partijen rekening wordt gehouden. Op 24 februari 2024 werd voor het gebouw van de Tweede Kamer de Oekraïense vlag gehesen, twee jaar na de Russische inval. SGP vindt dat er terughoudend omgegaan moet worden met het hijsen van vlaggen anders dan de Nederlandse vlag. "De regenboogvlag betreft geen nationale vlag, maar een vlag van belangenclubs die inmiddels is uitgegroeid tot een symbool van activisme", aluds SGP-Kamerlid Van Dijk. Een aantal oppositiepartijen zoals Pro, Partij voor de Dieren, 50Plus en Volt waren zo verbolgen dat ze een motie indienden om te proberen het besluit terug te draaien. "De Tweede Kamer moet opkomen voor de rechten van de wereldwijde lhbti-beweging", stelden de Kamerleden in de motie. Ze schreven in de motie dat het ook belangrijk is dat er voor de medewerkers van de Tweede Kamer "sprake is van een inclusieve werkomgeving." Over de motie moest donderdagavond laat nog hoofdelijk worden gestemd, op aandringen van de SGP. Dat betekende dat elk Kamerlid apart, dus niet per fractie, zijn of haar standpunt liet weten. Rechtsomkeert Alle Kamerleden moesten opgetrommeld worden voor die hoofdelijke stemming. Dus moesten allerlei Kamerleden, die op donderdag al naar huis waren gegaan, weer rechtsomkeert maken. En dat zorgde voor de nodige irritatie. Een verspilling van duizenden kilometers, zei BBB-Kamerlid Van der Plas die terug was gekomen uit haar woonplaats Deventer. CU-Kamerlid Grinwis noemde de hele gang van zaken "treurig en potsierlijk", maar stemde wel in met de motie. "Om de mensen om wie het gaat."

title: Pentagon wants to livestream Nidal Hasan's execution by firing squad
lead: The US Department of Defense wants to livestream the execution of a man who killed thirteen people in 2009. It would thereby become the first public execution in the US in ninety years. Nidal Hasan was a major and worked in the US army as a psychiatrist. Because he was a soldier and shot people dead on a military base, he is executed by the army. Last Tuesday it was already announced that this would happen with a firing squad. Now the Pentagon also reports that it can be watched live by Americans. 3 December The execution is scheduled for 3 December, but due to appeal proceedings it is questionable whether that date will be met. "We are going to do it on a Thursday, at 13.00, when he committed his act," says Minister of Defense Pete Hegseth: If the execution can indeed be seen via a livestream, that is probably the first time since 1936 that a large public can watch an execution. Almost always an execution in the US can only be seen by a limited group of people such as lawyers, relatives of victims and a small group of media representatives. Approved by Trump The execution of Hasan by firing squad has been approved by president Trump, which is required for military executions. The Pentagon gives no further details about broadcasting the execution and states in response to questions from among others CNN only that "the execution will be livestreamed". It is the first time since 1961 that the US army carries out the death penalty. It also occurs very rarely that in the US a convicted person is executed by firing squad. That happened since 1977 only six times out of 1684 executions. By far most death row inmates received a lethal injection . Hasan opened fire in a building where American soldiers were medically examined on the Texas military base Fort Hood. Thereby the American of Palestinian origin shouted "allahu akbar". The soldiers who were medically examined there would be deployed to Afghanistan. In addition to the thirteen dead, more than thirty people were injured in the attack.

title: French minister comes with emergency plan after protests: 3000 substitute teachers
lead: The French Minister of Education has announced an emergency plan in response to the ongoing protests in France. In the short term he wants to deploy more than 3000 extra teachers. According to minister Geffray, the teachers must go to work at the 514 schools where the teacher shortage is greatest. According to the minister, most of them can start as early as next Tuesday. In addition, Geffray and French prime minister Lecornu announced that money will be made available to hire temporary staff after the autumn holiday, which in France lasts from 17 October to 2 November. 'Little convincing' Whether the measures will calm the protests is questionable. "Édouard Geffray tries to offer reassurances....without really convincing anyone," headlines Le Parisien for example. And Le Monde states that it is mainly a stopgap, with the question being whether shortages will not still arise later in the year. Teachers' union SNES-FSU calls it "a hasty attempt to create the appearance of a political solution, but one that is not sustainable". For further measures the government points to the budget for 2027. Lecornu wants to make a change in it in which he can free up extra budget to further absorb shortages. 71,500 demonstrators Yesterday there were again demonstrations in many places by secondary school pupils. But university students have also joined in. According to the Ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, 71,500 people took to the streets yesterday. The marches and blockades largely proceeded peacefully, but besides the peaceful demonstrations there were also outbreaks of violence in some places. In Strasbourg, for example, a police car was set on fire and in Bordeaux arson was committed at a police station. During the protests yesterday 504 arrests were made and 48 police officers were injured. Quiet in Liège The protests have also spread to Belgium. There, protests have taken place in recent days against planned cuts to education. In Liège, damage was caused during the protests, after which a ban on assembly came into effect yesterday. Because of that and because of tightened checks, yesterday was a quiet day according to Liège police. No damage was caused and it was quiet in the centre. However, 76 people were arrested, probably because they did not comply with the ban on assembly.

title: Terneuzen municipal council agrees to permit for asylum seekers centre
lead: After a debate lasting hours, the municipal council of Terneuzen agreed late yesterday evening to a permit for an asylum seekers centre. The previous council was still opposed to it. That was reason for then mayor <entity id="person:erik-van-merrienboer">Erik van Merrienboer</entity> to step down. The new executive, which was installed in July, amended the proposal to improve social safety. For instance, the focus was placed more on shelter for families. The new proposal was narrowly adopted with support from several opposition parties: there were sixteen votes in favour and fourteen against. Former office building That means the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-orgaan-opvang-asielzoekers">COA</entity> can get to work on realising an asylum seekers centre at the Handelspoort in a former office building. Terneuzen will accommodate a maximum of 200 people. After the vote, the PVV tabled a motion of no confidence against all aldermen. This to the displeasure of mayor Weerwind, who, according to Omroep <entity id="org:provincie-zeeland">Zeeland</entity>, addressed the council sternly: "There are difficult dossiers coming, and even then we must take our responsibility." The motion was rejected with 18 votes against and 12 in favour.

title: Wake-up service 9/10: Announcement of Nobel Peace Prize • Last day of fireworks surrender campaign
lead: Good morning! Today is the last day that you can surrender fireworks anonymously and in Oslo the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize will be announced. First the weather: it will be changeable with the most rain in the west and north of the country. A strong southwesterly wind is blowing with gusts up to 75 km/h in the coastal region. It will be 14 to 18 degrees. Saturday and Sunday will remain changeable, but the sun will also shine. With slightly less wind it will be around 15 degrees in the afternoon. Are you going out today? Here you will find the overview of the traffic jams and roadworks and here everything about the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What have you missed? The US Department of Defense wants to livestream the execution of a man who killed thirteen people in 2009. It is thereby probably the first public execution in the US in ninety years . The execution is scheduled for 3 December and will be carried out by a firing squad. Other news from the night: And then also this: In the building of the European Parliament in Strasbourg a remarkable statue has been unveiled.
