The 2.6-metre-high artwork shows a naked Donald Trump and is called The orange plague. The statue by the Danish artist Jens Galschiøt is covered with gold leaf and intended as a satirical protest against the American president. Galschiøt, who considers Trump a great danger to the international legal order, was inspired by the fairy tale The Emperor's New Clothes . In the well-known story a vain leader thinks he is walking in the most beautiful clothing, but in reality he is naked. The statue is part of a three-day exhibition organised by the Danish party in the European Parliament the Left Group. Have a nice day!

title: Rising French national debt and interest rates increasingly worrying for Europe
lead: Under pressure from the ongoing demonstrations, the French government has promised that there will be 3000 extra teachers. But the pressure on France to tackle its public finances is at least as great. France has, ever since the French revolution of 1789, had a tradition of mass protests that end in violence. And, to name two recent examples, whether it concerns investing in school buildings or reversing pension cuts: meeting the demands of the demonstrators costs the state money. Money that is not there. "The task of making cuts was already very large, but due to the rising interest rates it becomes much more difficult," says Rabobank economist Maartje Wijffelaars. According to a panel of economists appointed by the French government, 126 billion euros must be cut to stabilise the national debt by 2032. "That is going to hurt," says Wijffelaars, "because you cannot spare all households and businesses". Mountain of debt France structurally spends more than it takes in, and also more than is permitted under the EU's stability pact. And so the French national debt is rising. According to the latest European statistics, it amounts to more than 3500 billion euros. France's debt has risen to 119 percent of GDP (the total annual national income). A debt of at most 60 percent is considered desirable in the EU. France has already regularly been reprimanded by the EU because of the high budget deficit and the high national debt. Declining confidence Investors are also looking critically at France. The confidence that the country can repay its debts in the long term is falling. This is evident from the rising interest rate on government debt. Whoever lends money to France for 10 years now receives almost 5 percent interest per year. A year and a half ago that was still 3.5 percent. Investors demand a higher interest rate because they doubt France's creditworthiness. And so the country not only has to deal with a high debt, but the interest rate also takes an increasingly larger bite out of the budget. France correspondent Saskia Houttuin: "While the French debts and interest burdens continue to rise, the <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of prime minister Sébastien Lecornu is in a difficult position. In the coming period he must get the budget for 2027 through parliament. But just as in the Netherlands, the government has no majority. Last year that already proved to be an enormous challenge, but Lecornu got out of it thanks to a deal with the socialists. This year it becomes more difficult; with the presidential elections in prospect, opposition parties will not quickly want to burn themselves on unpopular cuts. Lecornu does have a trump card; he could potentially pilot the budget through outside parliament. But previously the use of that controversial legal article led to a government fall - so it is also a risk." Other countries also have a very high national debt, such as the United Kingdom and the United States. Even the Netherlands and Germany are seeing interest rates rise. But in France the interest rate is rising considerably faster. That interest rate difference, called the 'spread', was still 0.8 percent a year ago. In the meantime it is 1.5 percent. "That may seem little, but it is a point of concern," says ING economist Bert Colijn. Given the size of the national debt, it concerns billions. "If that difference becomes too large, it leads to doubts among investors, banks and other countries about the strength of the entire European Union," Colijn explains. Euro crisis That is reminiscent of 2010, when the Greek debt crisis erupted. Greece's enormous debt led to declining confidence in the euro. After long crisis consultations, the EU provided emergency loans to the country. That ensured that Europe stayed together politically and the euro did not sink further. In recent weeks too, the euro became less valuable relative to the dollar. The question is whether the situation is now just as serious as in 2010. Colijn says that the situation now is nowhere near as pressing as it was then with Greece, but that the consequences if France slides further are potentially greater. "France is a much bigger player than Greece, both politically and economically. If France weakens further financially, that reflects more on all of Europe than Greece did at the time." According to Colijn, the pressure on the European Central Bank to come to the rescue could increase, but it is really up to France first to solve the problems itself.

title: Two inspectors shot dead during weapons check in Germany, 60-year-old man arrested
lead: A routine weapons check in the German state of Bavaria got completely out of hand. Two local inspectors, according to German media a 54-year-old woman and a 45-year-old man, were shot dead by the 60-year-old resident of the house where the check took place. The police have arrested the suspect. This took hours. After the man had killed the officials, he barricaded himself in his home in the village of Berngau. To keep the police out, he had barricaded his home. The police deployed yesterday afternoon around 14:00 with many units and surrounded the house with specialist teams and an armoured vehicle. A police helicopter also flew above the home. Local residents were called on to stay inside. Meanwhile, the police maintained telephone contact with the man. When he continued to refuse to come outside, the arrest units entered the home last night around 03:00. Explosives were used and targeted shots were fired at the suspect. The 60-year-old was slightly injured during his arrest by a bullet in his leg. 'Died immediately' Why the man shot the officials dead is unclear. The local police report that the check concerned a standard procedure in which, for example, it would be examined whether the man's weapons permits were in order and whether his weapons were stored correctly. There was no intention to confiscate the weapons. Initially the police reported that the male inspector had died, and the woman had been seriously injured. Later this was corrected. A police spokesperson says about this: "We assume that she died immediately as a result of the shooting." He does not want to say anything further about the shooter's motive, writes Der Spiegel .

title: ICE shoots man in car in New York, with 5-year-old child in back seat
lead: The US immigration service ICE has shot a man in his car in New York City. According to mayor Mamdani, a 5-year-old child was also in the car. The man was taken to hospital with unknown injuries, the child remained unharmed. The shooting quickly led to protests from local residents and politicians. Mamdani says that ICE agents first surrounded the car and then fired shots. The Department of Homeland Security gives little information about the incident, except that it concerns a man from the Dominican Republic without valid documents. He would also have ties to a gang. Condemnation Mamdani condemns the shooting in fierce terms. In a statement he calls it "an unacceptable and very serious situation". He also says he will call president Trump. "I will then demand that all actions by ICE in our city be halted. I will no longer stand by while ICE agents terrorise our communities." "ICE must disappear from our neighbourhoods," Mamdani's statement continues. "ICE must disappear from our hospitals. ICE must disappear from our streets. ICE must stay away from our children." The mayor concludes with: "Abolish ICE." Other local politicians also expressed their indignation. For instance, the borough president of the Bronx district, where the incident took place, said: "ICE, get lost!" She also encouraged the crowd to resist the immigration service. Demonstrations Shortly after the shooting, demonstrators gathered around the site of the incident. They carried signs with texts such as: "All murdering ICE agents must go to prison" and "Leave our neighbours alone". A large group of people also gathered at the hospital where the victim is being treated. There, a confrontation arose between demonstrators and the police. Since president Trump began his second term in the White House, the immigration services ICE and CBP (Customs and Border Protection) have arrested tens of thousands of people. Dozens of people have also been shot, with at least eleven deaths. Dozens of people arrested by ICE have died in detention centres, where people are held in deplorable conditions.

title: Rotterdam woman (23) was herself behind the wheel during fatal accident on Aruba, says OM
lead: The Rotterdam woman (23) who died last month in a single-vehicle accident on Aruba was herself behind the wheel of the SUV. That is the conclusion of the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> on Aruba based on video footage. The woman's family members said earlier to Rijnmond that they could not imagine that the woman was driving herself. Kimberly van Ardenne was on holiday on the island with her boyfriend. Together with a Dutch marine who lives on the island, they set off on Sunday afternoon 13 September in a UTV, an open off-road vehicle. The off-road vehicle flipped over for a still unknown reason. The two male occupants remained unharmed. The woman died at the scene. The men stated to the local authorities that Kimberly was behind the wheel, but family members in the Netherlands cast doubt on that. "She falls more into the category of scaredy-cats than daredevils," her cousin Stephanie told Rijnmond. The woman reportedly already experienced a lot of tension in the Netherlands when driving in the morning rush hour or parallel parking. 'Public attention' The judiciary on Aruba now says that the account of the two other occupants is correct. The investigation has not yet been completed. But because of the "public attention" the judiciary is already releasing this information now. The family's lawyer, Peter Schouten, says in a statement on X that he finds it "extremely strange" that the judiciary is now coming out with the information about the film clip. "The family also finds it cruel and inhuman that this film clip was not shown to them immediately and that their mourning was therefore unnecessarily disturbed for four weeks by the uncertainty about Kimberly's death," he writes.

title: Americans protest against sexual violence: 'Done with protecting the elite'
lead: In dozens of American cities people have taken to the streets against sexual violence. What began with anger over the rape case at the prestigious Cornell University has grown into something bigger. Demonstrators want accountability and justice, "from the student house to the White House". In Washington, D.C., hundreds of people gathered last night. "How many young women do we silence to protect the future of 'promising young men'?", activist Cheyenne Hunt asks the crowd. "Zero!", is the answer. Jane Doe The demonstrators across the country expressed their support for Jane Doe. That is the name given to the anonymous student who has filed a case because she says she was raped two years ago by students of Cornell. The suspected perpetrators, seven members of a student corps, were not punished or only lightly punished by the university. "I am furious", says Grace Wankelman, one of the organisers of the protest in D.C. "And not only about what happened at Cornell. There are countless stories of perpetrators who get away with sexual violence without justice coming for the victim." "I am also Jane Doe", she adds. At seventeen she was raped by a man she trusted. "When I started crying after I could not get him off me, he said that at least I could pretend I enjoyed it too." Signal to boys "He said those words six months after Trump, who brags about 'grabbing women by the pussy', was elected president. What kind of signal does that give to boys when a rapist holds the most powerful position in the country?" "It shows that they can use women as objects without consequences, because they are promising young men", Wankelman believes. "But what about the promising young women?" Demonstrators speak of a system in which the elite, from 'the Cornell Seven' to Jeffrey Epstein, is protected at the expense of victims. "It is part of a larger pattern of institutions that protect their reputation instead of people", says Epstein victim Dani Benski at the protest. "Powerful men are protected, while victims have to fight to prove what happened to them and to be believed." With the nationwide protests they are asking not only for justice for 'Jane Doe' and Epstein's victims, but also for better protection for victims of sexual violence. Trump recently changed the rules for handling complaints about sexual misconduct at schools and universities, to the dissatisfaction of advocates for the victims. 'Men look away' "Many men choose to look away", believes Kim from Virginia. "To listen to inappropriate jokes and remarks and not speak out against them. That is why it is important that we are all here." A male student at the protest agrees with her. "If we as men do not speak out and support women, we leave intact the system that makes this terrible behaviour possible. That is why we must all take to the streets." From the Washington Monument the demonstrators move to the White House. Shelly Kohl from Tennessee is angry, but also glad to be there. "I realise that I am not alone. There are many victims and by hearing their stories I feel less alone." In front of the White House the group shouts for justice for Jane Doe and for all victims of sexual violence. "Nine years ago I lost the fight with my rapist, but I will not lose this fight", Wankelman promises. "I will not stop fighting until the perpetrators are driven out of positions of power." Podcast De Dag: Jane Doe and the uprising against elite university Cornell Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Enjoying it? Then do not forget to subscribe.

title: Former Prime Minister Schoof: 'US Ukraine policy impossible to follow after Trump took office'
lead: From the moment Donald Trump entered the White House for the second time, US policy on Ukraine was impossible to follow. That is what former Prime Minister Dick Schoof says in the podcast De Atlantische Blik. The plans of the European allies made little progress time and again because the US repeatedly pulled back at the last moment. After President Trump made clear that the US would not support Ukraine unconditionally, a large number of European countries established the coalition of the willing. In order to take a leading role on Ukraine's security. Schoof, who took part in the discussions on behalf of the Netherlands, says that the leaders of the European countries repeatedly took important steps to protect Ukraine at the moment there would be a ceasefire or deal. "But every time that slipped through our fingers", says Schoof. "Because the American negotiators, who had a direct line to the White House, sometimes made a retreating move again just when they had earlier made a forward one." Schoof mentions in particular Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. This pair is constantly deployed by Trump on the international stage. Kushner is Trump's son-in-law, Witkoff is a friend of the president from the real estate world. According to Schoof, the change of guard in Washington had a big impact. "Especially for international relations. Trump and Putin also performed a kind of dance that was very difficult for Europe to follow. It then turned out that European security is simply not the first priority for the US. That lies much more in China." Zelensky also not happy with US Schoof's statements come at a time when Ukrainian President Zelensky also says that the US no longer provides aid in the fight against Russia. According to Zelensky, the Americans cannot at the same time improve economic ties with Russia and mediate in the war. Recently Russia has been increasing the number of attacks on Ukraine. Increasingly, civilians are being killed. According to President Zelensky, more than 130 people were killed in Russian attacks in recent days alone. Zelensky has asked the US to give Ukraine more access to the Starlink satellites. That way the country can better defend itself against Russian ballistic missiles. According to Zelensky, Putin will come to the negotiating table when Ukraine has the upper hand in the air.

title: Peace Prize for South African human rights chief and ICC judge Navi Pillay
lead: This year's Nobel Peace Prize goes to South African judge Navi Pillay. She was a judge at the International Criminal Court (ICC) from 2003 to 2008 and United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights from 2008 to 2014. She is currently active for the International Court of Justice in the case concerning genocide against the Rohingya in Myanmar. According to the Nobel Committee, Pillay shows "enormous courage" by committing herself to the prosecution of perpetrators of war crimes and crimes against humanity. Her work is of great significance for the international legal order, says the jury, which praises her "strong moral compass". Pillay was born into an Indian Tamil family during apartheid in South Africa. She became a lawyer and resisted the "deep-rooted structural discrimination, segregation and exclusion", according to the jury. Early in her career she defended Nelson Mandela and others who spoke out against apartheid. Importance of international law Striking was that the committee devoted much attention to the importance of international law. "In a time of existential challenges including more wars and conflicts than the world has known in a long time, international law is no longer merely a supplement to peace and security. It is an absolute necessity." That system of international law is currently "under enormous pressure", said the jury, "and its institutions are being attacked". "We see a shift towards power politics at the expense of legal frameworks and worldwide respect for law and justice." And that is dangerous, as appears from the words of the jury: "When power takes over from law, that undermines stability, trust and peaceful co-existence." The prize is therefore also a message to those who undermine international law, said the chair of the Nobel Committee: US President Trump recently attacked the ICC. He spoke of "show trials" and said he wants to "dismantle the Court stone by stone". The US has already imposed sanctions on ICC staff and is threatening even further-reaching sanctions. Benefit from migration On 9 June 2016, Pillay received an honorary doctorate from Erasmus University Rotterdam. She then delivered the Mandeville Lecture, in which she spoke out about human rights and the refugee crisis of that year. She noted at the time that xenophobia, rejection, suspicion and aggression were dominant in the public debate. She said it was a misconception that migration would pose a threat. Europe had also greatly benefited from migration in history, she argued. Nominations not known The winner of the Nobel Prize is chosen every year by the Norwegian Nobel Committee. Members of that committee are Norwegian citizens who are selected by the Norwegian parliament for a period of six years. To be eligible for the prize, you must be nominated. According to news agency Reuters, US President Trump was nominated by Cambodia, Israel and Pakistan. Who else had a chance at the Peace Prize was not clear in advance. The full list of names is only made public after fifty years.

title: Dutch Dachau Committee knew that camp stories of 99-year-old did not add up
lead: The Dutch Dachau Committee has known since 2024 about the untruths regarding the wartime past of Willem Wilbrink and has tried to prevent him from spreading them further. That is what chairman <entity id="person:wimar-jaeger">Wimar Jaeger</entity> of the foundation says to the NOS. The 99-year-old Wilbrink was regularly present at Second World War commemorations and at schools to talk about his wartime past and his time in Dachau concentration camp. But from a publication this week in the Historisch Nieuwsblad it appears that it is highly unlikely that he was imprisoned there. The publication also reveals that other claims he made are probably not true. By his own account, Wilbrink was arrested as a 15-year-old because of resistance work and taken to the concentration camp near Munich. There he would have been put to work as a corpse carrier. In that capacity he says he saved forty people from death. He did this, he claimed, by taking people who were said to be dead and had to go to the crematorium but turned out to still be alive to the sick bay. No evidence According to researchers there is no evidence for these statements. For instance, there is no documentation about his imprisonment in Dachau and no camp number of his is known, while precisely in this concentration camp, where more than 43,000 people died, everything was recorded meticulously. Wilbrink also wears decorations of which it is unknown how he obtained them. For example, Wilbrink claimed that he had been given a Polish hero title, but from research by RTL Nieuws it appears that his name does not appear in the country's archives, and that the title mentioned by Wilbrink does not exist. Furthermore, Wilbrink told stories that other Dachau survivors had no memory of and that according to researchers also did not take place. Wilbrink also does not appear in the stories of and about well-known people who were imprisoned in Dachau, such as those of priest and war hero Titus Brandsma , who was murdered there in 1942. Organisations informed about untruths Jaeger says that the National Dachau Committee discovered that Wilbrink's stories did not add up after the publication of his biography. The organisation found that book remarkable because it did not know Wilbrink's story. The Committee therefore conducted research and spoke with historians, after which the conclusion was drawn that Wilbrink's past in Dachau was made up. "We subsequently tried to stop the distribution of the book and informed commemoration committees that Wilbrink's story is not true," says Jaeger. The National Dachau Committee did not actively publicise the news about Wilbrink because "we know better than anyone what a war trauma can do to the stories in your head", says chairman Jaeger. "We are convinced that Wilbrink thinks he experienced this." Jaeger states that the organisation has empathy and wants to show understanding for people with a war trauma, but also that it is important that the stories about the Second World War and Dachau are based on truth. That is why the committee now cannot do otherwise than make clear what the reality is, he says. "Otherwise the lessons we learned there are of no use to us." Although the Dachau committee already knew about the untruths in 2024, Wilbrink was still at the National Commemoration of the Capitulations of 1945 in Wageningen in 2025. <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">Minister Karremans</entity> wrote on LinkedIn at the time that he "had the honour of sitting next to Wilbrink". The organisation of the Wageningen commemoration did not know about the untruths in the story of the 99-year-old, says a spokesperson. He says that Wageningen45 had not been informed about it by the Dutch Dachau Committee. According to him, the organisation bases the recognition of veterans and their stories on expert bodies. "Wageningen45 has taken note of the article in Historisch Nieuwsblad and takes this very seriously," he says to the NOS. For the organisation, "it is paramount that the stories we tell and the changemakers we honour are reliable and authentic", the spokesperson says. "So that we can keep the stories of veterans alive with great care and respect for a broad audience." Newsletter Second World War Interested in the Second World War? Then subscribe here to our newsletter.

title: A2 in Limburg closed all weekend, significant delays already this morning
lead: The A2 in Limburg will be completely closed in both directions this weekend. Last night the section between St. Joost and Roosteren was already closed. That was already clearly noticeable during the morning rush hour: motorists faced significant delays. Tonight at 21.00 the A2 will close between the Het Vonderen interchange (Echt) and the Kerensheide interchange (Urmond) due to works. The A2 is being widened: an extra lane will be added in both directions. The total works will take years. This weekend <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> is keeping a liveblog about the so-called WeekendBreek . During such a full closure, work can continue day and night for a whole weekend. This weekend, among other things, two wildlife crossings will be constructed. Less traffic The first night of the works went smoothly despite the rain, Rijkswaterstaat told L1 Nieuws . The motorway runs through the narrowest part of the Netherlands and there are no good alternative routes. Today traffic is being diverted from the St. Joost exit via Echt along the N276. Rijkswaterstaat is calling on people not to take to the road if it is not necessary. "There was somewhat less traffic heading north compared with other Fridays," said Rijkswaterstaat. Hundreds of people are working day and night on the A2 this weekend. It is the second weekend closure in a series of seven weekend closures in the coming five years. The closure lasts until Monday morning 05.00.

title: Thousands of Spaniards take to the streets to commemorate Maricarmen Abascal: 'This is murder'
lead: In Madrid, some twenty thousand people took to the streets last night to commemorate Maricarmen Abascal, who died on Wednesday. The 87-year-old woman became the face of large-scale housing protests after she was evicted from the apartment where she had lived her entire adult life by a real estate investor. The cause of the woman's death has not been made public, but since she was carried out of her home on a stretcher on 23 September, she had been in hospital with fear, stress and exhaustion. With many candles, flowers and cards with loving messages, the thousands of demonstrators marched last night from the Puerta del Sol, the central square of the Spanish capital, to her home, in the prestigious Retiro district. Anger towards real estate company Candles were lit and drawings and letters were laid at the apartment complex, creating an improvised altar. The demonstrators expressed their anger at the investment company that bought the residential building in 2020 and raised the woman's rent from 500 to more than 1600 euros per month. With her pension of 1400 euros, the woman could not pay this. The real estate manager then tried for years to get Abascal out of her home, but through various legal procedures she managed to prevent this. Until the end of September. The demonstrators chanted: "This is not a death, this is murder." One woman said: "This is about dignity." And: "Enough is enough. We cannot go on like this." A young man added: "Maricarmen's situation is not unique. She symbolises everything we are fighting for: a dignified existence now and in the future." The fact that after Abascal's eviction the real estate party succumbed to massive public opinion and the woman was allowed to return to her home after all, at a reduced rent, did not make the demonstrators any milder. Just a few hours before she was to sign her new rental agreement, she died in the Gregorio Marañón hospital in Madrid. 'Maricarmen lives on' "Drive these vultures out of our neighbourhoods", was chanted. A spokesperson for a tenants' union became emotional while reading a tribute to the woman: "The fight continues, Maricarmen lives on", she said. A minute of silence followed for the woman who became an icon in the fight against speculation and high housing prices in Spain. Many Spaniards cannot afford housing due to inflation and a shortage of homes. Especially Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia have too little housing. Because of the social unrest, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called early elections on Monday for 29 November.

title: Former OpenAI employees speak out about their dismissal and warn the company
lead: Three dismissed employees of OpenAI warn the company in an open letter about a culture of fear. The three-page letter was published by them on social media. Last week the American company dismissed the three safety employees. According to OpenAI, they would have shared company information with external parties. In the letter, the dismissed employees deny this. They think they were dismissed because they had expressed their criticism and concerns internally about the safety of the AI models. The dismissal subsequently set off a rumor mill, causing people who still work at OpenAI to no longer dare to express criticism. "If OpenAI employees no longer feel free to flag internal safety concerns, then we all run the risk that something truly catastrophic goes wrong," they write in the letter. They also call on OpenAI to work with an external supervisor. Response OpenAI A spokesperson for the company said in response to the open letter to the newspaper The Wallstreet Journal that the employees were not dismissed because they had criticized the company's safety measures. OpenAI also says it is grateful for the contributions the three former employees made. OpenAI has been much in the news recently because the company lost control over its own AI models. In three months' time, OpenAI had to halt work twice. The first time was in July when 1200 agents managed to break into the AI company Hugging Face.

title: Riots during major strike against cuts in Brussels
lead: In Brussels, a strike by trade unions has led to unrest. There are riots near the Brussels-Central railway station. Streets are blocked and the police are being pelted with fireworks, stones and bottles. The police respond with tear gas. A water cannon has also been deployed. The demonstrators are protesting against the national government's policy of cutting social security. At this moment the government is deliberating on the budget. The protesters fear that wages, public services and pensions will also be cut. According to the trade unions, the strongest shoulders must bear the heaviest burdens. Black clothing According to Belgian media, hundreds of young people dressed in black with masks are causing the unrest. They are said to have mingled among the demonstrators. Several people have been arrested, it is unclear how many. According to the VRT, the trade unions' demonstration in other parts of Brussels is proceeding calmly. Thousands of people are walking in a march through the city. Because of the strike, a large part of public transport in Brussels is at a standstill. There is also disruption at the airport. View images of the unrest here:

title: France warned about non-visible military aircraft near Curaçao
lead: France warned during the American attack on Venezuela on 3 January about military aircraft that were not visible to civil air traffic control in the Caribbean. Because they were not visible, controllers could not always inform other aircraft about the presence of military aircraft. This is evident from documents that the Dutch <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> released after an appeal under the Open Government Act (Woo). NOS reported on 14 December about a near-collision between a passenger aircraft and an American military tanker aircraft above Curaçao, in which the military aircraft was not visible on radar. The danger of military aircraft that are not visible to civil air traffic control is that controllers cannot warn other aircraft in time. Without information about the position of those aircraft, they also cannot ensure sufficient mutual distance. Pilots of passenger aircraft can therefore unexpectedly encounter a military aircraft and may then have to intervene themselves to prevent a collision. That risk also played a role in the near-collision that NOS reported on in December. The French warning makes clear that during the American attack on Venezuela, military aircraft that remained outside the view of civil controllers were again taken into account. Listen here to part of the conversation between air traffic control and the pilots during the near-collision: The French warning concerned the flight information regions of Curaçao, San Juan and Piarco. Pilots were also advised to carry extra fuel within operational possibilities so that they could divert if necessary. The documents do not show that such aircraft actually flew in the Curaçao flight information region on 3 January. Emergency consultation after near-collision The incidents that NOS reported on first led to emergency consultation between airlines, the American aviation authority FAA, the Curaçao air traffic control and international aviation organizations. KLM subsequently tightened its safety measures for flights through Curaçao airspace. Aircraft had to carry extra lighting throughout the flight through that area from then on. On 18 December, the governments of Curaçao and Aruba reported that agreements had been made with the United States about the activation of transponders by American military aircraft. American flight ban More than two weeks later followed the American attacks on Venezuela, in which president Maduro and his wife were captured and transferred to the United States. The FAA issued a flight ban on 3 January for American civil aviation operators in the Curaçao Flight Information Region (FIR). That applied at all flight altitudes because of safety risks due to military activities. American military and state aircraft were exempted from the ban. The Curaçao FIR covers a large part of the southern Caribbean and borders the Venezuelan flight information region Maiquetía. Air traffic services are provided by the Curaçao air traffic control. The American ban applied to American aviation operators and did not mean that the airspace was closed to all aircraft. Other airlines had to assess for themselves whether they could carry out their flights safely. View here our special about the near-collision: KLM cancelled flights to the ABC islands, Sint Maarten and various other Caribbean destinations on 3 January. TUI and Corendon also scrapped flights. According to Buitenlandse Zaken, approximately 2600 KLM passengers were affected by the cancellations. The Curaçao <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> stated at the time that the airspace was not completely closed, but that there was increased readiness. Airlines had to assess for themselves whether they could fly. On 4 January the American restrictions were lifted and airlines resumed their flights to the islands. Crisis consultation in The Hague The Dutch government held crisis consultation on 3 January about the American attacks and the consequences for the region. The ministries of Buitenlandse Zaken, <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity>, <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, <entity id="org:ministerie-van-infrastructuur-en-waterstaat">Infrastructuur en Waterstaat</entity> and <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> were involved, among others. Representatives of KLM, TUI fly and Corendon also received information about the security situation. On 4 January it was announced that a steering group Caribbean region under the chairmanship of Binnenlandse Zaken would meet. Defensie and Buitenlandse Zaken would share information there. The released documents do not show when the Curaçao aviation authorities were informed about the international security warnings or what agreements were made with the United States about military flight movements during the attack. Crisis phase scaled down On 6 January the Dutch crisis consultation met again. The consultation decided to reduce the crisis approach back to the pre-crisis phase. A next consultation was planned for 13 January, unless the situation gave reason to meet earlier. The scenario analyses on which the decision-making was partly based are largely redacted. The disclosed documents do not state what information the Curaçao air traffic control had during the American attack about military flight movements. It also does not become clear whether the agreements that Curaçao and Aruba announced in December with the United States about the use of transponders during the operation were still in force and were complied with.

title: Rotterdam files report against employees for fraud around childcare benefits scandal
lead: The municipality of Rotterdam suspects that several employees committed fraud with money intended for victims of the childcare benefits scandal. The municipality has filed a report against two people, writes regional broadcaster Rijnmond . Five others have been suspended. The municipality is conducting further investigation into them. The employees helped victims of the childcare benefits scandal, for example with the purchase of new furniture or equipment at the municipality's expense. They had access to a municipal payment card for this. The victims received help from the municipality because they had got into financial difficulties after the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> had wrongly accused them of fraud with the childcare benefit. Expenses for themselves The municipality of Rotterdam believes that at least two civil servants also bought things for themselves or others. This concerns expenses where it is not clear what the money was spent on and expenses where it is not clear why they were made. "As far as we know, the victims simply received their things. They were not left short, but that does not take away from the fact that it is fraud", alderman Diederik van Dommelen (VVD) tells Rijnmond. The possible fraud was discovered more than a year ago after a report about one of the employees. Hundred people Van Dommelen does not yet know how much money is involved. That is currently being investigated. "What happened is really unacceptable. I want to know what happened and how much went wrong." Around a hundred people had access to the municipality's credit card. The alderman considers it justifiable that so many people had the freedom to make purchases for the victims. "Let's not forget: we did this to help the victims and then you need speed, because those people need help", he says. "Speed and carefulness can sometimes clash." To prevent fraud, the spending limits have now been adjusted. "We have also reduced the number of people who can use the credit card", says alderman Van Dommelen. Fingers in the sugar bowl "We cannot prevent people from putting their fingers in the sugar bowl. But we must be able to discover it as quickly as possible", says the alderman. "The checks must therefore be faster. At the same time, we want to be able to help the victims quickly. It will always be a search for balance."

title: Paintings by Renoir found a month after theft from French museum
lead: Two paintings by Renoir that were stolen from a museum in the south of France last month have been found. The police do not want to say where they were found or whether they are damaged. The works in question are Madame Colonna Romano and Jeune Femme au puits, which were stolen. On 8 September, four paintings by the famous French impressionist Pierre-Auguste Renoir were stolen from the Musée Renoir in Cagnes-sur-Mer. The value of the four works is estimated at 9 million euros. Within three minutes the thieves managed to get in, take the canvases and leave unseen. During their flight outside, two thieves left two paintings behind in the museum garden. Six arrests On Wednesday, six suspects were arrested, including the two suspected burglars. The six are suspected, among other things, of theft in an organised context. The paintings are normally on display in the Musée d'Orsay in Paris, but were on loan. The four pieces were the most valuable works of the Musée Renoir. The museum is located in the painter's last home.

title: Recreational anglers also deployed to get rid of harmful crayfish
lead: Recreational anglers, sport fishing associations, contractors and muskrat control workers may also in the future catch invasive American crayfish on a larger scale. Currently the water boards do this, but they have too few people to reduce the harmful crayfish population. So a new scheme for fishing for non-native crayfish is coming, <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">staatssecretaris Erkens</entity> informed <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> today. Burrows and holes In Dutch ditches, canals, lakes and ponds there are estimated to be tens of millions of crayfish that cause great damage to water quality and biodiversity. They cut water plants to pieces with their claws, they eat water insects and eggs of amphibians and fish. They also dig burrows and holes and thereby make banks and dikes less stable. The non-native crayfish reproduce quickly and it is already no longer possible to get rid of the animals entirely. But the ministry does want to do more about the so-called 'catching' of the animals. Umbrella trap So from now on other catching equipment may be used, such as the trench trap and the umbrella trap. Currently the water boards mainly work with fykes and kubben, but the disadvantage is that many other fish and water animals are also caught with them. They are then released, but are often injured or have already died from the catch. The hiring of other fishermen, such as sport fishermen, members of fishing associations, contractors and muskrat control workers is also new. Until now they were only allowed to catch crayfish on a small scale, namely with a fishing rod. Under the new rules, more will therefore be allowed, but that does not mean that everyone may always catch crayfish. A water board can locally issue "an assignment", says staatssecretaris Erkens (Fisheries), and recreational anglers, for example, can then get to work on it. Crayfish cuisine Erkens speaks of "an important step" to get the plague under control. He does point out that the animals, once caught, should not be released elsewhere. "They must be destroyed or consumed." The staatssecretaris himself has eaten crayfish before, he says when asked. "I thought they were quite tasty," says Erkens. "Who knows, a very beautiful Dutch crayfish cuisine may be at the beginning of its emergence." Ruben Ariaans is a professional crayfish fisherman. He is not necessarily keen on recreational anglers also hunting the animal:

title: Twenty asylum seekers slept in the rain in Ter Apel: 'Fallen below the humane lower limit'
lead: In Ter Apel, twenty people who want to apply for asylum slept outside on the grass in the rain last night. According to the aid organisations Vluchtelingenwerk Nederland and the Red Cross, this is a direct consequence of the shortage of shelter places in the Netherlands. According to the aid organisations, the Netherlands is falling below a "humane lower limit". At the registration centre in Ter Apel there is a building with a day shelter. There is room to offer a roof over the heads of a maximum of 150 people. People who want to apply for asylum can go there if there is no place at the registration centre. "By now we have people who have been in that shelter for ten days, people cannot wash themselves there," a spokesperson for the Red Cross told the NOS. That limit of 150 people has been reached several times in recent weeks, the aid organisations say. According to them, they have to make "impossible choices to keep the situation safe and manageable". That is why only the 150 people from the day shelter can go to the emergency night shelter. According to the Red Cross, there have been earlier incidents in the night shelter, such as theft. "For safety, we now have to say: we will only help the people we know from the day shelter in the night shelter. That is why people are sleeping on the front grounds," the spokesperson says. Spreidingswet The aid organisations call on municipalities in the Netherlands to arrange emergency shelter immediately. "It is the responsibility of the government and we do what we can to help," the spokesperson for the Red Cross says. What is the spreidingswet? The spreidingswet must ensure since 2024 that the shelter of asylum seekers is distributed more fairly across the Netherlands. The Netherlands has a structural shortage of shelter places for the number of people who come here and apply for asylum. That shortage plays a role at the registration centre in Ter Apel and at (emergency) shelter places throughout the country. After registering in Ter Apel, someone awaiting the asylum process should move on to a shelter location elsewhere in the country. That often does not happen, because those shelter locations are full. Places there are largely occupied by status holders; people who have applied for asylum and are allowed to stay. They have difficulty moving on to a home because of the problems in the housing market. The number of pending asylum applications and the duration of the asylum process have also been rising for years. People who want to apply for asylum therefore remain dependent on asylum shelter for longer than before, which leads to fuller asylum seekers' centres. According to the <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">IND</entity> (the Immigration and Naturalisation Service), the number of people coming to the Netherlands is higher than the number of applications that the IND says it can process annually. From earlier research by the NOS it appears that most municipalities say they are willing to cooperate with the spreidingswet. Yet the aid organisations state that about two thirds of municipalities in practice do too little. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> placed 24 of the 342 municipalities under supervision this summer, because they arrange too few shelter locations. Minister Van den Brink of Asylum, who is responsible for shelter, calls the situation in Ter Apel "unworthy of the Netherlands". The minister says that in the short term he will look for shelter locations with municipalities. "Sometimes you have to keep persisting with what you are already doing." Since this summer there has also been temporary extra emergency shelter in Ter Apel. Nieuwsuur went to look:

title: Dave De K. shares new details about the abuse and death of toddler Dean
lead: Dave De K., the man suspected of killing the Belgian toddler Dean, has shared new details in court about the violent death of the child. That writes Omroep Zeeland . Four years ago, the 4-year-old Dean was found dead near the work island Neeltje Jans in Zeeland. De K. (39) told during the second hearing day in the court in Ghent that he had an outburst of rage in the car and hit Dean several times with his fist. "I vented my anger and Dean unfortunately became a victim of that", the man said. He was, according to himself, not angry at the child, but frustrated about his relationship and his life. Dean's mother was at that moment voluntarily admitted to the psychiatric ward of the hospital in Sint-Niklaas, near Antwerp. Dave De K. and his girlfriend Romy W. were said to have cared for Dean together during her stay. De K. is suspected of kidnapping and manslaughter of the Belgian toddler, his girlfriend of complicity in the kidnapping. Collapsed The little boy lived for a few more hours after the serious abuse. De K. changed Dean's clothes in the apartment of him and his then girlfriend Romy. He then got into the car with the child to his drug dealer in Koudekerke. The suspect told today that Dean was largely conscious but kept fading away. The toddler was said to have said that he needed to pee. The man helped the child out of the car on a hard shoulder. There Dean collapsed and died on the spot. De K. then drove around Zeeland for another day with the child on the back seat. He had laid a blanket over him. Eventually De K. left the body at Neeltje Jans. Jury The trial against Dave De K. began yesterday and is expected to last eight days. A people's jury of twelve members will, together with judges, consider the question of guilt. In 2010 De K. already received a prison sentence of ten years for the fatal abuse of his 2-year-old stepson. He served that sentence.

title: Cabinet apologises to Q fever patients: 'Sent from pillar to post'
lead: Twenty years after the start of the largest Q fever epidemic in history, healthcare minister Hermans apologises on behalf of the cabinet. Tens of thousands of people in <entity id="org:provincie-noord-brabant">Noord-Brabant</entity> became infected through contaminated goat farms in the area. Various investigative committees, ombudsmen and doctors have since established that the government fell short in protecting the people in that region. The minister does not apologise for what happened during the epidemic. She does apologise on behalf of the cabinet that there was no good social safety net for the people who became long-term ill. "If you are not believed, have to tell your story again and again and are sent from pillar to post, then that is terrible. And I apologise for that," said Hermans in the presence of hundreds of patients during a meeting in the provincial government building of Den Bosch. Chronically ill Two thousand people are chronically ill to this day, have mostly lost their jobs and live a life on the margins of society. There was already hope that the minister would apologise. Her ministry had instructed independent experts to evaluate the policy and actions regarding the Q fever patients. The researchers see the minister's apology as "essential", according to the report . It is an echo of the recommendations from three earlier reports by the <entity id="org:nationale-ombudsman">Nationale Ombudsman</entity> from 2012, 2017 and 2024. Time and again, successive ministers refused to apologise. Other important recommendations were also ignored, such as investing in medical science and setting up an expertise centre for the treatment of the chronically ill. Also, the long-term version of Q fever, Q fever fatigue syndrome, is still often not recognised by the <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity>. As a result, patients cannot count on disability benefits. The loss of income has in turn led to other suffering. 'Trust in government damaged' Also, how well social support is arranged differs from municipality to municipality. Patients often experience little understanding and are sent from pillar to post for help. "This has damaged trust in the government as a whole," the researchers write. They strongly advise the minister to take the initiative herself to improve the help from and cooperation between various municipalities, support services and organisations such as the UWV. The new report also emphasises the recommendation to "invest heavily" in an expertise centre, medical knowledge and long-term research. The researchers see that medical indifference towards the patients "has reduced trust in the medical world and in the government." Q fever fatigue syndrome Q fever fatigue syndrome fits in the list of other post-acute infectious diseases (PAIS) such as long covid, ME, Lyme and post-sepsis syndrome. Medical knowledge about these conditions is still in its infancy. Curative treatments do not yet exist and the few treatments that can lead to relief still have an insufficient scientific basis. The result is that there is virtually no reimbursed care in regular healthcare. In recent years, tens of millions of euros have been invested in research into long covid and ME. But most findings are not yet concrete enough for the practice of regular healthcare. More time needed for medical science Nevertheless, it is the intended policy of <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">minister Hermans</entity> to soon not make large follow-up funding available for research. In addition, funding for the existing long covid expertise centres will be stopped in the short term. The cabinet's idea is that general practitioners and other care providers can take on the care for PAIS patients. The researchers oppose this intention and write that medical science must be given more time and space so that diagnoses and treatments with a scientific basis also become possible, so that they can also be reimbursed. "Until then, in the opinion of the review team, embedding in regular healthcare is not yet appropriate." The <entity id="org:gezondheidsraad">Gezondheidsraad</entity> gave a similar warning earlier this year in an advisory report : "The estimated large numbers of people with long covid and other PAIS cannot simply be absorbed into regular healthcare." One-off 2.5 million euros During the meeting in which minister Hermans apologised, patients from the audience asked whether tens of millions of euros will be invested in scientific research into PAIS. For the time being that will not happen, according to the minister. However, a one-off 2.5 million euros will be made available in 2027 to improve the quality of life of Q fever patients. Proposals for spending this budget have been drawn up in consultation with the Q fever ambassador, patient organisation Q-uestion and Q-support. The funds will be spent to help Q fever patients who have become stuck, for example at the UWV, but also in healthcare. Not all Q fever patients can be helped with this budget, but the minister hopes that the lessons learned from this approach can lead to a better standard of support for all PAIS patients.

title: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles of wine from famous Italian winery
lead: The prominent Italian winery Marchesi Antinori has become the victim of perhaps the largest wine theft in Italy's history. On Saturday, seven masked men broke into the distribution centre in Tuscany and then loaded two trucks full with around 30,000 bottles of red wine. The estimated value: 5 million euros. The wine was intended for customers outside Italy and was ready to be transported. The Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera writes that the gang acted well prepared and professionally. Security cameras were disabled, as was the alarm system. Once the trucks were parked in the warehouse, the men used the winery's forklifts to calmly move all the wine. Thieves with knowledge The thieves did not just do anything. According to Albiera Antinori, the chair of the board of directors of the family business, the thieves had their wine knowledge in order: all the stolen wines come from 2023, which was an exceptionally good wine year. and especially for the Solaia, one of the most iconic and exclusive wines in the world. Only around 60,000 to 70,000 bottles of the Solaia are produced annually. The thieves took 10,000 of them. The price of a bottle of Solaia can quickly rise to around 500 euros. The shock within the company is therefore great, Antinori tells the Corriere della Sera. "It may well have been the best wine of the past twenty years." Renzo Cotarella, the general director of the winery, cannot imagine that the burglars were small fry: "It is absolutely a highly trained gang." According to him, a theft of this scale and value has never happened before in Italy. "The people at the winery were crying," he tells the Financial Times . Although the theft was only discovered on Monday morning and no arrests have yet been made, Cotarella still hopes the wine will be traced quickly. "Two trucks don't just disappear. The roads in Tuscany are full of cameras; maybe with a bit of luck we will find part of the stolen bottles back." Not an incident The winery has meanwhile begun informing its customers. The company exports to 170 countries, says Antinori. "We want to warn them to be on their guard against offers outside the official channels." According to the winery, the theft is not covered by insurance. Italian media write that there is a good chance the gang operated on behalf of others. Which organisation might be behind this is unclear, but Italian wineries have long been plagued by burglaries. Last month, for example, around 3000 bottles were stolen from the Conterno Fantino winery with a combined value between 300,000 and 400,000 euros.

title: US announces sanctions against International Criminal Court in The Hague, wants to 'paralyse' court
lead: The American government has announced sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague. They are largely to take effect in April next year. "President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans," says Minister Rubio of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> in a video message on X . "That is why the US is imposing sanctions on the ICC. We will prohibit transactions with this out-of-control court, cut them off from resources and paralyse their ability to function." Microsoft Earlier, the American government already imposed sanctions on individual prosecutors and judges. For example, an affected jurist of the court would no longer have access to Microsoft, and financial services via American companies were cut off. Now the US is expanding the package of measures and threatens to cut off the entire court from such services. "We don't need the Criminal Court," says Rubio. "Americans do not fall under the jurisdiction of this 'fake ICC'." The American government believes that the court has no authority to prosecute American citizens or citizens of American allies. 'Not stop' Acting prosecutor of the ICC, Nazhat Shameem Khan, says in a response that the American sanctions against the Criminal Court must be condemned and promises that they will not prevent the work of the tribunal. "The sanctions are intended to undermine the international legal order and the work of an independent judicial institution. Our work will continue in all our cases, in our investigations and in our prosecutions." US does not recognise Criminal Court The ICC, based in The Hague, is an international court founded in 2002. It can prosecute people suspected of genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes. The United States, like Russia, China, India, Israel and Iran, is not a member of the ICC and does not recognise it either. These sanctions do not come unexpectedly. Trump has a far-reaching dislike of the ICC, sanctions against the Criminal Court had been in the air for some time. In his speech during the UN annual meeting, he called on all member states of the ICC to leave it. The direct reason for the sanctions is the arrest warrant against Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu. Israel is an ally of the US. American personnel were also investigated for involvement in war crimes in Afghanistan. Support for the ICC was also limited under Democratic presidents. When the International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants in 2024 against Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Gallant, Biden called that "shameful". Nobel Peace Prize Today, not entirely coincidentally, ICC President Tomoko Akane had coffee with <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> at Huis ten Bosch. What was discussed there has not been made public. And today of all days, a former judge of the ICC, Navi Pillay, also received the Nobel Peace Prize. The system of international law is currently "under enormous pressure", the jury said about the appointment, "and its institutions are being attacked".

title: Olympic Stadium unscathed after fire in garage, offices affected
lead: The Olympic Stadium in Amsterdam suffered little damage from the fire that broke out last night in the crawl space of the parking garage. However, some offices in the building are temporarily unusable. For example, the head office of Topsport Amsterdam must remain closed for the next five months. The organization, which supports Olympic and national top athletes, announced this in a statement. The full extent of the damage has not yet been mapped out. The fire in the national monument released a lot of smoke, which caused odor nuisance in the area. The fire was only under control at the beginning of the night. The stadium, including the business premises in the building, was evacuated. The stadium houses more than thirty companies. The monument appears to have suffered no significant damage. The cause of the fire is still under investigation. Marathon All cars that were in the parking garage also remained undamaged. This morning the garage reopened and owners could pick up their cars. The TCS Amsterdam Marathon, which takes place next Sunday, can for now go ahead. The sports event starts and finishes every year in the Olympic Stadium. Geert Wit of organizer Le Champion tells NH Nieuws that minor adjustments may be needed. "We are in close contact with the parties involved and are monitoring the situation closely. Preparations are continuing as planned. The safety of our participants, visitors and employees is of course paramount," says Wit.

title: Bicycle brands Batavus, KOGA and Babboe continue to exist, sold to Dutech
lead: The bicycle brands Batavus, KOGA and Babboe are making a restart. That is reported by the curators of the Dutch bicycle manufacturer Accell. The brands have been sold to the Singaporean investor Dutech. The bicycle manufacturer's IT platform and Accell Group's Hungarian activities have also been sold. Accell was declared bankrupt in August. The company employed nearly 2000 people spread across fifteen countries, with its headquarters in Amsterdam. Possibly part of the staff can continue under the new owner. The IT platform will transfer to Dutech at a later time. For the time being the platform remains available for the further settlement of the bankruptcy. Talks are still ongoing about the sale of the remaining parts. The curators expect to be able to say more about that at a later time.

title: Podcast De Stemming: Waving cyclists, water pistols and the Jetteritus
lead: There was old-fashioned poldering again this week, because at the Catshuis the trade unions, employers' organisations and <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> consulted about the future of social security. But whether they actually made progress is the question. In addition, <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> debated the budget of the kabinet-Jetten. And there too it proves difficult for the prime minister to get a broad majority enthusiastic. And there is again disagreement in the coalition about box 3. The VVD and the CDA are not on the same wavelength about the 'paper gift tax'. What does that do to the relations within the coalition? Podcast De Stemming This episode of De Stemming by Vullings and De Rooy can be listened to at <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister There you will also find all previous episodes . Just like at all other well-known podcast channels . About this podcast Political journalists Joost Vullings ( EenVandaag , AVROTROS) and Marleen de Rooy (NOS) review the Hague week every Friday, with sharp analyses, rumours and predictions. Do you want to respond? Then email destemming@nos.nl.

title: Netherlands returns twenty stolen objects to Indonesia
lead: The Netherlands is returning twenty objects to Indonesia. These are cultural objects that were looted in colonial times, or obtained under duress and brought to our country. Among the objects being returned are the diamond of Banjarmasin, a handwritten Quran and several gravestones. Eighteen objects were until now in the possession of the Wereldmuseum, two were from the Rijksmuseum. "We are actually always pleased with a restitution," says Marieke van Bommel, director of the Wereldmuseum. "We believe that if objects have come into our collection improperly, it is also entirely right that they go back to the country of origin." The handwritten Quran from Aceh: "Of some objects you know that they come from a particular war," says director Van Bommel. "Then you actually already have a suspicion that they were acquired in colonial times." According to the director of the Wereldmuseum, there were often unequal power relations and violence involved. "Sometimes we know it for certain and some things we investigate extra after a request." With the return, <entity id="person:rianne-letschert">minister Letschert</entity> of Culture is following the advice of the Commissie Koloniale Collectie. It investigated the provenance and concluded that with these twenty objects there was "involuntary loss of possession". "These objects have great cultural and historical value for Indonesia," says Letschert. "They should never have been in the Netherlands. This injustice we are now righting." Still to be packed first The objects will remain in the Netherlands for the coming months. "Today is the legal transfer," says director Van Bommel. Minister Letschert and her Indonesian counterpart will sign an agreement in Amsterdam today. "In the coming months the objects will be packed and all the papers put in order for transport to Indonesia," says Van Bommel.

title: Disappointment about 'camp lies' of 99-year-old: 'The truth is bad enough already'
lead: "It is important that the stories that are told and the people we honour are reliable and authentic", says the Nationaal Comité Herdenking Capitulaties about the news that claims by the 99-year-old Willem Wilbrink, who until now was regarded as a war hero, are not true. From among other things a publication in the Historisch Nieuwsblad it emerged this week that Wilbrink, among other things, was not in the concentration camp in Dachau . The NIOD Instituut voor Oorlogs-, Holocaust- en Genocidestudies also says that his name does not appear on the list of Dutch people who were imprisoned there. NIOD researcher Kees Ribbens says in a response that this kind of story undermines the truth about the Second World War. Malicious people can seize on it to sow doubt about what happened in the Holocaust. 'He really believes it' Although the Nederlands Dachau Comité has known about the untruths since 2024, it is only now coming forward. Chairman <entity id="person:wimar-jaeger">Wimar Jaeger</entity> does so "because it is important that the stories about the Second World War and Dachau are based on truth", he says. Jaeger says he has understanding for the 99-year-old, and Jaeger is convinced that Wilbrink thinks he experienced this. "We know better than anyone what a war trauma can do to the stories in your head." Carolien Brugsma, journalist and daughter of Dachau survivor Willem Brugsma, likewise assumes that Wilbrink has a war trauma. She too thinks that he really believes that he was in the concentration camp. She herself was interviewed last year for Andere Tijden about the concentration camp and her father's time there. Her father was a resistance man and was arrested in Paris. He was imprisoned in three camps before he ended up in Dachau. Unlike camps such as Auschwitz, which were set up for the destruction of Jews, Dachau was mainly intended for heavy forced labour. It held mainly resistance people and political opponents of the Nazis, such as priest and war hero Titus Brandsma . Checking claims At first Brugsma thought on hearing the news: "How sad for him and his children", she says. "But now I am starting to get angry. Not at him, but at the person who wrote his biography." As far as she is concerned, that person should have verified Wilbrink's claims. She herself also did that with her father's war past when she went to Dachau for Andere Tijden. Although she was certain that her father had been there, she checked once more whether she remembered his camp number correctly. Brugsma finds it especially reprehensible that in times when knowledge about the Holocaust is declining , untruths such as Wilbrink's are spread. Precisely now, the stories that are told about the Second World War must be true, she says. "The truth is bad enough already." Biographer about Wilbrink: 'He is himself responsible for statements' Wilbrink's biography appeared in 2023 and was written by Laurens van Aggelen. He says that he checked everything he could check. "But Wilbrink is also himself responsible for what he says", Van Aggelen believes. The story that he wrote in the biography had already been told in other media, he states. "Only mine is more extensive." Yet the biographer also omitted claims by the 99-year-old from the book, because they could not be true, Van Aggelen says. That Wilbrink said things that were presumably incorrect can, according to him, have to do with his advanced age. But, Van Aggelen states: "I am a biographer, it is not a scientific book." Family does not want to go into the matter Wilbrink's family has let other media know that they stand behind his claims. To the NOS they do not want to go into the substance of the matter. NIOD researcher Ribbens agrees with that. He states that people know the general story about the Second World War as it is in the history books, but that personal stories make the war more imaginable and easier to empathise with. "Precisely because those stories have emotion, they are appealing and valuable." The problem with this kind of personal story is that they are held up to the light less critically than historians normally do, Ribbens says. At the NIOD hardly any comparable cases are known. "But if there are more examples of this kind, then people will become critical of stories that are in fact very well substantiated and factually correct." "Towards the end of his imprisonment my father weighed only 40 kilos", Brugsma concludes. "He barely survived his time in Dachau. Those are the real stories." Newsletter Second World War Interested in the Second World War? Then subscribe here to our newsletter.

title: Podcast De Dag: No Televizier ring, but pearls
lead: Yesterday evening the reality programme De Bondgenoten won the Gouden Televizier-ring. The other nominees were consumer programme Kassa and the drama series Woeste Grond . Very different programmes competed for the TV prize and there is so much more to see. Many programmes get barely any attention. Then do not forget to subscribe. title: Ice rinks open despite high temperature: 'Otherwise we run into trouble with competitions'
lead: Despite temperatures around 20 degrees, many Dutch artificial ice rinks opened again last week. Skaters could not wait to get on the ice, but others often look at it with amazement. The question is regularly heard whether the skating season could not start later. Because the higher the temperature outside, the more energy it takes to lay an ice floor. Ice master Frank Zuurendonk of the rink in <entity id="org:gemeente-haarlem">Haarlem</entity> thinks there is something to be said for starting later. "You could ask yourself: shouldn't you just start in November?" But other ice rinks consider this not an option because of the competition calendar of the Dutch skating association KNSB and the international skating association ISU. "As long as the ISU calendar does not change, the skating season will not change either," says ice master Tonnie Horstman of ice rink De Scheg in <entity id="org:gemeente-deventer">Deventer</entity>. 'Lay the best ice' The Netherlands has 22 permanent artificial ice rinks. They decide for themselves when they open. Most do so at the beginning of October. The ice rink in <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> always opens later than the rest: in November. The rink in <entity id="org:gemeente-alkmaar">Alkmaar</entity> opens not at the beginning, but halfway through October. "We sail our own course," says location manager Roy Lennings. "We want to lay the best ice for our skaters." For the quality of the ice it is indeed better to start later, says ice master Zuurendonk of the rink in Haarlem. Not only because of the temperature, but especially because of the wind. In October, due to the strong autumn wind, it is often difficult to make good ice, says the ice master. Less energy In the discussion about the length of the skating season, sustainability is also a theme. Because ice rinks are energy guzzlers. Commissioned by the <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">gemeente Amsterdam</entity>, research was done in 2020 into the consumption of various ice rinks. The rink in <entity id="org:gemeente-leeuwarden">Leeuwarden</entity> would consume 49.3 kilowatt hours per day for every cubic meter of ice. That is roughly as much as a family consumes in electricity in a week. Opening later in the year could mean less energy consumption. In November, after all, the outside temperatures are lower than in October, so less energy is needed to make ice. But opening later is not the only way to save energy, says Joris Wouters, director of the Jaap Eden Baan in Amsterdam. "We should not choose between skating and sustainability, but look at how we can make skating more sustainable." According to him, the KNSB and the ice rinks are actively working on this. The so-called Team Duurzaam IJs, of the KNSB, Essent and Daikin, was founded two years ago with the aim of making ice rinks energy neutral. Ice rink De Meent in Alkmaar underwent a sustainability process in 2023 that serves as an example for the other rinks. "The heat released during ice making we now store in the ground and with that we heat the sports complex," says location manager Lennings. Running into trouble with competitions "The most sustainable is of course not to skate, but that is very black and white," says manager of sports participation Jurre Trouw on behalf of the KNSB. He points out that in the whole discussion about the length of the skating season you should not forget the skaters. "The rinks are open in October for clubs: they have the wish to skate and you want to offer them a decent sports offering." Moreover, "you run into trouble with competitions" if the opening of the skating season is postponed, says Trouw. The international skating association ISU makes a competition calendar, on which the KNSB in turn aligns the national calendar. In a week, the Dutch skating season will traditionally be opened with the IJsselcup. If we really want the season to start later, a change is needed in the mindset of skaters, says ice master Zuurendonk. "They are really raring to start now." Wouters of the Jaap Eden Baan also says that. "You should not express the value of an ice rink only in kilowatt hours. An ice rink is more than a layer of ice."

title: EU and China reach provisional agreement on export of hybrid cars
lead: After two days of talks, the European Union and China have reached a provisional agreement in Beijing to slow down the export of Chinese hybrid and plug-in hybrid cars to Europe. European Commissioner Sefcovic, who held talks with Chinese Minister of Trade Wang Wentao, spoke afterwards of "tangible results". According to him, they agreed to halve the Chinese export of hybrid and plug-in hybrid cars to the European market. Over the next four years, that means a decrease of several million cars, he said. In addition, according to Sefcovic, agreements were made about better access for European products to the Chinese market and about, for example, the export of rare earth metals from China. China has published a statement confirming that there is an agreement on this subject. Details are not mentioned in that statement. Unfair competition The talks had to provide an answer to the rising trade tensions between Brussels and Beijing. The EU has long complained about the large trade deficit with China and unfair competition due to Chinese state aid. According to the European Commission, that trade deficit cost more than 1 billion euros per day last year. The car sector was an important topic during the talks. The import of plug-in hybrids from China increased sharply last year, while prices fell. European manufacturers therefore fear unfair competition. 'Positive step' The European car industry organisation ACEA welcomes the agreement. The organisation speaks of a positive step to reduce the trade tensions. However, ACEA says it still has to analyse the details of the agreement. Sefcovic says in his statement that European Commission President Von der Leyen will assess the outcomes of the talks. Follow-up steps will then be discussed with European government leaders during the upcoming European Council.

title: Cabinet condemns US sanctions against Criminal Court, but still hopes for diplomacy
lead: The Dutch cabinet condemns the new American sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC). <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> says in an initial response that he fully supports the institution in The Hague. He calls the sanctions "deeply regrettable". On the other hand, Jetten is pleased that the new measures will only take effect in six months. There is then still "plenty of time" to talk with the United States about what Jetten calls "a suitable solution". The US has previously announced measures against the ICC, which prosecutes people suspected of, for example, genocide and war crimes. President Trump does not recognize the institution and finds it unacceptable that the Criminal Court has issued an arrest warrant against Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu. Paralyze The Americans now want to prohibit transactions with what they see as a "runaway court" and also "paralyze their ability to function", said US Secretary Rubio of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> today in a video message on X . This could mean that ICC employees can no longer access their bank accounts or can no longer travel to the US. It has not come to that yet, also to the relief of <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> of Foreign Affairs. In an initial response, he does speak of an "undesirable and new escalation", but he also emphasizes the importance of the diplomatic talks with Trump. Berendsen repeatedly speaks of following the "diplomatic track". He does not want to comment on what the Netherlands will offer to accommodate the United States. "We will enter into an open conversation." And Jetten also speaks of an "open conversation". Outside political The Hague too, there is indignant reaction to the sanctions. President of the European Council António Costa says he "will take appropriate steps to protect the court". EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas emphasizes that protecting the ICC remains "a European priority". Like Jetten, she says there is room for dialogue in the coming months. The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, calls the measures "unacceptable". He calls on the US to withdraw all sanctions against the ICC and its staff. The ICC itself is also unhappy with the American decision.
