"The sanctions are intended to undermine the international rule of law and hinder the work of an independent judicial institution," ICC deputy prosecutor Nazhat Shameem Khan told Reuters news agency. Difficult position Trump's sanctions against the International Criminal Court have put the Netherlands in a difficult diplomatic position. On the one hand, the Netherlands wants to stand firmly for the international legal order and in particular for the Criminal Court based in The Hague. But on the other hand, the Netherlands must also not provoke the United States, an important NATO ally, too much. The United States is also an important trading partner of the Netherlands. Jetten's first appearance at the UN General Assembly in New York at the end of September was therefore awaited with some tension. At that time, Jetten chose harsh words to make clear to Trump that his attacks on the court were not accepted. They undermine the international legal order as a whole, he said. The VVD already let it be known today what the party considers important. In a tweet on X, MP Rajkowski says that as far as the VVD is concerned, the "economic and security interests of the Netherlands weigh heavily in how the cabinet responds to these sanctions".

title: Flemish politician Filip Dewinter gets hit in row with wedding guests
lead: Vlaams Belang politician Filip Dewinter sustained minor injuries to his head in a scuffle at Antwerp city hall. He became involved in a row with a Moroccan-Belgian family that was celebrating a wedding on the Grote Markt, Flemish media report. The leading figure of the right-nationalist party was at city hall together with party colleague Anke Van dermeersch to sign the condolence register for the Antwerp singer John de Wilde, who died last week. At the same time, a group of about fifty people had gathered for a wedding. In footage it can be seen that there is pushing and pulling when Dewinter tries to move through the crowd. Van dermeersch filmed part of the row, Dewinter has shared that footage on X. What happened before or after the clip is not clear. The parties involved have differing accounts of how the incident arose. Hard blows According to Dewinter, as he passed he was "immediately mocked and called a racist". He was reportedly grabbed by the throat by a man, after which he was hit by ten to fifteen people. "Usually it does not come to physical blows, but it stays with insults, shouting and yelling," he tells VRT. "As a politician of Vlaams Belang I unfortunately have to deal with that regularly, but I have the impression that this is getting worse and worse." A member of the family that was celebrating the wedding party tells Gazet van Antwerpen that the discussion had already arisen earlier, because Van dermeersch wanted to film them. A family member tells VRT that Dewinter pushed several people on his way to city hall. When the bride's mother asked them to stop filming, Van dermeersch reportedly hit her in the face first. The police have detained two persons, both from the group of wedding guests. Dewinter suffered a bleeding wound on his eyebrow. He has given a statement to the police.

title: Three men arrested in Ghent for shooting in Overasselt
lead: In Ghent, three men have been arrested who were presumably involved in the shooting in Overasselt early last month. That reports the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. The suspects are 23, 25 and 28 years old. They are suspected of murder, manslaughter, firearm possession and membership of a criminal organization. The police do not say what their role would have been in the explosion of violence on 1 September in the Gelderland village. The men, all three of whom live in the vicinity of the city of Ghent, were arrested by a special police team. Three homes and a warehouse were also searched. Various data carriers and vehicles were seized. The Dutch <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> has requested the extradition of the three suspects. Last week, RTL Nieuws wrote that the men who entered Overasselt and shot dead a security guard were recruited via social media. They would have received instructions for the attack via messages on Signal and Snapchat.

title: No BMW for AfD member Tobias Rausch after lease offer withdrawn
lead: AfD member Tobias Rausch will have to do without a company car for now. The right-wing radical politician was elected on Tuesday as president of the state parliament of Saxony-Anhalt and therefore claimed a BMW, but the car manufacturer withdrew the lease offer. BMW has not explained why the offer was withdrawn. However, a BMW board member earlier told a local Frankfurt newspaper that far-right parties are "poison for the economy". The AfD branch in Saxony-Anhalt has been classified as far-right by the German security service. Rausch is not happy with the decision. In a letter to the BMW board of directors, which is in the hands of the German medium Die Zeit, he writes that he is very surprised and disappointed. So far, no other car brand has come forward to supply the company car. Rausch has announced that he will then just go to business appointments in his private car. Switching to moped AfD parliamentary group leader in Saxony-Anhalt Ulrich Siegmund says that in solidarity he is switching to a Simson moped. He also spent the entire election campaign on one recently. "In December I will come to the State Chancellery with that specific moped," he declared to Die Zeit. With that, he refers to the minister-presidency of the state, a position for which he himself is in the running after the AfD's recent election victory. BMW's action also did not go unnoticed by Beatrix von Storch, vice-chair of the AfD parliamentary group. On X she addressed Elon Musk with the question of whether Tesla is willing to make a company car available to Rausch.

title: Powerful earthquake in Panama, power out and damage to buildings
lead: Panama has been hit by an earthquake with a magnitude of 7.7. That would make it one of the heaviest quakes of the year, worldwide. There are no reports of casualties yet. The epicenter of the quake was in the southern province of Herrera, a sparsely populated area. Local media report that in various regions of the country people had to leave buildings, businesses, schools and homes. "We felt it very strongly. Things fell over in the kitchen, but we are all right, although we are very scared," the 60-year-old Rosendo Domínguez from Herrera tells news agency AP by telephone. "Everyone is outside, full of fear." Damage to buildings A spokesperson for the national civil protection service tells news channel Telemetro Reporta that there is mainly damage in the provinces of Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos. In the city of Penonomé, roughly halfway between the epicenter and the capital Panama City, the cathedral, the governor's office and a hotel, among others, are said to have suffered considerable damage. The power supply has failed in six provinces. The tremors were also clearly felt some 200 kilometres away in Panama City, according to people at the scene for around 40 seconds. Buildings began to shake and people fled into the street. So far no damage has been reported in the city, which is known for its hundreds of skyscrapers. The country's international airport is temporarily closed. Shipping through the Panama Canal is continuing as usual, the authorities report. Shortly after the quake there were several aftershocks. The national weather service initially issued a tsunami warning for the coasts of Panama and several surrounding countries, but it was later withdrawn. Panama lies along the 'Ring of Fire', the arc of fault lines around the Pacific Ocean where most and the heaviest earthquakes in the world occur. Next Monday a large national evacuation exercise was to take place in the country, to test how well the emergency services function during earthquakes.

title: 'Co-pilot who wanted to crash the aircraft was inspired by 9/11'
lead: The co-pilot who wanted to take over the aircraft during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv and stabbed his captain in the process, wanted to carry out an attack inspired by the terrorist attacks of 9/11. That is what the public prosecutor of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has made known. The prosecutor's investigation also brings other important findings to light. The 29-year-old suspect would have used two earlier flights to Tel Aviv to "familiarise himself with the flight route and the airport", in preparation for his deed. Whether he was also a pilot on these flights or flew along as a civilian is not known. During interrogations the man, who is an Omani citizen, has stated that he acted alone. Israeli passengers The man would have intended to fly into a terminal of the Israeli Ben-Gurion airport, the authorities confirm. Earlier this week sources close to the police investigation already reported that the co-pilot was probably planning to crash the aircraft at the international airport of Tel Aviv, the largest airport in the country. The suspect had "the intention to cause the largest possible number of victims", according to public prosecutor Hamad Saif al Shamsi. Most of the 174 passengers on board came from Israel. For the Israeli government that was reason enough to state immediately that the co-pilot was out to kill as many Israelis as possible. Israel has announced that it will request the man's extradition. According to the public prosecutor, the co-pilot was inspired by the attacks of 11 September 2001 in the US, when hijackers of the terrorist organisation al-Qaida flew two aircraft into the Twin Towers in New York. Nearly 3000 people died in the process. The Omani co-pilot was on his way to Tel Aviv together with his Indian captain on 30 September, when he attacked him with an emergency axe . Although the captain was seriously injured, he managed to open the cockpit door, after which passengers could storm in and overpower the attacker. Two pilots who were flying along as passengers on the flight of airline Flydubai then took over the controls of the aircraft and landed it safely in Saudi Arabia. On footage on board the Flydubai flight chaotic scenes could be heard: The suspect, who had been employed by Flydubai since January, had according to the prosecutor previously worked for airlines in several countries, including Oman Air and Royal Air Maroc. At Oman Air he was previously suspended , because extremist material was found on him. How he was nevertheless able to start work as a co-pilot at Flydubai is not yet clear. In 2017 there were already indications that the suspect slid into extremism and terrorism during a study in Australia, the investigation establishes. What those indications are has not been made known. Earlier this week Australia would have opened an anti-terror investigation. Saudi Arabia has started a separate security investigation into the incident with flight FZ1073. The aircraft was in Saudi airspace when the Omani co-pilot attacked the captain.

title: 110 arrests on a day full of violence in central Brussels
lead: In Brussels at least 110 people have been detained after a strike day by trade unions ended in riots. Only in the course of the evening did calm return to the Belgian capital, reports VRT Nieuws. The trade unions protested today against cuts to social security. After some time, hundreds to thousands of young people mingled among the demonstrators. According to various media, that was because of the planned cuts to education, but the police deny that there was a connection with those cuts or with the trade union action. The young people were mostly dressed in black and wore masks. They threw stones, set cars and shared bicycles on fire and caused many other acts of destruction. The police deployed water cannons and tear gas to drive the young people apart. The Belgian minister Quintin of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> has announced that there will be a response proportionate to the damage caused. The mayor of Brussels has also spoken out against the violence. He calls it "absolutely scandalous" that public services were attacked during the riots. The mayor wants firm action to be taken against the rioters and wants identified perpetrators to bear the financial cost of the damage. According to VRT, the trade unions had been warned that their strike action could be hijacked. After education protests earlier this week in Luik, it had been advised to possibly postpone the action. On Tuesday, dozens of activists there went along secondary schools, where they smashed windows and set fire to rubbish bins. The trade unions nevertheless decided to take to the streets today. This weekend the federal government will negotiate again about the cuts to social security. That is why the unions considered it important to make themselves heard today. According to Belgian media, the federal government is looking for about 10 billion euros to balance the budget. The trade unions fear that cuts will be made in, among other things, social security. Watch here footage of the disturbances earlier in the day:

title: Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in mountain village Peru
lead: Residents of a remote village in the Peruvian Andes have a new mayor. Normally not world news, but because of his name it is: the new mayor is called Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores. The candidate of the centre-left party Ahora Nación has been elected mayor of Queropalca, a small place in the province of Lauricocha north of the capital Lima. As mayor, the 45-year-old Simeon Flores will represent a community of just over 700 inhabitants. 229 inhabitants voted for him. With this he stayed 25 votes ahead of the candidate of the right-wing party Renovación Popular Perú. That he is named after the fascist dictators Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini has made his candidacy a "remarkable event", reports the local news channel Peru21. Yet Simeon Flores is not the first mayor in Peru named Hitler. In 2018 Hitler Guesclin Alba Sánchez was elected mayor of Yúngar, elsewhere in the Andes. In that election this Hitler defeated a candidate with another remarkable name: Lenin Vladimir Rodriguez Valverde, inspired by the founder of the Soviet Union, Vladimir Lenin. But even there the story about Hitlers in politics in Peru does not end. Until 2024 there was also a Hitler in the Peruvian congress. This Hitler Saavedra was a member of parliament in the South American country from 2021 until his death. Remarkable first names occur more often in Peru, also if they can have a negative historical association. Besides being named after historical figures, Peruvians are also named after celebrities like Bad Bunny, fictional characters like Spider-Man and there even appears to be a Netflix walking around in Peru. Namibian Hitler Also outside South America there are politicians named after the Nazi dictator. A politician named Adolf Hitler Uunona attracted worldwide attention in 2020 after he won local elections in Namibia. In that country - a former German colony - names like Adolf and other Germanic first names are not unusual. By the way, the Namibian politician announced last year that he had dropped his second first name because it reflected "neither his character nor his ambition". Moreover, he constantly had to answer questions from abroad about his name.

title: US suspends its own sanctions and accepts Russian diesel: 'Gift for Putin'
lead: Russia will "immediately" supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the American market and the world market. That is what president Trump writes on his platform Truth Social, after he said he had spoken with the Russian president Putin. The US is temporarily suspending sanctions on Russian oil for this. According to Trump, Russia has also agreed to supply another 500,000 tons of diesel in November and later another deliveries of one million and three million tons. The latter, according to him, does depend on "the condition of their diesel refineries". After Trump's announcement, the Ministry of Finance granted a temporary permit that makes the import of Russian diesel possible. Since the start of the war in Iran, diesel prices in the US have doubled. At the end of last month the price per gallon (about 3.8 litres) rose to a record high of 6.53 dollars. The average price per gallon is according to the platform AAA today 6.28 dollars. Election theme The high fuel prices are an important theme in the November midterm elections in the US. Last week the G7 countries already announced that they would release millions of barrels of diesel and crude oil in the coming months after increasing pressure from Trump. In his message Trump states that diesel prices for Americans, and for the rest of the world, will fall quickly. "Lower prices for our great farmers, cattle farmers and truck drivers are my greatest priority." What is the problem on the diesel market? Years ago, among others Europe imported a lot of diesel from Russia. Because of the Russian invasion of Ukraine that was stopped. In 2022 that was a problem, and it caused high prices at the pump. Now the war in the Middle East is the cause of the high diesel prices. That is initially because much fewer raw materials, including oil, can be transported through the Strait of Hormuz. Also many production locations around the Persian Gulf have suffered damage and it will take a long time before those locations function normally again. The production locations make refined products from crude oil, including diesel. Trump is trying to solve the higher prices at the pump: if more diesel comes onto the market, prices will fall as a result of market forces. Ukrainian president Zelensky has reacted to the American-Russian agreement. According to him, it plays into Russia's hands. "Any easing of sanctions against Russia without a clear and sustainable de-escalation agreement with Russia is an obvious weakness, which will cause Russia to kill more people, fight longer, respect America even less and cause even more losses and damage to the world", he states in a message on Telegram. According to him, "gifts to Putin will not contribute to peace and will yield no advantage whatsoever to the civilised world". Zelensky writes that granting Russia permission to sell oil products amounts to an investment in a war. Shadow fleet The European Union has imposed sanctions several times on the Russian shadow fleet, one of the few ways in which Russia gets its oil products across the world. The aim of the sanctions is among other things that less money flows to the Russian treasury for the war in Ukraine. For the same reason Trump himself signed a sanctions law against Russia in mid-September. The law imposed for example further restrictions on Russia in the sale of oil. The sanctions were also aimed at Russian tankers of the shadow fleet .

title: Yesilgöz despite criticism: 'I am the next VVD lead candidate'
lead: VVD leader Yesilgöz wants to become lead candidate again at the next elections. In an interview with the NOS after a VVD meeting in Veghel, she clearly expresses her ambitions. Asked whether she is the logical next lead candidate of the VVD, Yesilgöz says: "Yes I am." She has been party leader since August 2023 and succeeded <entity id="person:mark-rutte">Mark Rutte</entity> at that time. Criticism within the party base of Yesilgöz and of the course of the VVD leadership in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> has been growing recently. In the polls the governing party is not doing very well and former VVD politicians are voicing their dissatisfaction through newspapers . Especially last week - when the cabinet plans of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Jetten were considerably adjusted at the urging of Pro and the trade unions - considerable dissatisfaction was heard among the party base . Concerns One of the points of criticism was that the party would have given in too quickly to pressure from Pro-<entity id="person:jesse-feras-klaver">leider Klaver</entity>. That stung all the more because Yesilgöz during the campaign for the House of Representatives elections had promised her voters not to enter into a coalition with this party, which in her view is too left-wing. There also appeared to be concerns among VVD members about changes surrounding the wealth tax (box 3). There is still no clarity about that . Yesilgöz says in the NOS interview that she does not like the criticism. "Not as a person either". She does think that the media devote disproportionately much attention to what happens at the VVD. She does not want to dismiss the criticism, but the emergence of unrest within a party "is of all times". She has also experienced it as a council member, House of Representatives member and minister. "We are a party that loves to debate and then we move on again." Today's meeting with critical VVD members from <entity id="org:provincie-noord-brabant">Noord-Brabant</entity> was according to Yesilgöz "very good". Together with House of Representatives parliamentary group leader Brekelmans she answered questions for two hours before a hall of about 150 members. According to her, the image has wrongly arisen that the VVD "was rolling out a left-wing agenda". Yesilgöz emphasises that she does want to cooperate with Pro, but then also together with the right-wing party JA21. "We do want to work with Pro, but then not without the right". Afterwards she says that cooperation only with Pro on "parts" might be possible, such as with the nitrogen plans. At the end of November there is a VVD congress. Then it will become clearer whether the VVD leadership has succeeded in reassuring the critical members about the approach.

title: Right-wing political commentator Katie Zacharia new White House press secretary
lead: Donald Trump has appointed right-wing political commentator Katie Zacharia as the new White House press secretary. She succeeds Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down from her position at the end of August. Like Leavitt, Zacharia is also a loyal MAGA supporter. She described the American president in a guest column in the conservative newspaper New York Post a few months ago as "the greatest president in American history". Zacharia worked among other things as a communications adviser at the Trump Media & Technology Group, which manages Trump's Truth Social network, and she worked briefly as deputy press secretary for the American Department of Homeland Security. She was also a legal adviser to the conservative political lobby group Fix California. In addition, she was seen among other things as a political commentator on CNN, Fox News and Newsmax. Swing states Trump announced the appointment on Truth Social. He calls Zacharia someone who "has been a loyal and brilliant supporter from the very beginning". According to him, the conservative jurist assisted him already during the election campaign and supported him in important 'swing states', states that are fiercely contested by Republicans and Democrats. Zacharia calls the appointment "the honour of my life". She states that her task is to convey what she calls the "great successes" of the Trump administration to the American people. Low approval ratings Zacharia faces a challenging task. She will be at the centre of attention at a time just before next month's midterm elections. She must convey Trump's positions as effectively as possible at a time when the president is struggling with low approval ratings in his own country. A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll shows that Trump's approval rating has fallen to 32 percent, the lowest level of his political career. That is partly because fellow Republicans are dissatisfied with America's war with Iran and the cost of living. A lawsuit is also ongoing by several media outlets that have been denied access to the White House by Trump's administration.

title: Winner of prestigious scientific image competition disqualified over AI
lead: The winner of a prestigious competition for images made with the help of a microscope has been disqualified. The spectacular winning short video of minuscule moving cilia in a child's airways turned out to have been made with artificial intelligence (AI). Researcher Ning Xu of Tsinghua University in China had submitted a short video for the Small World in Motion competition showing the cilia moving in the airways of a child with the rare hereditary condition PCD. With that condition, the microscopic cilia do not move properly, which means, among other things, that mucus is poorly cleared. Immediately after the winner was chosen, scepticism about the video arose in the scientific world. A British scientist who has been researching PCD for more than 20 years states to the BBC that he "immediately knew that the video was staged". The cells and cilia look in the video "completely different from those of PCD patients", states Robert Hirst. Maker denies that images are fake Others also described how in the video cells appeared and disappeared in a way that does not occur in cell biology. People also discovered watermarks in the source files that are added to AI-generated videos. Maker Xu denied that the images are fake. He stated that he had only used artificial intelligence "to distinguish and visualise features in the reconstructed grayscale images", reports news site Ars Technica. Nikon, the organiser of the competition, started an investigation and concluded that the video indeed did not comply with the rules of the competition. The winner is now the Vietnamese Nam Nhat Nguyen, who captured a small roundworm and a single-celled organism. Since the rise of AI, it occurs more often that in a photo and video competition people make unauthorised use of artificial intelligence. For example, a German artist who won the Sony World Photography Award in 2023 was disqualified after it turned out that his photo was made entirely with AI, while the jury thought the basis was real. Artist Boris Eldagen had admitted the use immediately after receiving the prize. He stated that with this he wanted to start a discussion about the future of photography. But sometimes it can also 'go wrong' the other way. For example, in 2024 a photographer was disqualified who submitted a photo of a flamingo to a photo competition with a category for AI images. Photographer Miles Astray deliberately broke the rules. "I realised that I could turn it around the way only a human can by submitting a real photo for an AI competition. Of course I deliberately chose a photo that is so surreal and unbelievable," he stated. This is what that photo looked like:

title: Brazilian police kill man who held thirteen young children hostage
lead: The Brazilian police have killed a man in the southern city of Curitiba who held thirteen children hostage in a school for more than two hours. The hostage-taking was at a complex containing a kindergarten and a primary school, reports the newspaper Folha de S. Paulo . According to the newspaper, the children were between 4 and 5 years old. According to a police spokesperson, the man threatened to pour petrol over himself and the hostages and set them and himself on fire. "Our negotiators were present, but we saw no other option than to take him out," the spokesperson states. Crying parents According to the police, the man suffered from schizophrenia. Local footage shows crying parents waiting outside the school for information while the police are negotiating with the hostage-taker. After about two hours, two bangs were heard, after which officers came outside with a number of the children. The city council of Curitiba says it is offering psychological help to the children and the staff who were held hostage.

title: Wake-up service 10/10: Housing protest on Dam Square • Feyenoord-AZ in the Eredivisie
lead: Good morning! Today there is another housing protest in Amsterdam and in the eredivisie, among others, Feyenoord and AZ play each other. First the weather: in many places it will rain, especially in the north there is also a chance of thunder, hail and heavy gusts of wind. The wind comes from the west and the maximum temperature is 15 degrees. Are you going out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks and here everything about the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? Russia will immediately supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the US and the world market. President Trump announces this after a conversation with the Russian president Putin. The US temporarily suspends its own sanctions against Russia for this. The high fuel prices, partly caused by the war in Iran, are an important election theme in the US. According to Trump, this will quickly lower diesel prices for Americans and the rest of the world. In a response, Ukrainian president Zelensky says that "gifts to Putin do not contribute to peace". Other news from the night: And then also this: The Dutch women's football team won convincingly against Hungary in the play-offs for the 2027 World Cup. On a visit to the Central European country, it became no less than 0-8. Good weekend!

title: Dozens of bullets fired in Overasselt: reconstruction of a night full of excessive violence
lead: More than forty times shots are fired in the direction of the officers who are the first on the scene at the house of Jan G. in Overasselt on 1 September. Shortly before that, a large group of armed men had moved through the village and shot a security guard dead in his car. In the meantime, 42 suspects have been arrested for this explosion of violence, the last three yesterday. Some perpetrators do not shy away from heavy violence, others seem to have hardly any idea what they were recruited for. That emerges from a reconstruction by the NOS based on documents from the criminal file, in collaboration with Omroep Gelderland. 'Light flashes from all sides' Shortly after 04:00, the first police car arrives on the Ewijkseweg in Overasselt. The officers are responding to an emergency report and have already been warned by the dispatch center en route to "put on heavy vests". When the two officers get out, they immediately come under fire. One of them presses his emergency button and shouts in panic that he has a gunshot wound in his leg. His colleagues hear through the radio that the shooting continues incessantly. He is also hit in his other leg, his colleague is shot in his foot. A second police car arrives on the scene. These officers see "many shadows of persons" who "run crisscross through each other". They too are shot at; there are "light flashes from all sides". At risk to their own lives, the officers run to their seriously wounded colleague. He lies on the ground behind the police car. Blood flows from his leg and the officers immediately know that his artery has been hit. They fear that he will die on the spot. The shooting is still going on, in total about forty shots are fired. The officers try to hoist their hit colleagues into the car. The windshield has been shot out, there is no time to close the doors. While the lower body of the seriously wounded officer is still hanging out of the car, they speed away. A colleague holds him so that he does not fall out of the car. 'Dead man in the car' The officer behind the wheel wants to drive to a safe location, but has to stop along the way first to apply a pressure bandage. While officers who have rushed over cordon off the area in Overasselt with tape, a man walks up to them. In English with a French accent he says: "There is a man dead in the car." He points to the Ewijkseweg. The man who addresses the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is himself arrested shortly afterwards. He is one of the now 42 suspects, 39 of whom are in custody. All but one are suspected of murder, attempted murder and a series of other crimes. The youngest suspect is 16 years old and they come from all directions: some from the Netherlands, others from Belgium, yet others from France. A French suspect says after his arrest that he is homeless and sometimes steals food. Another still lives with his mother and has a debt of 25,000 euros. He is no longer allowed to come to Marseille because he dealt drugs there. Some of the suspects were lured by intermediaries or via social media with the prospect of a "well-paid job". Many men say they had no idea what that job entailed exactly. One has stated that he assumed he had to steal cars, other suspects were told that they had to beat someone up for 15,000 euros. "Is 15k, we get 7.5 today the rest in 2 days max", says a message on his phone. The French suspects gather in Brussels and are taken to an unknown warehouse in the early evening, on 31 August. There their phones and identity papers are taken away. They are also handed heavy weapons and pistols. The group is divided in two: people who can handle a weapon, and people who have never fired a shot. The first group must go in front later, the second group forms the rear guard. Refusing the job is no longer an option. A suspect says he was threatened with a firearm in the warehouse because he wanted to leave. Another says he was beaten, after which his phone and the 85 euros he had on him were taken away. One of the leaders appears to be someone called "the Chechen". Whoever does not listen will be killed, he is said to have threatened. According to one of the suspects, it was said in the warehouse that someone else had been shot dead the week before who refused to cooperate. The group that has experience with weapons is told: "Everyone must die. Whether it's the goldfish or the cat: everyone must die." Then the men are driven in the back of a truck or a van to Overasselt. The police investigation also shows that several cars drove from Amsterdam to Overasselt. Those are presumably the Dutch suspects. A number of them have a substantial criminal record, from violent crimes to bank helpdesk fraud. Futile warning Surveillance footage shows how two vans arrive in the street. A large group of men gets out. Some carry automatic firearms, others hold a pistol. A few minutes later the vehicles drive away again. In a car in front of the house of convicted drug criminal Jan G. sits security guard Berry. By chance Berry is on the job that night, he swapped a shift with his employer. When the two vans drive past his car, he gets out to see what is going on. Then he calls his boss. Who shouts that he should "get the hell out of there". The connection is broken. This is how the vans arrived: The owner of the security company apps him a few more times: "Get away from there", "Are you gone?" and "Let me know something". He also calls him four more times, but Berry no longer answers. He has been shot dead. The footage shows that 'the Chechen', a 30-year-old man from Ukraine, walks in front on the Ewijkseweg. From the same footage, the detectives deduce that he may be the one who killed Berry. He is recognized by his Lacoste shoes. Other suspects may also have shot at the security guard. Not everyone within the suspect group is keen on this violence. When the first shots are fired at 04:05, part of the men immediately flee. Others shoot at the police, who arrive a few minutes later, and then take off. The moment the security guard is shot: With suspects scattered in all directions, a large search operation immediately begins in the wide surroundings of Overasselt. Some suspects can be arrested fairly quickly in the village. A group hides in a cornfield less than two kilometers from Jan G.'s house, which is surrounded by the Special Interventions Service. With thermal imaging cameras, drones and a helicopter, the police manage to locate several suspects. 'The Chechen' is also plucked from the cornfield. The suspects try to flee the area in all kinds of ways. A truck with a Polish license plate that was used, containing three suspects, is forced to stop on the A50. Three other suspects who flee in a car with a Belgian license plate are arrested at a gas station in Nijmegen. Someone is arrested at a bus stop in Mill, another tries soaking wet in Malden to order a taxi. Three suspects get away thanks to a lift, but stand out elsewhere because they are covered in mud. There are even two suspects caught on stolen bicycles on a dike. The furthest come two suspects who are arrested on the A76 in Limburg, just before the Belgian border. They took a taxi from Cuijk, but the police still manage to find them shortly after 12:00. Also in the weeks after the incident, the police continue to arrest new suspects who would have played a role in the events in Overasselt. Yesterday three young men were arrested near Ghent. Client The investigation into the client of the violence is still ongoing; no one has been arrested for this yet. The first hearing in the case is in December. Target Jan G. is now also in custody. He managed to escape the outbreak of violence at his house, but was arrested more than two weeks later in Germany because he would be involved in a large cocaine transport.

title: Podcast De Dag: waiting for the surrogacy law
lead: In the Netherlands, approximately thirty to fifty families have a child each year with the help of a surrogate mother. And that number is increasing. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> also says he sometimes thinks about it for himself. But legally nothing is arranged for this group and that leads to unpleasant situations for both intended parents and for surrogate mothers. Annemiek van Tilborgh, also known from B&B Vol Liefde , was a surrogate mother twice for a good friend. She does not want to raise the children herself, but does regret how quickly she gave up legal parenthood. Want to listen? You can listen to this episode of De Dag via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. A new surrogacy law that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> wants to introduce continues to be postponed. Why? What are the dilemmas? Nieuwsuur -journalist Fleur Damen spoke with among others surrogate mothers, intended parents and juvenile judges. She saw how this dossier is vulnerable and emotional for everyone. The need for clarity is great among many, but there are also objections and criticism of the draft law. Respond? Mail dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Elisabeth Steinz Editorial staff: Rosanne Sies Final editing: Judith van de Hulsbeek

title: Controversial Orange march banned after 13-day stalemate: 'Situation has changed'
lead: Thirteen days after large-scale protest made a controversial Orange march in Northern Ireland impossible, the parade has been definitively cancelled. The British Minister for Northern Ireland Affairs fears that the heightened tensions will erupt into violence and therefore bans the march. Orange marches by Protestant unionists through neighborhoods where many Catholic republicans live caused much tension and violence for years. After the Good Friday Agreement ended the violence in Northern Ireland, no more permits were granted for the controversial marches. This year that changed: the permit committee ruled that a limited march in the town of Portadown should be possible. A limited number of people would be allowed to follow this route, without musicians. Residents of the Catholic neighborhood reacted furiously and blocked the route of the march on 27 September. The small parade in Portadown occupied all of Northern Ireland. In this article you can read where those great tensions come from: Since then there have been consultations with both parties about how the march can still take place. Minister Chris Bryant now draws the conclusion that further talks are pointless. "The situation has now changed so much that the march can no longer go ahead," he explained his decision last night. "It could no longer happen without enormous police involvement and with a serious risk of injuries, unrest and repercussions throughout Northern Ireland." The residents of the Catholic neighborhood applaud the decision. "Strength and dignity have overcome provocation and intimidation," says the chair of the political party Sinn Féin, Mary Lou McDonald. "This will mean an enormous relief for the community." The unionist DUP, by contrast, says that this undermines the rule of law. "That the parade cannot go ahead is due to republican incitement and the threat of violence," believes DUP leader Gavin Robsinson. "This sends the signal that the country listens to whoever can get the most people on their feet and shouts the loudest.

title: No longer burning but recycling: manufacturers must start collecting old furniture
lead: Many discarded sofas and other furniture still end up in incinerators. A waste, thinks <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>. Furniture must be better recycled and reused. Just as with plastic bottles and cans, manufacturers and importers of products such as sofas, kitchen cabinets and beds will therefore also be made responsible within four years for the collection and reuse of their products. The cabinet expects to have a first draft plan ready this autumn. A growing number of municipalities is already anticipating this and has started recycling furniture itself. At this recycling center in Geldrop they show how that works: In total, about 2 billion kilos of new furniture is sold in the Netherlands per year, according to research agencies Tauw and Rebel. Annually, 260 million kilos of discarded furniture gets a second life via, for example, online sales platforms or thrift stores. But the largest part ends up at the recycling center. "Furniture lasts less and less long," says Jacolien Eijer, director of the NVRD, the interest group for municipalities in waste collection. "Most furniture that comes to the recycling center ultimately ends up in the incinerator." And that is a waste, because materials such as wood, metal, textile and foam can often be reused very well. That is why producers and importers of furniture will be made responsible by 2030 at the latest for the collection and recycling or reuse of the items they put on the market. Barbecue aprons and animal belts More and more municipalities and public waste companies do not want to wait for that and have already set up dismantling halls themselves. There are now six of them throughout the Netherlands. Often people with a distance to the labor market take the furniture apart. One of the waste companies involved is Cure Afvalbeheer, which handles collection in <entity id="org:gemeente-eindhoven">Eindhoven</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-valkenswaard">Valkenswaard</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-geldrop-mierlo">Geldrop-Mierlo</entity>. "We take apart all box springs and sofas that we receive via the recycling centers," says Twan de Waal of Cure. "Sofas without staples with a lot of cardboard are taken apart in 20 minutes. Others are more difficult and take half an hour." Box springs are even more difficult. "There is a hard side of wood stapled on. You can hardly get those staples out." Cure does this partly from the point of view of sustainability. The materials from the furniture are reused. For example, plastic is used to make beer crates and shopping baskets, wood is used to make new bathroom furniture, and leather is used to make animal belts and barbecue aprons. In addition, cost savings are an important motive. Because the more waste is burned, the more incineration tax must be paid. And that adds up considerably for furniture, precisely because it forms such a large and heavy mountain of waste. "That tax is already very high and will become much higher in the coming years," says De Waal of Cure. Citizens feel that in their wallets through the waste levies they pay. That is why it pays to extract reusable materials. "The less we have to burn, the lower the waste levy." Better to repair Furniture manufacturers and importers will now therefore pay the costs. "This creates an incentive for producers to make furniture that is easier to take apart, better to repair and reuse and lasts longer," says NVRD director Eijer. A number of companies have already started themselves. For example, IKEA has a buy-back service and customers can repair their furniture with spare parts. Office furniture company Ahrend refurbishes office furniture to sell it again. Mandatory reuse According to Eijer, it is especially important that clear targets are set upon introduction for more sustainable design and reuse of materials in furniture. For example, that a certain percentage must consist of recycled material by obligation. "Then a market arises for it and it becomes economically viable." Industry associations of furniture manufacturers CBM and RND support the introduction of producer responsibility. However, according to CBM it must happen in a "workable way" and according to RND there must first be data on how much furniture can be recycled and reused "in a profitable manner" before targets are set. The municipalities hope for cooperation with the manufacturers. "Furniture producers take in as many old furniture themselves as possible when they sell new ones. For the remaining part, municipalities are happy to help collect them," says NVRD director Eijer. In recycling too, the municipalities expect to continue to play a role. "It will be quite difficult for companies to do that in a good way."

title: Criticism of execution via livestream, Trump says decision is not yet final
lead: US President Trump says it has not yet been definitively decided to livestream the execution of a US soldier. The announcement yesterday by minister Hegseth drew much criticism. "Well, they still have to make a decision about it," Trump said evasively without going into detail when asked about the planned execution. "But he is being killed, that will happen by firing squad." Trump added that it "really doesn't matter how he goes, as long as he goes. I think the death penalty is a dignified way for him to go." 'Disgusting' On Thursday, minister Hegseth announced that the execution of Nidal Hasan "will be followable for everyone". The Pentagon later clarified that a livestream is being considered. Former major Hasan shot thirteen colleagues dead in 2009 at the military base Fort Hood in Texas. The Palestinian-American soldier stated that he wanted to protect Muslims in Afghanistan in this way. If the execution is indeed livestreamed, it will be the first public execution in the US since 1936. It is also the first time since 1961 that the US military carries out a death penalty. American politicians react with shock to the idea, including Republican party members of Trump. Influential senator Thom Tillis calls it "more than disgusting" and says that the US thereby joins the list of "tyrannical dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan". His colleague John Curtis warns that the Roman statesman and thinker Seneca already warned against bloody spectacles in Rome: "A civilization slides down when it regards executions as a form of entertainment". 'Sick' Democratic senators are even harsher. Jon Ossoff calls it an "obscene medieval spectacle" and considers Hegseth "a sick person who seems to revel in this kind of cruelty". His party colleague Jack Reed speaks of "a gift to anti-American terrorism recruiters". Vice President JD Vance also reacts with little enthusiasm. "I don't know if it will really happen," he said briefly to reporters. Afterwards he mainly wanted to talk about Hasan's crimes: "The method may be controversial, I hope people do not forget that this man cruelly murdered many innocent people". He added on his own initiative that he would not turn on the livestream himself. "I will not watch it."

title: Pedestrian killed on the A58 near Tilburg
lead: Someone was killed on the A58 near Tilburg last night. The victim presumably wanted to cross the motorway, reports Omroep Brabant . A truck could not avoid the pedestrian. Many emergency services were called out, including a trauma helicopter. However, the victim turned out to have already died. The A58 was closed near Tilburg for some time after the accident. Why the pedestrian was walking on the motorway is still being investigated. Nothing has yet been made public about the person's identity.

title: Arson at the railway, no trains between Rotterdam and Delft
lead: A fire was started last night at a railway bridge near Rotterdam-Delfshaven. That has major consequences for train traffic; it is at a standstill at least for the rest of the day between the stations Rotterdam Centraal and Delft Campus. Around 02:30 a malfunction occurred at the railway bridge. A contractor who went to the malfunction saw that the door of a technical room had been pried open. Inside lay smoldering cables. According to a spokesperson for rail manager ProRail, a fire was started there. It may be sabotage. The fire brigade has been present at the railway bridge over the Delfshavense Schie since last night. The fire has been extinguished and the technical room is being ventilated so that the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> can conduct an investigation. Only after the police have completed the investigation can ProRail go inside to assess the damage and make a recovery plan. How great the damage is will therefore only become clear later. No trains What is certain is that no trains will run between Rotterdam and Delft all day today. "I do not rule out that it could take longer," says a spokesperson for ProRail. The track between Rotterdam and Delft is one of the busiest routes in the Netherlands and is also used by trains that cover long distances, for example between the Randstad and Zeeland or Limburg. For travelers, this therefore causes a lot of disruption. Detours by train are possible via Gouda, NS is deploying buses between Rotterdam Centraal and Delft station. <entity id="person:annet-bertram">Staatssecretaris Bertram</entity> of Infrastructure is shocked by the incident. "That there is arson here and therefore intent, I find very reprehensible and worrying," she says.

title: AI tips off police about Philadelphia murder case, but it is talking nonsense
lead: "I may have information about the murder case," an unknown source wrote to the American police on 18 July. "I can remember that I saw someone who matches your description." A tip for the police in the American city of Philadelphia about an unsolved murder case. The message, however, did not come from an eyewitness at all, it now appears. In fact, the message was not even written by a human: the tip was submitted by artificial intelligence (AI). The American AI company Anthropic tested its AI application Claude on the internet in recent months, in order to develop advanced models. Things went wrong in the process, the company admits. Instructions unclear During that test phase, the AI model was given a number of restrictions. For example, it was not allowed to create accounts and not allowed to take harmful actions. The assignment did not state that the AI models had permission to fill in forms on the internet, but that was also not explicitly prohibited. For Claude, that was reason enough to submit a tip about a murder case. Which murder case it concerns has not been made public. It has also not been made public what the aim of the AI program was with the tip. The AI tip about the murder case already came in to the police this summer, but Anthropic only shared this week that the tip was fake. "The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident is unacceptable," the Philadelphia police say. No data stolen The police say that the AI tip "had been marked as spam" and that nothing was ever done with the report. Anthropic is said to have since stopped the tests. According to the police, there are no indications that the AI models had access to the police systems. As far as is known, this is the first time that an AI model has passed on a false tip to the police. Anthropic reported the incident this week to the American regulator FTC. Other incidents Anthropic also reported incidents on American government websites to the regulator. The company does not say what exactly it was able to do there and which websites were involved. All parties involved are said to have been informed. The AI models are also said to have succeeded in bypassing an online paywall. The models did this by modifying website links. Anthropic only shared the incidents with the American regulator at the end of September. "Companies must report incidents with their models immediately and then act quickly and decisively to repair any damage," the regulator writes. AI companies want attention In recent months, AI companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI massively tested their advanced models. Several incidents also occurred in the process, in which the models gained access to places where they should not have been at all. The AI companies like to talk about the risks of their newest AI programs in order to remain relevant. The models they warned about earlier usually still come onto the market later. This summer things also went wrong in Australia. AI models gained access to various government websites, without having permission to do so. OpenAI, the company behind the models, apologised for this. Australia's Prime Minister Albanese called the incidents "unacceptable".

title: KPN outage resolved, university hospitals reachable again
lead: Due to an outage at telecom provider KPN, part of the business customers were poorly reachable via the landline for hours. That also applied to a large number of university hospitals, such as in Utrecht, Maastricht, Nijmegen, Rotterdam and Groningen. Around 14.00 KPN reported that the outage that arose last night has been resolved. KPN says that the outage was caused by a malfunction in the cooling system of one of the network locations. As a result, part of the equipment could no longer be used, because it threatened to become too hot. How that outage could occur is being investigated. A spokesperson for KPN does not want to say at which location the outage was, for security reasons. Extent unclear According to the telecom company, a small group of business customers was affected. Because of the outage, the UMC Utrecht and Wilhelmina Children's Hospital reported on their site that an alternative phone number had been opened for urgent matters. The UMCG in Groningen also had an alternative number. Emergency number 112 was still normally reachable. In an explanation for patients, the Radboud UMC in Nijmegen wrote that callers might get a connection, but that they then would not hear the hospital employee.

title: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida, southern US braces for severe weather
lead: Hurricane Isaias has made landfall in the United States near the town of Destin in Florida. Shortly afterwards the hurricane weakened in strength, and so the weather services now speak of a severe storm. However, the risk of flooding in Florida is still considerable, according to governor Ron DeSantis. Because of the flooding risks and strong wind gusts, he warns people not to take to the road. In Destin streets have flooded, in the neighboring city of Pensacola trees have been blown over and power lines have been hit in the process. Videos circulating on social media also show how an entire roof of a hotel is being torn off by the wind. Footage from the small town of Crestview, not far from Destin: Storm Isaias has also caused damage in the south of neighboring state Alabama. Fallen trees block roads, and power lines have been damaged there too. In total, nearly 800,000 people in Florida and Alabama were without power on Saturday night. People who now still try to drive to family or friends are too late: because of the fallen trees it is almost impossible in many places to get from A to B. Although Isaias is no longer an official hurricane, the southern states of America will still experience disruption this weekend. The expectation is that 10 to 20 centimeters of rain will fall this weekend in Florida, Alabama and Georgia.

title: Prominenten verlaten NSC: 'Partij is volledig afgedwaald'
lead: Oud-Kamerleden Ilse Saris en Harm Holman hebben hun lidmaatschap van Nieuw Sociaal Contract opgezegd, nadat woensdag de laatste actieve NSC-politicus, Europarlementariër Dirk Gotink, uit de partij stapte . Directe aanleiding is de uitnodiging aan Mona Keijzer om vandaag op het partijcongres van NSC te spreken. Op het moment dat zij het woord nam verliet ongeveer de helft van de aanwezige NSC'ers de zaal. Het partijbestuur bevestigt dat deze week nog meer leden hun onvrede hebben geuit door hun lidmaatschap op te zeggen. In een intern bericht schrijft Saris: "In mijn ogen is de partij volledig afgedwaald van waar NSC voor stond." Holman zegt tegen Nieuwsuur : "NSC was een redelijke middenpartij op de inhoud, maar het is verworden tot een steeds rechtsere en populistische partij. En daar voel ik mij niet bij thuis." Inmiddels is Holman weer lid geworden van het CDA. De partij Nieuw Sociaal Contract werd drie jaar geleden opgericht door oud-CDA'er Pieter Omtzigt en behaalde datzelfde jaar vanuit het niets 20 Kamerzetels. Na een kabinetsdeelname en het vertrek van Omtzigt om gezondheidsredenen, behaalde de partij bij de daaropvolgende Tweede Kamerverkiezingen 0 zetels . Sindsdien is er sprake van een leegloop onder de leden, en vertrekt de ene na de andere partijprominent. Ruzie Ook Nicolien van Vroonhoven, voormalig fractievoorzitter, heeft haar lidmaatschap opgezegd. Dat deed ze na de zomer, vanwege een persoonlijk conflict met het partijbestuur. "Ik heb het bestuur een brief geschreven en ik wens ze veel succes. De liefde tussen mij en de partij is bekoeld. Veel meer wil ik daar niet over kwijt." Voormalig minister van <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> Judith Uitermark is ook al langer geen lid meer van NSC. "De beweging die ik zie in de partij, daar voel ik mij niet bij thuis." Voormalig staatssecretaris Tjebbe van Oostenbruggen zegt tegen Nieuwsuur : "NSC is voor mij een gesloten boek." Oud-Kamerlid Olger van Dijk hoort ook bij de opzeggers, en wenst de partij "het allerbeste". Amateuristisch Voormalig campagneleider en oud-Kamerlid Wytske Postma was er vanaf de oprichting bij, maar de partij van toen herkent ze nu niet meer terug. De partij is volgens haar in een interne strijd verwikkeld en is "een politiek amateuristische club geworden". Postma ziet de uitnodiging voor Mona Keijzer als een ruk naar rechts, waar lang niet iedereen achter staat. De partij is opgericht vanwege goed bestuur, en Keijzer heeft "een iets andere stijl". Volgens Postma was vandaag een opheffingscongres "verstandig geweest, hoe moeilijk dat ook is". Tijdens het congres vandaag verliet de helft van de aanwezigen de zaal op het moment dat Keijzer het woord nam: Partijvoorzitter Ronald de Bruin ziet dat toch anders. "We zitten in een moeilijke fase en we zijn een partij zonder leider. We hebben Mona Keijzer uitgenodigd als gastspreker om te zoeken naar de overeenkomsten." Volgens een woordvoerder van Keijzer wordt het een verhaal over haar nieuwe politieke beweging Project 2029. Van de oud-Kamerleden die nog wel lid zijn en die Nieuwsuur heeft gesproken, zijn de meesten niet aanwezig op het congres vandaag. In de evenementenzaal in Breda zaten deze zaterdag ongeveer honderd leden. Het partijbestuur overleefde een motie van wantrouwen uiteindelijk niet en trad af.

title: Curator zit met honderden kilo's medicinale wiet na failliet enige Nederlandse teler
lead: De enige legale kweker van medicinale cannabis in Nederland is failliet verklaard. Het betekent dat zo'n 7000 mensen met ziektes als MS en epilepsie vanaf volgend jaar waarschijnlijk geen medische wiet uit Nederland meer kunnen krijgen. Ondertussen zit het Groningse bedrijf Bedrocan met een overschot van honderden kilo's mediwiet die via de curator verkocht moeten worden. Het bedrijf van de Groningse ondernemersfamilie Erkelens kreeg in 2003 als eerste en enige in Nederland toestemming van de overheid voor de productie van medicinale wiet. Bij het bedrijf werken zo'n zeventig mensen. Hun banen staan op de tocht. "Dit heeft een enorme impact en het verdwijnen van Bedrocan is voor de familie Erkelens, het personeel en de regio erg zuur", zegt een woordvoerder tegen RTV Noord . De eigenaren willen zelf niet reageren op het faillissement. Contract opgezegd Het contract tussen de overheid en Bedrocan liep begin dit jaar af. Bovendien komt er mogelijk een wetswijziging van de Opiumwet aan. Die moet het mogelijk maken voor cannabisproducenten om rechtstreeks aan apotheken in binnen- en buitenland te verkopen. Bedrocan heeft nog geprobeerd het faillissement te voorkomen. De bank zou bereid zijn geweest om de grootste schuld aan de energieleverancier voor te schieten. Gehoopt werd dat het Bureau Medicinale Cannabis, dat nu verantwoordelijk voor de productie, handel en export van Nederlandse cannabis, geplaatste bestellingen vast vooruit wilde betalen. Maar het bedrijf kwam er niet uit met de schuldeisers en het BMC. De curator trok daarom afgelopen week de stekker uit het bedrijf. Een doorstart lijkt niet erg realistisch. Volgens de woordvoerder heeft de eigenaar van Bedrocan er "alles aan gedaan om te redden wat er te redden viel". Partij cannabis Bij het bedrijf liggen nog honderden kilo's mediwiet opgeslagen, ter waarde van miljoenen euro's. De curator zal de partij proberen te verkopen. Maar omdat de wiet onder de Opiumwet valt kan de curator dat niet zomaar aan de hoogste bieder doen. Verkoop kan alleen met medewerking van het BMC. Patiënten die medicinale wiet gebruiken tegen pijn en andere ongemakken moeten mogelijk overstappen naar wiet uit de coffeeshop of medische wiet uit het buitenland. Hugo Beukeveld (26) zei eerder tegen de regionale omroep dat dat "verschrikkelijk" zou zijn. Hij heeft cerebrale parese en cannabis helpt hem bij de pijn en spierspanningen. De Nederlandse mediwiet is gestandaardiseerd. Het is altijd afwachten welke uitwerking andere wiet heeft. "Dat is juist de kracht van de cannabis van Bedrocan, de consistentie", zegt Beukeveld.

title: Households will pay more for gas in the coming period, increase in fixed energy contracts
lead: "The heating does sometimes go on already, but we take into account that it is expensive. So in the evening a blanket over you or a thick sweater on, that is something you think about now." This customer, like other visitors to the hardware store, is busy with autumn, which has now really begun. In many households the heating is going on again. The chance is high that that turn of the thermostat will turn out more expensive than last year. Due to the war in the Middle East, gas prices have been rising sharply for months. Tom Schuitemaker of comparison site Pricewise also sees this. "The price of gas compared to a year ago is really 40 to 50 cents higher per cubic meter. If you are around an average of 1000 cubic meters, then for gas alone it is already 500 euros on an annual basis. Add another 250 for electricity, then it goes very fast." This is how quickly the gas price rose At the end of October 2025, the average gas price for households was 1.19 euros per cubic meter. Yesterday that price was 1.60 euros. That is an increase of almost 35 percent. On the sites of price comparers, an increase is visible in the number of people who want to fix their energy price, other providers such as Independer and Overstappen.nl also see. Striking is that for the first time contracts with a term of several years are somewhat cheaper than annual contracts. This is partly because the expectation is that the supply of liquid gas will increase in the coming years. There are three types of energy contracts. Variable, fixed and dynamic. With a fixed contract you fix the same energy price for a longer time. For variable contracts there is no end date, but the energy provider can adjust the price every few months. With a dynamic contract the price changes constantly, every day or even every hour. A fixed annual contract is normally advantageous because you get a discount from an energy company, for example in the form of a welcome bonus. But the 3-year contracts can now compete, says Schuitemaker. "We see that longer contracts are requested 10 times more often than a year ago." Gas price still high for the time being Autumn has only just begun and although temperatures are already dropping somewhat, it will get colder from November. Then the demand for gas also increases. For households that want and are able to steer their energy use, a dynamic energy contract is an option, says Gerben Hieminga, senior sector economist energy markets and energy policy at ING. For example, charging your electric car or doing the laundry during the day when the sun shines. For people who want to avoid risks, a fixed contract is an alternative. "If it becomes a cold winter, prices shoot up. If you want to avoid that risk, you should take a fixed contract." Economist Hieminga expects that prices will remain high for the time being. Schuitemaker of Pricewise also thinks so. Due to the unrest in the Middle East, there is still less supply for the time being and it does not appear that that situation will change within a short time.

title: Oil deal or not, Russia attacks residential buildings in Ukraine: 15 dead
lead: Russia may have made agreements with the US about the export of diesel , in Ukraine the attacks continue. In Russian air attacks in the Zaporizhzhia region, at least fifteen people were killed, including three children. According to the local authorities in the southeast of the country, residential buildings were bombed. Footage shows how great the devastation is; entire rooms have collapsed and walls have been blown away. It also shows how a shovel drives over the rubble to clear away a bucket of debris. Emergency services managed to get people out from under the rubble. At least sixteen people have been injured. People are still missing. The Zaporizhzhia region was already attacked earlier this week. Ukraine reported on Tuesday that five people died in attacks on one of the bridges in the capital of the region. Rescue workers also evacuated people after an apartment building was hit and caught fire. In August, Russia attacked the nuclear power plant in Zaporizhzhia several times with drones. The nuclear power plant is located a few dozen kilometers from the capital of the region. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), the radiation level remained normal after the attacks. Attacks can release harmful radioactive materials. That is why the head of the IAEA called on Russia and Ukraine to be restrained with attacks on nuclear power plants. He calls every attack on nuclear power plants unacceptable. Oil deal Yesterday, US President Trump announced that he is suspending sanctions against Russia, allowing the Russians to export diesel again. In 2022, a large part of the world actually stopped buying Russian oil, because of the war in Ukraine. The Ukrainian president reacts cynically to the oil deal, after attacks on Zaporizhzhia from last night: "Today Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of the sanctions on diesel exports. It did so by dropping five glide bombs on homes in Zaporizhzhia. Read the article about Trump's suspension of the sanctions here: With the easing of the sanctions, Trump hopes that diesel prices in his own country will go down. In November there are midterm elections in the US, in which fuel prices are an important theme. The global price of diesel oil rose sharply after the US and Israel started their war against Iran. Oil trade from the Middle East has largely come to a standstill, creating a shortage on the market. More than 4.5 years ago, Russia invaded Ukraine, on 24 February 2022. Russian President Putin did so, according to himself, to "demilitarize" Ukraine.

title: Nuisance from group of young people in Heerenveen: 'Tie gas cylinders to fireworks'
lead: The municipality of Heerenveen has been struggling for weeks with a large group of nuisance-causing young people. Among other things, they set off fireworks in the evening. "It is also no longer about ordinary fireworks. They tie bottles of turpentine and gas cylinders to them," says council member Nando Vries at Omrop <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Fryslân</entity> . The council member of Heerenveen Lokaal, the largest faction in the municipal council, says that the impact on some residents and entrepreneurs is great. "We had a resident on the line crying because they no longer dare to go out in the evening." Mayor <entity id="person:avine-fokkens-kelder">Avine Fokkens-Kelder</entity> says that much is being done behind the scenes to tackle the nuisance. "Municipality and <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> have been in consultation with each other for weeks and a flex team from the police has been used." A flex team consists of extra officers who are deployed in a problem-oriented way. " Since Friday we also have concrete names in view." Cat-and-mouse game It is not known exactly how many young people are involved. According to Fokkens-Kelder, it was a challenge to map out the nuisance-causers because of the "cat-and-mouse game" between the authorities and the young people. The young people are among other things summoned for a conversation with the mayor. "But other measures can also be taken, ranging from fines to an area ban," says the mayor. The mayor also appeals to parents. "I hope that people at home have the conversation about what young people do in the evening." The Drenthe city of <entity id="org:gemeente-hoogeveen">Hoogeveen</entity> has also been plagued for days by nuisance from young people. There too the municipality intervenes . For example, the police can carry out preventive searches in the evening, cameras hang in the center and a gathering ban applies.

title: Karbonkel, childhood trauma for millennials, on display in museum: 'Cult phenomenon'
lead: Nightmares and sleepless nights were what schoolchildren were left with in the mid-1990s: villain Karbonkel from the TV series Ik Mik Loreland. The puppet that was used for the Schooltv programme can now be seen restored at the Beeld & Geluid museum in Hilversum. "Teasing, holding back and obstructing" was the one-eyed troll's strategy in the series. The intention was to teach children in group 3 to read by having them, together with the girl Mik, find the letters that Karbonkel had stolen. The series was broadcast between 1994 and 2002. A deliberate choice had been made to make the series exciting: "Research shows that children then pay better attention", broadcaster NOT explained. Made less scary For some children, however, the teasing fright and his unsightly fish were too much. Children burst into tears in class, had to sit on the teacher's lap or even leave the classroom entirely when the programme was watched. "One of the biggest bogeymen of my generation", a traumatised schoolchild described him years later. "Children dived under the desks in fear", another states. Another columnist remembers how her mother had to stay with her in bed "because otherwise I feared that Karbonkel would sneak out from behind my Barbie house and get me". The NOT intervened quickly after the criticism. The music with which Karbonkel made his entrance was made less threatening, the fish disappeared and in the third season the puppet was replaced by a real person with somewhat less scary make-up. Schools could also request a visit from a Karbonkel puppet to show that it was all fake. A retrospective with puppeteer Siem van Leeuwen: Beeld & Geluid, where the puppet ended up in storage after the end of the series, knew of this generation's love-hate relationship with Karbonkel: visitors often had a pronounced reaction to the museum piece, sometimes they preferred to stay away from it. When earlier this year it turned out that the puppet was slowly decaying, it was decided to restore it. The foam of his body, which slowly decayed through exposure to light, was given a kind of sunscreen to protect him better. He was also kept in an airtight bag for a time, so that insects that had been feeding on him died. Insect eggs then disappeared into the restorer's vacuum cleaner. Since today, the spruced-up Karbonkel can be seen for a month in his own experience in Beeld & Geluid. He may look slightly different from how people remember him: when a human replaced Karbonkel, this puppet was converted into troll boss Bovenbonkel. For that, his skin was painted grey and he was given a little hat. Accompanied Beeld & Geluid now calls its newest resident a cult phenomenon as "one of the scariest television figures from our childhood". "For those who dare" it can become "an exciting reunion", according to the museum. Besides the puppet itself, video footage and photos can also be seen. To prevent Karbonkel from traumatising a new generation, Beeld & Geluid warns that the exhibition has been made "deliberately exciting", in a dark room with music, sound effects and flickering light. According to the museum, parents are best placed to judge for themselves whether a visit is suitable for their child, but "we advise allowing children to take part accompanied by an adult".

title: New proposal for billions less EU budget still not enough for cabinet
lead: Ireland, as the six-monthly EU president, has made the proposal to cut the EU budget for the coming years. Ireland proposes to take 140 billion off it. There is much discussion about the coming seven-year budget. The Netherlands and five other countries believe that the European Commission wants too large a budget. The European Commission had proposed a multiannual budget of 1.76 trillion euros (1760 billion). In a letter to EU president Ireland, the prime ministers of the Netherlands, Germany, Sweden, Denmark, Austria and Finland urged reducing the budget by hundreds of billions of euros. The countries, which like to call themselves the frugal six, believe that less money should go to farmers and poorer regions in the EU. Traditionally, they receive about two thirds of the budget. The countries instead advocate more investment in security, defence, economic competition, innovation and the fight against illegal migration. In the Irish proposal, 3 percent is cut from the budget proposed by the Commission for, among other things, agriculture, fisheries and poorer regions. Under the heading of security, competitiveness and prosperity, the Irish plan instead cuts 13 percent from the budget proposed by the Commission. That therefore goes against the wish of, among others, the Netherlands to actually allocate more money for it. Inflation The current budget, which runs through 2027, is 1.2 trillion euros. With the Irish proposal, the EU budget still rises by billions to 1.62 trillion. That is an increase of 30 percent, but 8 percent less than the proposal of the European Commission. That increase of 30 percent does not mean that the European Commission can also do much more with it, because due to inflation the money becomes worth less. The European coronavirus debts of 750 billion euros must also be repaid by 2050 at the latest. Due to risen interest rates, the repayment has become more expensive. The new Irish proposal is part of the negotiations that have been going on for months and will be discussed next week. On Thursday and Friday, the European leaders will meet for an EU summit. Netherlands against new proposal The cabinet has already indicated that the new proposal is also insufficient. <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> says in a written response: "The Netherlands cannot agree to this proposal either. The Netherlands wants to see a much larger reduction of the budget together with other countries. We are therefore returning the proposal by return." The German government is also not yet satisfied. Chancellor Merz says that "we are still far removed" from an agreement. Many other EU countries, including Spain and Italy, want to hold on to support for agriculture and poorer regions and want more money to go there. Ultimately, all 27 member states must agree to the budget.

title: Several leaders of Indian cockroach movement arrested at demonstration against Modi
lead: The Indian authorities arrested thousands of supporters of the cockroach movement even before their demonstration got underway. The large square where the protest against Prime Minister Modi was to take place was blocked by police vehicles with tear gas installations. The internet was also almost completely shut down, and 45 metro stations closed. Buses were pulled over to the side of the road to pick up demonstrators, and the leaders of the protest movement were arrested on a plane upon arrival in Delhi for the protests. See here how the three leaders were arrested on a full plane: "The pre-planned interception by the Delhi police is intended to paralyse the leaders of today's peaceful demonstrations before they even reach the protest site," the movement says. The Indian police say they banned the demonstration because the permit application was submitted too late. In effect, the protests are being suppressed because the cockroach movement speaks out against a revision of the electoral rolls. If the electoral rolls are actually amended, according to the activists, millions of Indians risk being unable to vote in future elections. On Thursday, the protests of the cockroach movement were also already put down by the authorities.

title: Wrong-way driver killed in accident on A2, road closed for hours
lead: In an accident on the A2 near Breukelen a wrong-way driver was killed early in the afternoon, reports the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Nothing has yet been made known about the identity of the wrong-way driver. According to witnesses the wrong-way driver initially drove on the motorway in the direction of Utrecht. At a certain point the motorist ended up on the other carriageway. At the height of the Breukelen exit he collided with two other cars. Debris lay spread over at least four lanes: The driver of one of those cars was injured. The driver of the other vehicle remained unharmed. Motorway closed The motorway in the direction of Amsterdam is closed for investigation. That is expected to last until 18:00. The police are investigating and are looking for witnesses and dashcam footage. Because of the accident there is a traffic jam of an hour and a half, writes RTV Utrecht . Traffic is being diverted from the Oudenrijn interchange via the A12, A27 and the A1.

title: Again five Palestinians killed in Gaza by Israeli attacks
lead: In Gaza at least five Palestinians have been killed by two different attacks by the Israeli army. Four people were killed near a shopping centre, the fifth victim was killed a few kilometres further on. That is what the health authorities in Gaza say, which are under the control of Hamas. The Israeli army says that it carried out the attacks to kill Hamas fighters. It is unknown whether that succeeded. Exactly a week ago Israel also killed five people in an apartment building in Gaza City. Among those killed were a mother and her daughter. The Israeli army said later that in the attack it had managed to kill the high-ranking Hamas leader Ali Ahmed Al-Amoudi. Gaza bombarded Between the attacks of last night and last week Israel bombarded the Gaza Strip several times. Last Sunday a Palestinian was killed when Israel attacked a civilian vehicle.
