Eleven people were injured in that. Israel said that it was trying to kill a Hamas fighter. On Tuesday Israel also attacked targets in Gaza. According to the health authorities in Gaza, two Palestinians were killed in that. The attacks took place near the Al Shifa hospital, which was destroyed by Israel more than two years ago . In these attacks too, according to Israel, Hamas militants were the target. 74,000 Palestinians dead Yesterday it was exactly a year ago that Israel and Hamas agreed a ceasefire. Israel has since killed more than 1467 Palestinians. In that time Palestinian militants killed four Israeli soldiers. This week Israelis commemorated the victims of the Hamas attack on 7 October 2023. In those attacks almost three years ago approximately 1200 Israelis were killed and 251 people were taken hostage. Since 7 October 2023 in total more than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza by Israel, among them many children. In that period 175,000 people were also wounded. Yellow line Israel has occupied more than half of Gaza. A ' yellow line ', consisting of yellow-painted concrete blocks, indicates where Palestinians may come and where not. Israel has moved the markings increasingly towards the coast. If Palestinians come near the border they risk being shot dead by the Israeli army.

title: Train traffic around Schiphol disrupted for hours by power outage
lead: A power outage caused problems for train traffic to and from Schiphol this afternoon. As a result, it was busy at the airport. Also fewer trains ran between Amsterdam-Zuid, Schiphol and Hoofddorp. Around 15.30 the outage was resolved. After that the timetable was restarted. It will still take a while before train traffic runs according to the normal timetable again, says a spokesperson for NS. Also switch failure According to rail manager ProRail, a power outage arose in a high-voltage cabinet at Amsterdam Riekerpolder, just before the branch to Amsterdam Lelylaan and Amsterdam-Zuid. "We replaced a defective part, which resolved the outage," said ProRail. What the cause of the defect was is still being investigated. There were more problems on the rails today. For instance, fewer trains run between Den Haag, Leiden and Rotterdam and between Rotterdam and Dordrecht due to a switch failure. Also no trains run between Rotterdam and Delft due to arson this morning at a rail bridge in Delfshaven. Possibly it concerns sabotage.

title: Jan G. stayed in Overasselt for another twelve hours after escaping, this is how he managed to get away
lead: After dozens of armed men had appeared at his gate and had shot dead his security guard, Jan G. was still in Overasselt for a large part of the day. He had fled to family elsewhere in the village. Broadcaster <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> spoke with several sources in Overasselt and, in collaboration with NOS, reconstructed the flight of Jan G. after the explosion of violence on 1 September at his home. Still suspecting nothing of what awaits him that night, the 28-year-old Jan G. enters the local supermarket in Overasselt on Monday evening 31 August. It will be the last time for the time being that he visits the supermarket. A few hours later, around four o'clock in the morning, G. is startled awake in his chalet on Ewijkseweg by the alarm of his security system. On the camera images a group of more than thirty men armed to the teeth appears. Three of them had earlier that evening tried to break into a house on Honingklaver in Overasselt. A brother-in-law of Jan G. lives here. Alarmed by the camera images, G. flees with his girlfriend and their two young children via a rear exit of the premises. His parents are still sleeping in a shed elsewhere on the 600 square metre yard. G. and his girlfriend probably walk along a path through a dried-up ditch to hide in the bushes at the edge of a meadow. G. had ordered security guard Berry 'urgently' Meanwhile, the armed men have arrived at his home on Ewijkseweg. One of them shoots security guard Berry, who is sitting in his car at that moment. Shortly before, Berry had, face to face with the group, called his employer in panic. The latter apped him that he should leave. But by then it is already too late. The security guard dies of his injuries. Jan G. had ordered security guard Berry two days earlier 'urgently' from a security company, after two suspicious persons had walked past his home. Shortly after Berry's death, two police officers who rushed to the scene are also shot at. They are seriously injured. While emergency services stream in en masse, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> opens a manhunt for the more than thirty suspects. G. and his family are meanwhile picked up by an acquaintance, who brings them to his house elsewhere in Overasselt, less than 1200 metres from Ewijkseweg 6. The police ring the bell at G.'s house and find his mother there. Once in the shed, where she and her husband live, the colleagues see G.'s father sitting. He says: "Go away, you weirdos. Who are you to tell me what to do? I am not going anywhere at all." The man and the woman are told to stay in the shed and keep the doors closed. At around five o'clock in the morning, G. contacts the boss of the shot security guard and tells him that Berry has died. In hiding in Overasselt While the chaos around Ewijkseweg continues, G. remains in hiding with his family in Overasselt. According to local residents, the fleeing suspects have no idea that they are running around in the vicinity of the home where their target is hiding. Only at the end of the afternoon does a taxi arrive here, after which G. gets in with his family and leaves. The municipality closes the home on Ewijkseweg for a year and imposes an area ban on G. During the course of the day, a video surfaces in which criminals demand compensation from him for a lost batch of 1283 kilos of cocaine. Visit to collect passports From that moment on, G. with his family, his parents, and two brothers-in-law with their families have disappeared from the village. Where they are is unclear. In the weeks after the attack, the municipality, under police escort, enters the closed-off premises on Ewijkseweg twice more. According to an insider, G.'s girlfriend may briefly return during one of those visits to collect essential items, such as identity documents. The house is said to have been completely turned upside down after several police investigations. The animals that stayed on the premises, including horses and large guard dogs, have been placed in boarding facilities. Arrest in Germany On 18 September, G. is arrested in Germany at the request of the Dutch authorities. He is suspected of involvement in the import of cocaine via the port of Dunkirk. According to the German police, he was travelling via motorway A44 from the direction of Sachsen-Anhalt to the Netherlands. Since then, G. has been staying in a German cell. Occasionally he still speaks with his lawyer, but meanwhile a trial in Den Bosch looms. There he will have to answer for his involvement in the cocaine case around Dunkirk, on top of all the other problems that haunt him. Interviews with those involved This story is based on a large number of conversations that the authors have had over the past five weeks with directly involved parties in the Overasselt case. All conversations were conducted on the basis of anonymity. We have tried to verify oral statements with other sources and official bodies.

title: 18,000 chickens dead in major fire in Zeeuws-Vlaanderen
lead: A very large fire raged this afternoon in a chicken shed in Biervliet in Zeeuws-Vlaanderen. The 18,000 chickens did not survive the fire, a spokesperson for the safety region confirms to Omroep Zeeland. The fire released a lot of thick, black smoke that was visible from a great distance. The Safety Region Zeeland (VRZ) warned local residents to keep windows and doors closed. Cause unknown According to the regional broadcaster, it concerns an organic laying poultry barn. The fire broke out around 15:00. Nothing is yet known about the cause. There were no people present in the shed. Three fire engines came to fight the fire. A crane is also being deployed to break open the shed. Around 16:30 the fire was declared under control. The fire brigade will be busy extinguishing for some time.

title: Another attack on educational institution in Poland, third in a week
lead: For the third time in a week there has been a violent incident at an educational institution in Poland. This afternoon a woman injured three people at an institution for higher education in the capital Warsaw. What the attack was carried out with is not yet known. The police speak of a "dangerous object". The three victims (17, 17 and 24 years old) are not in life-threatening danger. According to Polish media, one of the victims was taken to hospital with cuts. The suspect, a 21-year-old student of the institution, was overpowered by an employee. Other attacks On Wednesday there was a stabbing at a school for vocational education in Ostroleka, a town about 120 kilometers north of Warsaw. Five students, two teachers, two bystanders and the perpetrator were injured. A 19-year-old suspect was arrested shortly afterwards in the area. A day later, a 15-year-old killed a caretaker and injured two others in a knife attack at his former school in Leszczydol-Nowiny, slightly north of the capital. During the attack he wore a helmet with a camera. It is not known whether he was filming at the time of the attack. Those two incidents prompted the Polish authorities to check nearly 50,000 schools for weapons. Since then, more than seventy people have been detained. For example, a 14-year-old boy was detained because he had a knife with him. A 16-year-old boy was picked up because he had a butterfly knife in his bag. Other reasons for arrests were threats to peers or threats of attacks on schools. Unrest and measures In app groups on Thursday, a rumor circulated among parents that the two attacks were coordinated and that more attacks would follow on Friday. The Polish government says that so far no evidence has been found that the two attacks are related. Prime Minister Tusk said on Thursday that he feared copycat behavior and spoke of an exceptional situation. "For the first time we are dealing with an attacker who had the plan to film his attack with a camera helmet." The attacks are causing a lot of unrest. Yesterday security measures were taken at schools throughout the country, such as the presence of officers and extra bag checks. Dozens of educational institutions canceled classes. There are also reports that parents kept their children at home.

title: Unstable rock formation threatens Swiss village, but a Nepal scenario is not feared
lead: An unstable rock formation threatens to bury the idyllic Swiss mountain village of Kandersteg under millions of cubic meters of rock and ice. Due to global warming, the permafrost, which acts as the cement that holds the mountains together, is thawing. As a result, water can get between the rocks, causing parts to start sliding. Yet that nightmare scenario does not make the residents particularly nervous. It is worrying, but they are not concerned. From Kandersteg, the threatened mountain peak, the Spitze Stei, is clearly visible. The enormous mass of stone casts a shadow over the village with 1300 inhabitants and a multiple of that in tourists. One day that entire load will come down, that is certain. But how quickly and with how much rock and ice at once is still the question. "We live in the mountains and with nature. Something can always happen. But there is no mountain in Switzerland that is followed as closely as the Spitze Stei," says a resident. "We have all the information," says another. "If something happens, we know what to do." They still have the recent disaster in Nepal fresh in their minds and have certainly not forgotten how a glacier collapse last year destroyed the nearby town of Blatten . But the situation in Kandersteg should not be portrayed too dramatically, emphasizes hotel owner Casimir Platzer of the Spitze Stei interest group. Virtually everyone agrees: the authorities and local scientists have this well under control. That indeed seems to be the case. "At the moment it is small packages that come down," says geologist Cornelia Brönnimann of the canton of Bern. "But we expect that in the future they will be larger packages." She and her colleagues have been closely monitoring the process since 2018 and estimate the risk that the entire formation will come down over the village at once as very small. Nepal scenario "We will have to see how Kandersteg turns out. Science does not expect a worst-case scenario, but they have done the calculations," says the originally Nepalese natural disaster expert Chandani Bhandari of the University of Geneva. "If that scenario comes true, it really is an enormous disaster, even bigger than in Blatten." In Blatten, about 9 million cubic meters of stone and ice came down. In Kandersteg it would even be 15 to 20 million cubic meters, but compared to Blatten it is happening fairly slowly here. The population is continuously kept informed by the municipality, so that everyone knows what can happen and what they should do in the event of an evacuation. "That is the way to do it." The destruction in Blatten last year was immense: "The conditions in the mountains are changing very dramatically," emphasizes glaciologist Mylène Jacquemart of ETH Zürich. The effect of climate change, driven by human CO2 emissions, is very large in the mountains. "How we see the ice disappearing, the permafrost thawing; that does change the hazards that exist. The art now is to follow that well and keep track of how everything changes." Yet all the scientists interviewed call a Nepal scenario on an Alpine scale very unlikely in Kandersteg, precisely because of that good monitoring. Geologist Brönnimann: "The peak is so well guarded. We assume that we will see events early enough and that we will have at least two days to warn the population." A disaster in which thousands of people die therefore seems to be prevented in the Alps. There are blind spots, but with satellites and other measuring equipment the Swiss can keep an eye on enormous areas fairly well. 'Ideal conditions' Compared to her home country, Switzerland has ideal conditions, says the Nepalese natural disaster expert Bhandari. "Switzerland is much more developed than our country. There are virtually no financial or technical limitations." Nepal, land of thousands of mountain lakes and many more unstable rock formations, often does not have a clear picture of where the danger lurks. Bhandari: "And even if we know, there is building along, for example, rivers with flood risks. Even with the right knowledge, people can be very distrustful of the government that advises them not to do something." Kandersteg at least does not have that problem. Hotelier Casimir Platzer, who with his interest group critically follows the municipality in the Spitze Stei dossier, underlines his confidence in the measurements and the local approach. "The interim results presented to us at the end of June are very promising. They indicate that the risk situation in various places is more favorable than previously assumed."

title: 'Historic moment' in Haarlem: first female bishop in the Netherlands consecrated
lead: A first for the Old Catholic Church in the Netherlands this afternoon. In the Sint Bavokerk, on the Grote Markt in Haarlem, a woman has been consecrated as bishop for the first time in Dutch history. After the grand celebration, Erna Peijnenburg may call herself bishop of the Old Catholic Church in Haarlem. The Old Catholic Church is a small church denomination, with according to its own figures more than 5000 members. The church is very old, it arose in the Netherlands at the beginning of the 18th century as a split from the Roman Catholic Church. "It is a historic moment," says Peijnenburg. She considers it an enormous honour. "I am amazed and surprised that I have been chosen for this position by colleagues and believers from the diocese." She notices that it is a hopeful event for many people. "For women, but also for men," says the brand-new bishop. "I am receiving many enthusiastic reactions because this is possible. I think it is always beautiful when in a group where there were only men, a woman also comes along for once. That has an encouraging effect on the world." Nineteenth bishop At the end of August, the Electoral College of the diocese of Haarlem chose her as the new bishop. Previously, Peijnenburg was a pastor in Alkmaar and Enkhuizen. She succeeds Dick Schoon. He retired at the end of June. Peijnenburg is the nineteenth bishop of Haarlem. "Our church decided some time ago to also open the offices to women," she says. "Then women became deacons and priests. It might also have been coming that a woman would also be chosen as bishop." Tomorrow at 14:30, during the church service, Peijnenburg will take her place in her bishop's seat for the first time. Old Catholic Church vs. Roman Catholic Church Within the Roman Catholic Church, women cannot become bishop, but in the case of Peijnenburg it concerns the Old Catholic Church. That is a breakaway from the Roman Catholic Church. She explains that the Old Catholic Church is an independent church. "In terms of content, within the Catholic movement we are closely related to the Roman Catholic Church, but we have our own way of decision-making." The Old Catholic Church describes itself as "a small, self-aware and contemporary faith community that stands fully in the Catholic tradition and at the same time offers much room for a personal interpretation of the faith".

title: Explosions heard at Riyadh airport, airlines cancel flights
lead: Explosions have been heard at the international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh. Two regional officials say the airport was evacuated after a rocket hit a passenger terminal. According to witnesses, ambulances drove to the airport at speed. An official says all air traffic to and from King Khalid International Airport has been halted. It is still unclear whether there are any casualties. Security situation Data from Flightaware shows that in the past 24 hours at least 225 flights to King Khalid International Airport have been cancelled, after the earlier attacks on the airport this week. The airport calls on travellers to contact their airline in advance and check the status of their flight before coming to the airport. Several airlines have already taken measures. Kuwait Airways cancelled all flights to and from Riyadh today. The American embassy in Riyadh calls on American citizens to avoid King Khalid International Airport and the surrounding area. Yemen In attacks by Houthis two days ago three Saudi citizens were killed , including a pilot. That an international airport is the target of a series of attacks is exceptional. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has tightened its guidelines for Saudi airspace. It points to the ability of the Houthis to hit targets deeper in the kingdom including Riyadh, and to their "greater focus on aviation infrastructure". The rocket attacks and drone attacks, as well as the attempts to intercept them, "increase the risk that civilian aircraft are mistakenly hit", the agency says. Under fire Meanwhile, the fighting in Yemen between the Houthis and Yemeni government troops continues. Saudi Arabia provides air support to the government troops in an attempt to reverse the recent territorial gains of the Houthis along the Red Sea. Saudi Arabia has sought support from the US and other allies, now that its airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure are under fire. This concerns, among other things, the sharing of intelligence and the planning and identifying of targets. 'I am not happy' When American President Trump left the White House yesterday, he was asked about the attacks on Riyadh airport. "It is not good" and "I am not happy", he told reporters. There are as yet no signs of American military support in response to the attacks. The ministers of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> of Saudi Arabia and Oman spoke by telephone this week about the importance of "support for diplomatic solutions to reduce tensions in the region". Oman, which lies across the Strait of Hormuz opposite Iran, regularly acts as a mediator. But there is still no prospect of a solution to the escalation.

title: Christa Pike back in prison, but will still receive medical care
lead: A week and a half after the failed execution attempt in the American state of Tennessee, Christa Pike has been discharged from the hospital. She is back in prison, American media report . "She will continue to receive medical care in prison and we will continue to monitor her recovery", her lawyers say. "She is grateful to the aid workers and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances." On Thursday it was announced that Pike could walk a little again . Shortly after the failed execution attempt she was already conscious and responsive. The 50-year-old Pike was to be executed last week in Tennessee by injection, but that failed twice. She was convicted of a murder in 1996. According to the non-profit organization Death Penalty Information Center, she is the first person to survive her death sentence by injection. From death penalty to life imprisonment? What will happen now is not clear. This week her lawyers argued that Pike has suffered enough. They want the governor of Tennessee to commute her death sentence to life without the possibility of release. The investigation into what went wrong is still ongoing. After the failed execution, Tennessee decided not to carry out any more death sentences for the time being. A week ago the highest official of the prison system in the state resigned. This journalist was present at the failed execution: Livestream In the US there is also much ado about another execution . Minister Hegseth announced that the execution by firing squad of the American ex-military Nidal Hasan will be livestreamed. President Trump says that this has not yet been definitively decided. The announcement by Minister Hegseth last Thursday immediately led to much criticism. Former major Hasan shot thirteen colleagues dead in 2009 at a military base in Texas. If the execution is indeed broadcast live, it will be the first public execution in the US since 1936.

title: Municipalities want more money for resilience against disasters and threats
lead: Municipalities believe they receive too little money from the national government to make themselves resilient against all kinds of threats. This concerns, for example, cyber and hybrid threats or dangers arising from climate change, such as wildfires. <entity id="person:sharon-dijksma">Sharon Dijksma</entity>, chair of the Association of Netherlands Municipalities (<entity id="org:vereniging-van-nederlandse-gemeenten">VNG</entity>), says that municipalities need a multiple of what is budgeted in the Budget Memorandum for the resilience task. "I assume it will amount to hundreds of millions in total." "<entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> has made 35 million available for emergency support points and now in the Budget Memorandum an additional increasing series of 20 to 70 million for both digital resilience, social-societal resilience and continuity. But the gap between what municipalities need and what the cabinet makes available is therefore large", according to the VNG. <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> also wants more money. The port of Rotterdam is often mentioned as a possible target for threats from Russia . "Resilience goes further than emergency support points . We must also invest in society itself, in a strong social fabric that helps us during an emergency and in the recovery afterwards", says a spokesperson for the municipality. No evacuation facilities The VNG already has a good picture of how municipalities would like to deploy extra money. "You can think of neighbourhood emergency plans and training for residents. We will still talk with the Ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> about sheltering and evacuating, for which there are currently virtually no facilities." "Emergency generators, satellite phones and walkie-talkies are needed, and the emergency services need many more resources such as fire engines. The list is too long to list everything." VNG chair Dijksma, also <entity id="pos:burgemeester-utrecht">burgemeester van Utrecht</entity>, does have an idea of what should happen in her municipality. "We have many vulnerable residents who are not self-reliant, they do not always have the money to prepare. We also need money for communication resources that we currently lack." In Austerlitz, a village in the <entity id="org:gemeente-zeist">gemeente Zeist</entity>, people do not want to wait until municipalities have sufficient resources for safety exercises. Austerlitz is located in the middle of the forest and has few access roads. Because residents were afraid they would not be able to get away well in a major forest fire, volunteers set up a 'forest fire working group'. "I am part of the group of citizens that keeps an eye on everything when there is a wildfire danger", says Robert Schliessler. "We work together with the safety region and train for what happens when our village is threatened." Today Schliessler is also taking part in the first exercise together with the safety region. "We have a WhatsApp group in the village, there are six hundred people in it, they all hear about it there when the exercise starts. We have been asking the safety region for this exercise for three years and are super happy that it is finally here", he adds. "By now we work well together with the municipality and safety region." The intention is that the group of volunteers keeps a close eye on 112 reports and passes on to residents that evacuation is necessary. "We do that earlier than the emergency services. We have three locations where people can find each other and those are determined at the moment we know where the fire is." 'Cannot be financed' Dijksma is very pleased with the exercise in Austerlitz. "It is very important that people also prepare themselves, this kind of initiative is gold." The resilience of municipalities falls under the Ministry of Justice and Security and <entity id="person:david-van-weel">Minister Van Weel</entity> is also satisfied with the initiative. "I am glad that challenges are identified and this kind of thing is picked up and improved locally. The call from municipalities for more money is something Van Weel can follow. "In the Budget Memorandum we have designated resilience as an important theme, but our spending will not cover all wishes", he says. "It is an enormous task, so I will not say that we can do everything at once. We cannot finance that." According to the minister, municipalities can really get to work with the money they already receive, for example to work on the resilience of their critical processes. "Ultimately, resilience lies in the communities where people live, municipalities have a very large role in that."

title: No trains between Rotterdam and Delft until at least Sunday evening after arson
lead: Until at least 23.00 tomorrow evening, no trains will run between Rotterdam and Delft. The cause is the arson last night at a railway bridge in Delfhaven. ProRail does not rule out sabotage. According to the rail manager, it will take until at least Sunday evening before the damage is repaired. Trains may even not run on the route again until Monday morning. The railway between Rotterdam and Delft is one of the busiest routes in the Netherlands. It is also used by trains that cover long distances, for example between the Randstad and Zeeland or Limburg. For train travellers, this means a lot of disruption tomorrow as well. Eight-hour check According to ProRail, it is certain that the fire was deliberately set last night. The fire started last night in the technical room. The door to it had been ground open and inside lay smouldering cables. Investigation shows that 35 cables have been damaged. Fifteen of them have burned through completely and must be replaced and welded again. After all the cables have been replaced, several checks must be carried out to determine whether trains can run safely again. Those checks take about eight hours. Whether sabotage has actually been committed on the railway again still has to be investigated by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and fire brigade. No one has been arrested yet.

title: New York Times: 12 dead in attack on Riyadh airport
lead: At least 12 people were killed in the attacks on the international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh today. Fifty people were injured. Officials report this to The New York Times. This makes it the deadliest attack in a Gulf state since the start of the war between the US and Israel with Iran in February, the newspaper reports. Since the start of the large-scale operation Dawn of Yemen by the Yemeni army last Monday, the Houthis have significantly stepped up their attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia. On Thursday, the Iran-backed Houthi rebels also attacked Riyadh airport. Three Saudis were killed in that attack, including a pilot. Earlier this week, the Houthis also targeted airports in the Saudi towns of Jizan, Najran and Abha. The New York Times reports that the damage to King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh is being assessed and that air traffic has been halted.

lead: Archie gave his owners the fright of their lives this weekend. The Australian Shepherd cross managed to wriggle out of his harness and took off, after which he was hit. title: Municipality wants an end to permanent residency, court prevents eviction
lead: About fifty Romanian labour migrants may for the time being continue to live in the recreational homes they rent at a holiday park in Echten in Drenthe. The <entity id="org:gerechtshof-arnhem-leeuwarden">gerechtshof Arnhem-Leeuwarden</entity> rejected an eviction on Tuesday. lead: The Norwegian football association (NFF) has filed a series of complaints with two FIFA committees. The association announced this on Tuesday in an extensive statement. lead: NYON (ANP/RTR) - The national football team of Serbia must play the next home match without spectators. title: 600,000 in subsidy for caravan sites, almost nothing realised
lead: Years ago four municipalities in <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> received money from the national government to create extra places for caravan dwellers. lead: Some of the residents have few or no expectations about the representative role of council members. title: Another person has died in the Netherlands after infection with West Nile virus
lead: In the Netherlands, another person has died after an infection with the West Nile virus. This is the tenth person this year to die after an infection with the virus, the <entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu</entity> reported on Thursday.

title: Motorcycle racer Veijer makes comeback in free practice in Indonesia
lead: Moto2 rider Collin Veijer has made his return to the circuit after his collarbone fracture last month. The 21-year-old motorcycle racer from Staphorst took part in the first free practice at the Indonesian Grand Prix.

title: No one gets the Brussels deadlock over the budget moving
lead: The new EU budget, which will apply for seven years from 2028, has been publicly fought over for more than a year. On Saturday, rotating president Ireland made a proposal to get the negotiations moving.

title: Evenepoel takes European cycling title in Slovenia
lead: Remco Evenepoel won the European cycling title in Slovenia on Sunday. The Belgian beat the Italian Giulio Ciccone in an exciting sprint à deux. Another Italian, Christian Scaroni, finished third at just under a minute.

title: All those different rooms, and yet the same little nest
lead: For years, photographer Bieke Depoorter travelled around in Egypt, Russia and the United States and slept at people's homes. What stands out in particular is the similarity between the bedrooms; the more or less universal nature of the human sleeping place.

title: Botic van de Zandschulp beats world number 35 and reaches third round of Shanghai Masters tournament
lead: Botic van de Zandschulp is in the third round of the Shanghai Masters tournament. The best tennis player of the Netherlands defeated the American Alex Michelsen in the second round in two sets: 6-4 6-4.

title: Gordon no longer suffers from type 2 diabetes: can that happen by changing your lifestyle?

title: Bertram wants to combine public transport and other types of transport in the region
lead: Public transport and, among other things, pupil transport must be combined in regions where accessibility is declining. State Secretary <entity id="person:annet-bertram">Annet Bertram</entity> (Infrastructure, CDA) wants in that way to move from public transport to 'public mobility' that can be booked all day for everyone, she writes in a letter to the House.

title: An absurd project with a cubic kilometre of polar ice was able to capture elusive particles
lead: The Belgian Francis Halzen receives the Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on IceCube, a telescope on Antarctica to detect neutrinos. "No respectable, conservative physicist joined me"
